This disconnects the Business Chart Manager from the application, enabling independent user interaction. The user can now work with the Chart Manager and modify data, without affecting the data in the application.

returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

name: chm.domain.in

name: chm.draw
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This signals to the Business Chart Manager that it must start (re)drawing the chart. The optional argument enables you to specify the value of the first category for which the chart must be (re)drawn.
syntax: function long chm.draw ( [double cat_from_value])
returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

name: chm.first.data.out

This retrieves information from the Business Chart Manager about the first data point in the current chart. If the client application modifies the information and saves it to the source table or file, the new information is included the next time the chart is started. Use chm.next.data.out() to retrieve information about the next and subsequent data points.
syntax: function long chm.first.data.out (long option, ref double series_value, ref double category_value, ref long data_number, ref double data_value, ref long footnote_no)

name: chm.first.data2domain.out

name: chm.footnote.in

returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

name: chm.get.request
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This retrieves a request from the Business Chart Manager. After calling the function, the application waits for a signal from the Chart Manager that a request is ready. It can then check the return value of the function to determine the nature of the request. The application must react to the request appropriately.
syntax: function long chm.get.request (long chart_no, ref double category_from_value, ref double category_to_value)
returns: CHM_ABORT — Quit the Business Chart Manager. CHM_SOURCE_IN — Send data to the Chart Manager. This value is returned when the user chooses the IN command on the Chart Manager's File menu. CHM_SOURCE_OUT — Retrieve data from the Chart Manager. This value is returned when the user chooses the OUT command on the Chart Manager's File menu. CHM_TIMER — Execute actions after the interval set by chm.set.timer(). < value > — This is the ID of an application option defined in the Application Options session (ttchm1120s000). When this value is returned, the application must execute the specific actions related to the particular application option.

name: chm.new
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This creates a new chart. The chart is not saved until the user executes the Save command.
syntax: function long chm.new (string chart_name(16), ref string chart_type())
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error.

name: chm.next.data.out
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. You use chm.first.data.out() to retrieve information about the first data point in the current chart. You use chm.next.data.out() to retrieve information about the next data point in the same chart. To retrieve information about all subsequent data points, you can place this function in a loop that executes as long as the return value is CHM_OK. If the client application modifies the information and saves it to the source table or file, the new information is included the next time the chart is started.
syntax: function long chm.next.data.out (long option, ref double series_value, ref double category_value, ref long data_number, ref double data_value, ref long footnote_no)
returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

You use chm.first.data2domain.out() to retrieve the sequence number of the first graph series that is linked to the second data domain of the current chart. You use chm.next.data2domain.out() to retrieve the sequence number of the next graph series that is linked to the second data domain of the same chart. To retrieve information about all subsequent graph series that are linked to the second domain, you can place this function in a loop that executes as long as the return value is CHM_OK. If the client application modifies the information and saves it to the source table or file, the new information is included the next time the chart is started.
syntax: function long chm.next.data2domain.out (ref double series_value)
returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

name: chm.next.footnote.out
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use chm.first.footnote.out() to retrieve information information about the first footnote in the current chart. Use chm.next.footnote.out() to retrieve information about the next footnote in the current chart. To retrieve information about all subsequent footnotes in the chart, you can place this function in a loop that executes as long as the return value is CHM_OK. If the client application modifies the information and saves it to the source table or file, the new information is included the next time the chart is started.
syntax: function long chm.next.footnote.out (ref long footnote_no, ref string footnote_text())
returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

name: chm.set.timer
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This starts a timer. The Business Chart Manager sends a CHM_TIMER signal to the application every specified number of milliseconds. When the application retrieves the signal, it can perform appropriate actions (see chm.get.request()). You can turn off the timer by calling chm.set.timer() with a time of zero.
syntax: function long chm.set.timer (long time)
returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

name: chm.title.in
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This function defines a main title and a subtitle for the current chart.
syntax: function long chm.title.in (string main_title(80), string sub_title(80))
returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

name: chm.title.out
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This retrieves the main title and subtitle of the current chart. If the client application modifies the information and saves it to the source table or file, the new information is included the next time the chart is started.
syntax: function long chm.title.out (ref string main_title(), ref string sub_title())
returns: CHM_OK — Success. CHM_ERROR — Error.

name: choice.again
doc: This cancels execution of a standard command and transfers control to the 4GL engine. Statements programmed after this function will never be executed. You can call this function during execution of a standard command. You can also call the function in field sections, as these are called indirectly during execution of some commands.
syntax: function void choice.again ()
returns: void

name: choice.report
doc: This returns the name of a report from the session data in the data dictionary. The report is taken from the group defined in the predefined variable reportgrp (default = 1). If there is more than one report in the group, the user is presented with a menu from which to select the required report. The returned name consists of 15 characters, starting with an “r”. The language code is not included in the name. If you call brp.open() with the report name returned by this function, the report is opened with the user language. If you call brp.open.language() with the report name returned by this function, the report is opened with the specified language.
syntax: function long choice.report (ref string reportname(15))
returns: > 0 sequence number of report in the group -1 report not found, or no report selected by user

name: choose.time.zone.from.list
doc: This starts a session where the user can choose a time zone from a list. The function then calls set.timezone() with the time zone selected by the user.
syntax: function long choose.time.zone.from.list (ref string new.timezone)
returns: 0 — New time zone set. -1 — User aborted operation; time zone not set .

name: chr$
doc: This function returns a single-character string corresponding to the supplied TSS code point.
syntax: function string chr$ (long code_point)
returns: A string containing exactly one character, specifically the character determined by the specified code point. Code point range — Description of the return value [0 … 0xff] — In the context of the function chr$, all code point values in the considered range are regarded as valid. For these code point values the resulting string is a single-byte string; the supplied code point is encoded as a single byte; the byte limit of the result is 1, also for code point 0 (the code point of the NULL character, usually interpreted as the end of the string value and as such not part of the string value) and also for code point 0x9b (the lead-byte value for four-byte TSS sequences). [0x100 … 0x9affffff] — In the context of the function chr$, all code point values in the considered range are regarded as invalid. For these code point values, the behavior of this function is left unspecified and may change in the future. [0x9b000000 … 0x9bffffff] — For valid code point values in the considered range the resulting string is a multi-byte string; the supplied code point is encoded as a four-byte sequence; the byte limit of the result is 4. For other code point values, the behavior of this function is left unspecified and may change in the future. In the context of the function chr$, a code point value in the considered range is regarded as valid when the last three bytes of the resulting four-byte sequence are non-zero; notice that the first byte is 0x9b. [0x9c000000 … 0xffffffff] — In the context of the function chr$, all code point values in the considered range are regarded as invalid. For these code point values, the behavior of this function is left unspecified and may change in the future. Notice that for valid code point values the behavior of chr$ is very similar to that of mb.long.to.str$. For invalid code point values the behavior of chr$ is left unspecified and, above that, may be different from that of mb.long.to.str$.

name: cipher.decrypt.finalize
doc: Most cipher algorithms operate in block mode, which means the output is always a multiple of the block size. Because the input is not necessarily a multiple of that block size, this function returns the last (partial) block. It also frees up the resources that are used by the encryption and invalidates (closes) the handle
syntax: function long cipher.decrypt.finalize (long Handle, string data.out, long data.out.length)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error. The specifics of the error are logged by the Bshell. The problem can be caused by the underlying OpenSSL function, an invalid buffer length or an invalid handle.

name: cipher.decrypt.initialize
doc: Initializes the state of the Decrypt Algorithm and selects the appropriate decryption algorithm.
syntax: function long cipher.decrypt.initialize (long crypt.type, string key, string iv)
returns: A handle for this decrypt operation that must be used in subsequent calls to cipher.decrypt.update() and cipher.decrypt.finalize(). The returned Id can only be used in the original process where cipher.decrypt.initialize was called, and is useless in other processes in the same bshell. The allocated memory is freed explicitly by passing the Id to cipher.decrypt.finalize(). The allocated memory is freed implicitly when the process exits. Any number of Cipher Encrypt Algorithm ID's may be in use concurrently.

name: cipher.decrypt.update
doc: Feeds data to the decryption algorithm to be decrypted using the key (and optionally IV) given in cipher.decrypt.initialize().
syntax: function long cipher.decrypt.update (long handle, string data.out, long data.out.size, string data.in, long data.in.size)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error. The specifics of the error are logged by the Bshell. The problem can be caused by the underlying OpenSSL function, an invalid buffer length or an invalid handle.

name: cipher.encrypt.finalize
doc: Most cipher algorithms operate in block mode, which means the output is always a multiple of the block size. Because the input is not necessarily a multiple of that block size, this function returns the last (partial) block. It also frees up the resources that are used by the encryption and invalidates (closes) the handle.
syntax: function long cipher.encrypt.finalize (long handle, string data.out, long data.out.length)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error. The specifics of the error are logged by the Bshell. The problem can be caused by the underlying OpenSSL function, an invalid buffer length or an invalid handle.

name: cipher.encrypt.initialize
doc: Initializes the state of the Encryption Algorithm and selects the appropriate encryption algorithm.
syntax: function long cipher.encrypt.initialize (long crypt.type, const string key, const string iv)
returns: A handle for this encrypt operation that must be used in subsequent calls to cipher.encrypt.update() and cipher.encrypt.finalize(). The returned Id can only be used in the original process where cipher.encrypt.initialize was called, and is useless in other processes in the same bshell. The allocated memory is freed explicitly by passing the Id to cipher.encrypt.finalize(). The allocated memory is freed implicitly when the process exits. Any number of Cipher Encrypt Algorithm ID's may be in use concurrently.

name: cipher.encrypt.update
doc: Feeds data to the encryption algorithm to be encrypted using the key (and optionally the IV) given in cipher.encrypt.initialize().
syntax: function long cipher.encrypt.update (long handle, ref string data.out, ref long data.out.size, const string data.in, long data.in.size)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error. The specifics of the error are logged by the Bshell. The problem can be caused by the underlying OpenSSL function, an invalid buffer length or an invalid handle.

name: cl.screen
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This clears a specified area of the current window. The changes become visible on screen only after you call refresh()
syntax: function void cl.screen (long column, long row, long no_of_cols, long no_of_rows)
returns: void

name: clean.mess
doc: This removes a message that was displayed by using the mess() function with its mode argument set to 0.
syntax: function void clean.mess ()
returns: void

name: clear.query.extend.in.zoom
doc: This clears a query extension that was previously defined in the selection.filter section. The 4GL engine automatically clears the extension in the after.zoom section of the session. Use this function to force an earlier removal of the query extension. For example, to clear the query extension before defining an extension for another zoom session.
syntax: function void clear.query.extend.in.zoom ()
returns: void

name: client.add.download.file
doc: Add a file to the list of files to be downloaded to the client. The mime.type can be used to indicate the file type such that the browser has the option to start the client application which is associated with this mime.type. When the mime.type is not specified, the mime.type will be determined based on the file extension of the file specified in the optional target argument. When the optional target argument is also not specified, the mime.type will be determined based on the file extension of the file specified in the source argument Conversion of CRLF characters is only done for text files (file extension .txt or mime.type "text/plain"). All other file types are copied in binary mode. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function long client.add.download.file (long id, string source [, string mime.type] [, string target])
returns: 0 — success < 0 — when an error occurred (for instance invalid source path) -2 — The source file could not be opened.

name: client.delete.upload.file.object
doc: Delete the result object returned by client.upload.files. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function void client.delete.upload.file.object (long id)
returns: void

name: client.download.file
doc: Download the server file passed in the source argument to the client. Calling this function will result in a download dialog in which the user can choose to select the file for download. This function will return when the user closes the download dialog. The mime.type can be used to indicate the file type such that the browser has the option to start the client application which is associated with this mime.type. When the mime.type is not specified, the mime.type will be determined based on the file extension of the file specified in the optional target argument. When the optional target argument is also not specified, the mime.type will be determined based on the file extension of the file specified in the source argument. Conversion of CRLF characters is only done for text files (file extension .txt or mime.type "text/plain"). All other file types are copied in binary mode. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function long client.download.file (const string source [, string mime.type] [, string target])
returns: 0 — success <> 0 — when an error occurred (for instance invalid source path) -2 — The source file could not be opened.

name: client.get.media.type
doc: Returns the MIME media type based on the extension of the filename.
syntax: function string client.get.media.type (const string source)
returns: string representing the MIME Media type of the file. The official list can be found here: http://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/index.html.

name: client.get.upload.file
doc: Get the details about a file which is uploaded with function client.upload.files. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function string client.get.upload.file (long id, long index [, ref string client.filename] [, ref string mime.type])
returns: The server path name of the uploaded file or empty when an error occurred

name: client.get.upload.filecount
doc: Get the number of files which are uploaded with function client.upload.files. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function long client.get.upload.filecount (long id)
returns: > 0 — the number of files uploaded < 0 — when id is not a valid object returned by client.upload.files

name: client.prepare.download
doc: Prepare the download of one or more server files. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function long client.prepare.download ()
returns: <> 0 — the id of the download structure which can be used by subsequent calls. This id can be passed to client.add.download.file function to add a file to the download or to the client.start.download function to start the download. 0 — when an error occurred (for instance when using this function in WebUI or LN UI)

name: client.show.file
doc: Show the server file passed in the source argument in the browser. The browser can show some file types natively in a browser window (like for example plain text and pdf files). For other file types, the browser will show a browser specific download dialog. This function will return immediately (so will not wait until the browser window is closed or the file downloaded by the client). The optional parameter "remove.after.download" can be used to control automatic removal of the server file after the file has been downloaded by the client. Conversion of CRLF characters is only done for text files (file extension .txt or mime.type "text/plain"). All other file types are copied in binary mode. The mime.type can be used to indicate the file type such that the browser has the option to start the client application which is associated with this mime.type. When the mime.type is not specified, the mime.type will be determined based on the file extension of the file specified in the optional target argument. When the optional target argument is also not specified, the mime.type will be determined based on the file extension of the file specified in the source argument. When this function is called more than once for a single UI event, only the last function call will be effective. In case of a Document Viewer session this function may only be called after calling vwr.init() or from callback function vwr.bms.received(). In case of a Document Viewer session the following arguments are ignored: new.window, title. This function is only supported in WebUI and LN UI.
syntax: function long client.show.file (string source, boolean new.window, string title [, string mime.type] [, string target] [, boolean remove.after.download])
returns: 0 — success < 0 — when an error occurred (for instance invalid source path)

name: client.show.url
doc: This function opens a URL in an external browser window. The behavior is the same as function open.url.local() with the mode parameter set to OPEN_URL_EXTERNAL. This function is only supported in the WebUI and LN UI.
syntax: function long client.show.url (string url)
returns: 0 — success < 0 — when an error occurred (for instance invalid source path)

name: client.start.download
doc: Start a download dialog showing a list of files constructed in advance with the functions client.prepare.download and client.add.download.file This function will return when the user closes the download dialog. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function long client.start.download (long id)
returns: 0 — success < 0 — when an error occurred (for instance invalid id)

name: client.upload.file
doc: Upload a single file from the client and save this file on the server in the file location passed as the destination argument. Conversion of CRLF characters is only done for text files (file extension .txt or mime.type "text/plain"). All other file types are copied in binary mode. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function long client.upload.file (string destination [, ref string client.filename] [, ref string mime.type])
returns: 0 — success < 0 — when an error occurred (for instance destination is a directory)

name: client.upload.files
doc: Upload one or more files from the client and save these files in a server directory. Conversion of CRLF characters is only done for text files (file extension .txt or mime.type "text/plain"). All other file types are copied in binary mode. This function returns an id that can be used in the function client.get.upload.file to obtain information of an uploaded file. This function is only supported for LN UI.
syntax: function long client.upload.files (string destination)
returns: <> 0 — the id of the result object to be used by subsequent functions. This result object must be deleted using the function: client.delete.upload.file.object 0 — when an error occurred (for instance destination is a directory)

name: client2server
doc: Deprecated. This copies a specified file from the client to the server.
syntax: function long client2server (string source, string dest, boolean text.mode [, boolean rm.file] [, boolean progress.window])
returns: 0 — File copy success. 1 — Error. File copy canceled by the user. < 0 — Error. Source file not copied to the destination file.

name: close.message
doc: This removes the specified mailbox. All messages in the mailbox are also automatically removed.
syntax: function void close.message (long key [, long fast])
returns: void

name: cmf.addAddressEntry
doc: Creates an address child node in the address list aid. The attributes of the node are provided by the parameters of the function. Note: If an argument is left empty and the attribute is currently present in the message object, it will be removed completely.
syntax: function long cmf.addaddressentry (long aid, string role, string name, string address, string addresstype [, domain ttcmf.catg key] [, domain ttcmf.catg category])
returns: <> 0 — Object id of addresslist entry. 0 — Error creating entry (most likely invalid address list id).

name: cmf.addObjectToMessage
doc: The object identified by oid is added to the message object identified by mid. The class of this message is set to the string class (mandatory attribute for a message: for example CMF.TASK for tasks, CMF.APPOINTMENT for appointments and so on). The object is written to a temporary file with extension .xml, which is placed in the current working directory. This file is added as an attachment to the message object. The body attribute of this attachment is set to true, the mimetype is set to application/xml and the delete attribute is set to true. All attachments currently attached to the task are also attached to the message object. Finally the object identified by oid is deleted (because changes in this object are not reflected anymore in the message object). Note: If an error is returned, the object identified by oid is not deleted
syntax: function long cmf.addobjecttomessage (long oid, long mid, string class(100))
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — General error (check logfiles) . -2 — Oid or mid are not valid xml object id's. -3 — Class argument empty. -4 — Object could not be written to file.

name: cmf.copyAttachment
doc: Copies the attachment identified by attachment.id from the object identified by id1 to the object identified by id2. All attributes and their values are also copied
syntax: function long cmf.copyattachment (long attachment.id, long oid)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid attachment identification.

name: cmf.create
doc: Creates a new Infor LN eMessage Connector message object.
syntax: function long cmf.create ()
returns: <> 0 — (Bshell wide) unique Infor LN eMessage Connector message object id. 0 — Message object creation error.

name: cmf.createAddressList
doc: Creates an address list object.
syntax: function long cmf.createaddresslist ()
returns: <> 0 — Id of root-element of address list. 0 — Error creating object

name: cmf.createAppointment
doc: Creates a new Infor LN eMessage Connector appointment object.
syntax: function long cmf.createappointment ( [long mid])
returns: <> 0 — (Bshell wide) unique Infor LN eMessage Connector appointment object id. 0 — Appointment object creation error.

name: cmf.createAttachment
doc: Creates an attachment entry in the message identified by mid and returns the identification of the attachment.
syntax: function long cmf.createattachment (long mid)
returns: <> 0 — Attachment Identification. 0 — Attachment could not be created (most likely invalid cmf object).

name: cmf.createRecipient
doc: Creates a recipient entry of type role in the message identified by mid and returns the identification of the recipient object.
syntax: function long cmf.createrecipient (long mid, enum role)
returns: <> 0 — Recipient Id. 0 — Invalid object id.

name: cmf.createTask
doc: Creates a new Infor LN eMessage Connector task object.
syntax: function long cmf.createtask ()
returns: <> 0 — (Bshell wide) unique Infor LN eMessage Connector task object id. 0 — Task object creation error.

name: cmf.destroy
doc: Destroys the Infor LN eMessage Connector (message) object identified by id. This function can also be used to destroy recipient objects, attachment objects, etc.
syntax: function long cmf.destroy (long mid)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id).

name: cmf.enableService
doc: Checks in the Services (ttcmf030) table if service is enabled (ttcmf030.enab = yes) or not. If not, and enable is true, then service is enabled. If yes, and enable is false, then service is disabled. In the other (two) cases nothing happens.
syntax: function long cmf.enableservice (domain ttcmf.prov service, long enable)
returns: 2 — service is enabled. 1 — service is disabled. 0 — nothing changed. -1 — service not found in table Services (ttcmf030).

name: cmf.getAddressBookKey
doc: Gets the two key fields of the Address Book (ttcmf200) of the recipient identified by entry.id and returns them in the strings key and category.
syntax: function long cmf.getaddressbookkey (long entry.id, ref string key, ref string category)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error retrieving category and key: probably invalid recipient id.

name: cmf.getAddressDetails
doc: Retrieves the details of an address entry specified by entry_id. Entry_id is obtained from the function cmf.getNextAddress() or cmf.addAddressEntry(). The attribute values for the object identified by entry_id are copied to the appropriate parameter variables.
syntax: function long cmf.getaddressdetails (long entry_id, ref string category, ref string key, ref string role, ref string name, ref string address, ref string addresstype, ref long errorcode)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error retrieving details (most probably invalid address entry id).

name: cmf.getAppointmentAlarm
doc: Gets the alarm of the appointment identified by apid and returns it in the utc date alarm.
syntax: function long cmf.getappointmentalarm (long apid, ref domain ttutc alarm)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present. -2 — Date conversion error.

name: cmf.getAppointmentAlldayevent
doc: Gets the alldayevent flag of the appointment identified by apid and returns it in the string alldayevent.
syntax: function long cmf.getappointmentalldayevent (long apid, ref enum alldayevent)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present.

name: cmf.getAppointmentBusystatus
doc: Gets the busystatus of the appointment identified by apid and return string into busystatus.
syntax: function long cmf.getappointmentbusystatus (long apid, ref string busystatus)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id or element not present).

name: cmf.getAppointmentDescription
doc: Get the value of the description text of the appointment identified by apid and returns it in description.
syntax: function long cmf.getAppointmentDescription (long apid, ref string description)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present.

name: cmf.getAppointmentEndtime
doc: Gets the endtime of the appointment identified by apid and returns it in the utc date endtime.
syntax: function long cmf.getappointmentendtime (long apid, ref domain ttutc endtime)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present. -2 — Date conversion error.

name: cmf.getAppointmentLocation
doc: Gets the appointment location of the appointment identified by apid and return string into location.
syntax: function long cmf.getappointmentlocation (long apid, ref string location)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id or element not present).

name: cmf.getAppointmentMeeting
doc: Gets the meeting flag of the appointment identified by apid and returns it in the string meeting.
syntax: function long cmf.getAppointmentMeeting (long apid, ref enum meeting)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present.

name: cmf.getAppointmentMethod
doc: Get the value of the METHOD attribute of the appointment identified by apid and returns it in method.
syntax: function long cmf.getAppointmentMethod (long apid, ref domain ttcmf.mth method)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present.

name: cmf.getAppointmentStarttime
doc: Gets the starttime of the appointment identified by apid and returns it in the utc date starttime.
syntax: function long cmf.getappointmentstarttime (long apid, ref domain ttutc starttime)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present. -2 — Date conversion error.

name: cmf.getAppointmentSubject
doc: Gets the appointment subject of the appointment identified by apid and returns string into subject.
syntax: function long cmf.getappointmentsubject (long apid, ref string subject)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id or element not present).

name: cmf.getAppointmentUUID
doc: Get the value of the UUID attribute of the appointment identified by apid and returns it in uuid.
syntax: function long cmf.getAppointmentUUID (long apid, ref string uuid)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present.

name: cmf.getAttachmentBody
doc: Gets the type of the attachment identified by attachment and returns it in the enum body.
syntax: function long cmf.getattachmentbody (long attachment, enum ttyeno body)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid attachment identification.

name: cmf.getAttachmentFilename
doc: Gets the filename and display name of the attachment identified by attachment and returns them in the strings filename and displayname.
syntax: function long cmf.getattachmentfilename (long attachment, string filename, ref string displayname)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid attachment identification.

name: cmf.getAttachmentMime
doc: Gets the mime type of the attachment identified by attachment and returns it in the string mime.
syntax: function long cmf.getattachmentmime (long attachment, ref string mime)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid attachment identification.

name: cmf.getAttachmentPosition
doc: Gets the position of the attachment identified by attachment and returns it in the string position.
syntax: function long cmf.getattachmentposition (long attachment, string position(10))
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid attachment identification.

name: cmf.getCategories
doc: Gets the categories of the message identified by mid and returns string into categories.
syntax: function long cmf.getcategories (long mid, ref string categories)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id or element not present).

name: cmf.getChargeCode
doc: Gets the message charge code of the message identified by mid and returns string into chargecode.
syntax: function long cmf.getchargecode (long mid, ref string chargecode)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id or element not present).

name: cmf.getClass
doc: Gets the message class of the message identified by mid and returns string into class.
syntax: function long cmf.getclass (long mid, ref string class)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id or element not present).

name: cmf.getCreateTime
doc: Gets the message creation time of the message identified by mid and returns it into utc date createtime.
syntax: function long cmf.getcreatetime (long mid, ref domain ttutc createtime)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id or element not present). -2 — Date conversion error.

name: cmf.getDisplay
doc: Gets the display option of this message identified by mid and put it in the variable display.
syntax: function long cmf.getdisplay (long mid, ref enum display)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object.

name: cmf.getDueDate
doc: Gets the duedate of the message identified by mid and returns it in the utc date duedate.
syntax: function long cmf.getduedate (long mid, ref domain ttutc duedate)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present.

name: cmf.getExpiry
doc: Gets the expiry time of the message identified by mid and returns it in the utc date expiry.
syntax: function long cmf.getexpiry (long mid, ref domain ttutc expiry)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid cmf object or element not present.

name: cmf.getFollowupFlag
doc: Get the value of the followup flag from the message identified by mid.
syntax: function long cmf.getfollowupflag (long mid)
returns: true — Followup flag was set. false — Followup flag was not set or set to FALSE

name: cmf.getId
doc: Creates a path to the header.xml file, which consists of the message storage path in the Services (ttcmf030) table and inbox or outbox (depending on message direction) and header.xml. This file is opened in read mode and then parsed with function xml.read which returns the bshell-wide unique object ID of the message object, which is often needed to call other functions in this library.
syntax: function long cmf.getid (string messageld, string service, domain ttcmf.mdir message.direction, ref string error_string())
returns: <> 0 — mid = Bshell-wide unique message ID. 0 — mid = no valid object id error_string contains detailed error information.

name: cmf.getMessageId
doc: Gets the message id of the message identified by mid and return string into messageId.
syntax: function long cmf.getmessageid (long mid, ref string messageId)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error (most likely invalid object id or element not present).

name: cmf.getNextAddress
doc: Retrieves the next address child element in the address list root element identified by aid. If previous is 0 (zero) the id of the first entry on the addresslist is returned with type element. Else, the entry following the entry identified by previous is returned.
syntax: function long cmf.getnextaddress (long aid, long previous)
returns: <> 0 — Id of address list child element. 0 — End of child elements reached or invalid address list id supplied.

name: cmf.getNextAttachment
doc: Gets an attachment entry in the message identified by mid and returns the identification of the attachment. If previous is 0 (no valid object id), then the first attachment is returned. If previous is a valid object id (not 0) then the attachment id of the attachment that follows the attachment identified by previous is returned. name: cmf.sendToPerson
doc: Takes the message object and sends it to the recipients in the addresslist object that is identified by aid. Recipients are separated into groups by address type (fax, SMTP, telex, SITA, and so on). For each group a separate message object is built with the recipients in that group attached to it. The Infor LN eMessage Connector service for that address type is started and the message sent to it. If no sender information is available, it will automatically be added. This holds also for the notify recipient (who, for example, gets the delivery reports). Also it's checked that the addresslist object contains only one sender (from-recipient). Any errors encountered are stored for each recipient in the addresslist object. Infor LN eMessage Connector services opened by this function are not stopped. This is for efficiency purposes. It is expensive to start and stop services. This allows applications to make multiple calls to cmf.sendToPerson without incurring the overhead of service startup and shutdown. Instead another function will be provided to stop all services opened by this function (cmf.stopAllServices).
syntax: function long cmf.sendtoperson (long mid, long aid, long display, long show.progress, ref string message_string(), long convert, string filename1 ...)

name: cmp.mem
doc: This compares the values of two variables or arrays. By default, the values are compared for the length of the shortest argument. If you specify the optional count argument, the function compares the first count numbers or characters of both arguments. The number of numbers or characters compared will, however, never exceed the length of the shortest argument. Note that when the shorter array equals the first part of the longer array, they will be considered equal. A special situation occurs when two arrays of strings are compared. In this situation by default only the first string in the arrays is compared. To compare the complete arrays (limited by the length of the shortest array) specify the count argument, with a value exceeding the length of the larger array.
syntax: function long cmp.mem (void var1, void var2 [, long count])
returns: The return values depend on the types of the variables. Variables are of different types: 1 Variables are longs or doubles: 0: values are equal 1: values are different Variables are strings or arrays of type long, double, or string: < 0: first argument is less than second = 0: arguments are equal > 0: first argument is greater than second

name: concat$
doc: The function concat$ converts one or more values to strings and concatenates them, separated by a separator, to a single string. You can use string.scan() to split the string again into its individual parts. This function is used mainly by the report processor to save unsorted records in a sequential file for subsequent sorting.
syntax: function string concat$ (string separator, void value ...)
returns: The return value is the concatenation of the supplied values (implicitly converted to string values), separated by the specified separator character. As of bshell TIV level 2340, the resulting string is of type multi-byte string if and only if the supplied separator string or any of the supplied values is of type multi-byte string. In all other cases (i.e. when the supplied separator string and all supplied string values are of type single-byte string or when the bshell TIV level is less than 2340) the resulting string is of type single-byte string.

name: copy.mem
doc: This copies the memory space from the source argument to the destination argument. By default, the total length of source is copied. But, if the destination argument is shorter than the source argument, then source is truncated. Use the optional count argument to copy a specified number of array elements only. You can use this function to copy single variables or entire arrays. You cannot copy variables of different types. It you attempt to do this, the destination argument remains unchanged.

name: cos
doc: This computes the cosine of x, in radians. The x argument can be a long or a double.
syntax: function double cos (double x)
returns: The cosine of x.

name: cosh
doc: This computes the hyperbolic cosine of x.
syntax: function double cosh (double x)
returns: The hyperbolic cosine of x.

name: count.records.in.view
doc: Counts the number of records that exist in the maintable for the current view. Any filter or query extension that has been set is taken into account. This function can be used in combination with the display.total.fields() function.
syntax: function long count.records.in.view ()
returns: The number of records that are exists in the maintable for the current view.

name: cp$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to position the cursor at the specified column and row. The cursor position is always relative to the upper left corner of the current window.
syntax: function string cp$ (long column, long row)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: cps.add.child
doc: Add a child session to this controller, which will be shown and started in the frame of the composite controller. This session will be shown in the passed split pane. To a split pane exactly two objects must be added: sessions and/or split panes. The order of adding these objects to the split pane determines the order on the screen (left/right or top/bottom).
syntax: function long cps.add.child (const string session.code, long bars, const string title, long splitpane)
returns: 0 — on success -1 — on failure

name: cps.add.tree.detail.session
doc: Add a Tree-Detail session to detail area. Standard the detail session of cps.set.tree.detail is shown. The added tree detail can be activated with the function gbf.synchronize.detail(). Maximum of 4 Sessions can be added.
syntax: function long cps.add.tree.detail.session (const string detail.session.code)
returns: 0 — on success -1 — on failure

name: cps.create.splitpane
doc: Create a split pane which can either hold another split pane or a child session. There can only be one top-level split pane created. This function may not be called before the call to cps.init()
syntax: function long cps.create.splitpane (long orientation, long divider [, long splitpane])
returns: <> 0 — The id of the created splitpane 0 — When this funcion fails

name: cps.init
doc: Initialize the Composite Session Controller. This must be the first cps function called by the 3GL-Script. When this session was started from a parent session in modeless mode, this function will reactive the parent session. So any imports which must be done by this session from the parent should be done before this function is called.
syntax: function long cps.init ( [long cps.type])
returns: 0 — on success -1 — on failure

name: cps.set.tree.detail
doc: Sets the GBF session and Details sesion of a Tree-Detail session. The GBF session and Details session will be shown and started in the frame of the composite controller.
syntax: function long cps.set.tree.detail (const string tree.session.code, const string detail.session.code [, long divider] [, const string tree.title])
returns: 0 — on success -1 — on failure

name: cps.start
doc: Activates the Composite Session Controller and the related child sessions. This function will only return when the user decides to close this composite session.
syntax: function void cps.start ()
returns: void

name: cps.status.mess
doc: This function displays the specified message in the status bar of a composite session. To clear this message, an empty message string must be passed. This function can be called from composite child sessions (GBF or 4GL). When this function is called from other session types, it will do nothing.
syntax: function void cps.status.mess (const string message)
returns: void

name: cr$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to send a carriage return (without a line feed) to the screen or printer. The cursor is positioned at column 1 of the current line.
syntax: function string cr$ ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: creat.tmp.file$
doc: This creates a temporary file. The optional pathname argument may be used to specify the full path to the directory where the file is to be placed. When pathname is omitted or left empty, the file is created in the current directory. In UNIX environments, a unique temporary file is created with UNIX-privilege mode 0664.
syntax: function string creat.tmp.file$ ( [string pathname])
returns: The name of the temporary file.

name: create.extra.toolbar
doc: Worktop: This adds a secondary toolbar to a session. LN-UI: This adds the default icons to the commands. No secondary toolbar will be created.
syntax: function long create.extra.toolbar (string form_command, string gif_file [, string form_command] [, string gif_file])
returns: > 0 success 0 toolbar not allowed in this type of session -1 incorrect number of arguments

name: create.keyfields.collection
doc: Create an object which can hold a collection of key fields objects
syntax: function long create.keyfields.collection ()
returns: <> 0 — The id of the created collection. This id must be used in subsequent calls to other key fields collection related calls. 0 — When this function fails

name: create.keyfields.object
doc: Create an object which can hold the key fields and the corresponding values referring to one record of the passed database table. The key fields of index 1 are used.
syntax: function long create.keyfields.object (const string tablename [, long collection])
returns: <> 0 — The id of the created key fields object 0 — When this function fails

name: create.local.directory
doc: Deprecated. This creates a specified directory on a client system. You must have write permission in the parent directory to do this. Access permissions for the new directory are set to read and write for all users.
syntax: function long create.local.directory (string dirent)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error. Probably no permission.

name: create.local.file
doc: Deprecated. This creates a specified file on a client system. You must have write permission in the parent directory to do this. Access permissions for the new file are set to read and write, for all users. When the file does already exist, it will be truncated.
syntax: function long create.local.file (string filename)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error. Probably no permission.

name: create.node
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This adds a new node to a specified tree. The node_id, together with the parent_id, determine where the new node is located in the tree.
syntax: function void create.node (string tree_name, string parent_id, string node_id, string node_desc, long node_class [, long process_id])
returns: void

name: create.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This creates a new object of the specified type.
syntax: function long create.object (long type, long parent_object [, long attribute, value [, size]], ...)
returns: The ID for the new object, or 0 if an error occurs. You can subsequently use the returned ID as the object_id, parent_object, or object argument in other functions.

name: create.progress.indicator
doc: This creates a progress indicator with the specified title displayed in its title bar. The progress indicator is activated after the first update (using change.progress.indicator()). It is removed again using destroy.progress.indicator(), or automatically if PROGRESS.NOAUTODESTROY is not specified. Only one progress indicator can be active at the same time. If this function is not successful, then it is not allowed to change or destroy the progress indicator.
syntax: function long create.progress.indicator (string title [, long mode])
returns: 0 — Success -1 — Error

name: create.sub.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This creates a new subobject of the specified type. The subobject is drawn on the parent window. If the parent object is destroyed, its subobjects are also destroyed.
syntax: function long create.sub.object (long object, long type [, long attribute, value [, size]], ...)
returns: The ID for the new subobject or 0 if an error occurs. You can subsequently use the returned ID as the sub_object_id argument in other functions.

name: create.sub.object.by.id
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This creates a new subobject with a specified ID. The subobject is drawn on the parent window. If the parent object is destroyed, its subobjects are also destroyed.
syntax: function long create.sub.object.by.id (long object, long sub_object_id, long type, long attribute, void value [, long size])
returns: The ID for the new subobject (as specified by the sub_object_id argument) or 0 if an error occurs. You can subsequently use the returned ID as the sub_object_id argument in other functions.

name: create.tree
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This starts the Structure Chart Manager for a specified tree. It returns the process ID of the tree. If there is more than one tree with the same name, you can specify the process ID in the other functions in order to identify a particular tree. The process ID is the unique identifier of a tree.
syntax: function long create.tree (string tree_name, string tree_title)
returns: > 0 success; returns the process ID of the new tree 0 error

name: create.tree.button
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This adds a button to a specified tree. The client program can link a session or command to this button. An event is sent to the client when the user clicks on the button.
syntax: function void create.tree.button (string tree_name, long button_id, string button_desc [, long process_id])
returns: void

name: cs$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to change the window size and/or clear the window. The num_expr argument can have one of the the following values: 0 — clear current window 1 — clear current window (default value) 2 — set screen to 80 columns and clear current window 3 — set screen to 132 columns and clear current window 4 — set screen to 80 columns without clearing current window 5 — set screen to 132 columns without clearing current window
syntax: function string cs$ ( [long num_expr])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: curl.cleanup
doc: End cURL session.
syntax: function void curl.cleanup ()
returns: void

name: curl.create.oauth1.authorization.header
doc: Creates an OAuth 1.0 authorization header. Note that this function returns the header value, it must added to the HTTP request with header name "Authorization".
syntax: function long curl.create.oauth1.authorization.header (const string method, const string url, const string consumer.key, const string consumer.secret, ref string header)
returns: 0 — Ok curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.download.data
doc: Downloads data from the specified url and writes it to the specified data buffer. Note that the buffer must be large enough to store all downloaded data.
syntax: function long curl.download.data (const string url, ref string data, ref long data.size [, long header.list])
returns: 0 — Ok < 0 — Stream IO error curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.download.file
doc: Downloads data from the specified url and writes it to the specified file.
syntax: function long curl.download.file (const string url, const string file [, long header.list])
returns: 0 — Ok < 0 — Stream IO error curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.download.stream
doc: Downloads data from the specified url and writes it to the specified stream, which can be either a file or a memory stream. response.stream .
syntax: function long curl.download.stream (const string url, long response.stream [, long header.list])
returns: 0 — Ok < 0 — Stream IO error curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.download.string
doc: Downloads data from the specified url and writes it to the specified string buffer. Note that the string buffer must be large enough to store all data. The data will be null terminated, if possible.
syntax: function long curl.download.string (const string url, ref string data [, long header.list])
returns: 0 — Ok < 0 — Stream IO error curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.escape.decode$
doc: curl.escape.decode$() offers the inverse functionality of curl.escape.encode$().
syntax: function string curl.escape.decode$ (const string SomeText)
returns: Contains an string without escape sequences.

name: curl.escape.encode$

syntax: function string curl.escape.encode$ (const string SomeText)
returns: Contains an escaped string

name: curl.escape.encode.ext$

name: curl.escape.gettable

syntax: function void curl.escape.gettable (ref string(2,128) EscapeTable)
returns: void

name: curl.get.errorbuffer$
doc: Descriptive message on result of previous action
syntax: function string curl.get.errorbuffer$ ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: curl.http.status$
doc: Returns a english descriptive text for a given HTTP Status Code. E.g. when 200 (HTTP_STATUS_OK) is passed "OK" is returned, or when 503 (HTTP_STATUS_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE) is passed, "Service Unavailable" is returned. The descriptive text is meant for logging and tracing purposes and/or technical error messages.

name: curl.slist.append
doc: curl.slist.append() appends a specified string to a linked list of strings. This linked list can be used in some curl.setopt functions. The allowed value(s) of the passed string depend on the context where it is used. If the listId is zero, then a new list is created. The listId should be passed as the first argument if the string need to be appended to an existing list. The specified string has been added to the list when this function returns. The return value is the listId upon success or 0 upon error. The list should be freed after usage with curl.slist.free.all().
syntax: function long curl.slist.append (ref long listId, const string text)
returns: A list ID upon success or zero upon error.

name: curl.slist.free.all
doc: curl.slist.free.all() frees a linked list of strings. The listId will be reset to zero after completion.
syntax: function void curl.slist.free.all (ref long listId)
returns: void

name: curl.sso.user.encode$
syntax: function string curl.sso.user.encode$ (const string User)
returns: Contains an escaped SSO user string

name: curl.sso.user.gettable
doc: Returns a string array with an escapetable.
syntax: function void curl.sso.user.gettable (ref string(2,128) EscapeTable)
returns: void

name: curl.strerror$
doc: Descriptive message on result of previous action
syntax: function string curl.strerror$ (long CurlCode)
returns: Description of the error

name: curl.upload.data
doc: Uploads binary data to the specified url.
syntax: function long curl.upload.data (const string url, const string data, long data.size, long response.stream [, long header.list] [, const string method])
returns: 0 — Ok < 0 — Stream IO error curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.upload.file
doc: Uploads a file to the specified url.
syntax: function long curl.upload.file (const string url, const string file, long response.stream [, long header.list] [, const string method])
returns: 0 — Ok < 0 — Stream IO error curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.upload.stream
doc: Uploads data from a stream (a file or a memory stream) to the specified url.
syntax: function long curl.upload.stream (const string url, long request.stream, long data.size, long response.stream [, long header.list] [, const string method])
returns: 0 — Ok < 0 — Stream IO error curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.upload.string
doc: Uploads a (null terminated) string to the specified url.
syntax: function long curl.upload.string (const string url, const string data, long response.stream [, long header.list] [, const string method])
returns: 0 — Ok < 0 — Stream IO error curl.strerror$() > 0 — to get a descriptive message

name: curl.version
doc: Retrieves the current version of the cURL library that is being used and the versions of the other major components (like OpenSSL), as space-separated strings. This can be used to easily verify the level of support offered by the current bshell. The website of cURL lists the "available from version" for every feature and option.
syntax: function string curl.version ()
returns: Example: libcurl/7.57.0 OpenSSL/1.1.0g

name: curl.xml.get.error$
syntax: function string curl.xml.get.error$ ()
returns: Returns the errors in XML format.

name: curl.xml.set.whitespacehandling
syntax: function void curl.xml.set.whitespacehandling (long WhiteSpaceHandling)
returns: void

name: current.display
doc: This returns the identification number of the current display. It is provided to support the use of multiple displays in future versions of the software. Currently it always returns zero (0)
syntax: function long current.display ()
returns: This returns the identification number of the current display.

name: current.window
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This returns the identification number of the current window. A window becomes current when it is created or when you call change.window(). All actions to the screen ( print() for example) are sent to the current window.
syntax: function long current.window ()
returns: This returns the identification number of the current window.

name: d.expr
doc: Executes (or evaluates) an expression previously compiled by expr.compile(). The result is always converted to a double.
syntax: function double d.expr (long expr_id [, void value] [, boolean suppressError])
returns: The result of the expression converted to a double. You can execute compiled expressions multiple times without recompiling. The current values of the variables are used each time. Related topics

name: dal.any.parent.changed
doc: The function dal.any.parent.changed() determines whether any of the fields, from which the current field depends, is changed. This function can only be used in combination with dal.require.field().
syntax: function boolean dal.any.parent.changed ()
returns: true one or more parent fields have changed false no parent field has changed

name: dal.change.object
doc: Use this to indicate the DAL that the current record is about to be changed. After this call, fields can be changed with dal.set.field(). And after that, the record can be saved with dal.save.object().
syntax: function long dal.change.object (string dal_name)
returns: 0 — OK DALHOOKERROR — The DAL could not be opened

name: dal.check.field
doc: Checks whether the given field has a valid value. This performs the DAL check hooks in the given mode (default is DAL_UPDATE).
syntax: function long dal.check.field (string fld.name [, long element] [, long mode])
returns: 0 — Field is valid DALHOOKERROR — Field is invalid

name: dal.clear.error.messages
doc: This clears all DAL error messages from the message buffer. Abbreviation for dal.reset.error.messages(0).
syntax: function void dal.clear.error.messages ()
returns: void

name: dal.clear.messages
doc: This clears all DAL messages of the specified type from the message buffer. Abbreviation for dal.reset.messages(i.type, 0).
syntax: function void dal.clear.messages (long i.type)
returns: void

name: dal.copy.object
doc: Use this to indicate the DAL that a record is about to be copied. In contrary to dal.new.object(), this function does not call the set.object.defaults() hook! After this call, fields can be set with dal.set.field(). And after that, the record can be saved with dal.save.object().
syntax: function long dal.copy.object (string dal_name)
returns: 0 — OK DALHOOKERROR — The DAL could not be opened

name: dal.count.error.messages
doc: MSG.ERROR currently in the message buffer.
syntax: function long dal.count.error.messages ()
returns: The number of error messages in the message buffer.

name: dal.count.messages
doc: This returns the number of DAL messages of the specified type that are currently in the message buffer.
syntax: function long dal.count.messages (long i.type)
returns: The number of DAL messages of the specified type.

name: dal.destroy
doc: Use this to delete a database record. The function encapsulates the db.delete() function with the DAL hooks of the object set. If the before.destroy.object() hook fails, the database operation is cancelled.
syntax: function void dal.destroy (string dal.name, long object_set, ref long retval, long prop_check [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: void

name: dal.destroy.object
doc: Deletes a record of the given table. The record must have been locked for update. This function does the same as dal.destroy(), however it does more detailed permission checking. Further, the method.is.allowed() hook is always called ( dal.destroy() allows you to skip this hook by passing FALSE to the prop_check parameter). Except for more detailed permission checking, this function is equivalent to: dal.destroy(tbl.name, tbl.cursor, retval, true, db.retry) The sequence of the actions is as follows:
syntax: function long dal.destroy.object (string tbl.name [, long error.flag])
returns: 0 — Record is deleted DALHOOKERROR — One of the hooks blocked the delete action DALNOSETPERM — No table level permission DALNOOBJPERM — No record level permission > 0 — The error code of the db.delete() action

name: dal.execute.hook
doc: This starts a specified hook. This function will for the hooks is.applicable, is.derived, is.mandatory, is.readonly,never.applicable, is.valid, make.valid and update execute the extension hooks before and after executing the hook. If this is the first call to a particular class (that is, table), the before.open.object.set() hook is automatically called before the hook is called.
syntax: function void dal.execute.hook (string set_id, string name, ref long retval, long mode, long elem)
returns: void

name: dal.field.depends.on
doc: Use this to define that a field depends on one or more other fields. Dependencies are defined in terms of field hooks. dal.field.depends.on("a", HOOK_X, "b") means the following: the result of hook a.x() depends on the value of field b. So when changing field "b", hook a.x() is executed. dal.field.depends.on("whinh312.fire", HOOK_IS_APPLICABLE, "whinh312.lsta") should be used if the result of hook whinh312.fire.yes.is.applicable() depends on the value of whinh312.lsta.
syntax: function void dal.field.depends.on (const string fieldname, long hook.list, const string parent.fld.name, ... [, long hook.list] [, const string parent.fieldname, ...])
returns: void

name: dal.get.error.message
doc: MSG.ERROR from the message buffer. The message is removed from the buffer.
syntax: function long dal.get.error.message (ref string mesg)
returns: The number of error messages that remain in the message buffer, or -1 if the buffer is empty. (In the latter case the returned message is "".)

name: dal.get.error.msgcode
doc: This retrieves the message code of most recent DAL error message from the message buffer. The message is not removed from the buffer.
syntax: function string dal.get.error.msgcode ()
returns: The message code.

name: dal.get.field.mode
doc: Returns the mode of the given field. The mode indicates if the field has changed. This function is equivalent to: dal.get.property.flag(tbl.name, tbl.cursor, fld.name)
syntax: function long dal.get.field.mode (string tbl.name [, long element])
returns: 0 — Field is not changed DAL_NEW — Field has changed during insert of a record DAL_UPDATE — Field has changed during update of a record

name: dal.get.first.error.message
doc: MSG.ERROR from the message buffer, together with the message code. The message is removed from the buffer. Note that this function is slightly slower than dal.get.error.message().
syntax: function long dal.get.first.error.message (ref string mesg, ref string code)
returns: The number of error messages that remain in the message buffer, or -1 if the buffer is empty. (In the latter case the returned message and message code are both "".)

name: dal.get.first.message
doc: MSG.ALL is passed as the type, then the type of the message is returned in the 4th argument.
syntax: function boolean dal.get.first.message (long i.type, ref string o.code, ref string o.text [, ref long o.type])
returns: This function returns TRUE if a message could be retrieved, else FALSE is returned.

name: dal.get.last.message
doc: MSG.ALL is passed as the type, then the type of the message is returned in the 4th argument. The message is removed from the buffer.
syntax: function boolean dal.get.last.message (long i.type, ref string o.code, ref string o.text [, ref long o.type])
returns: This function returns TRUE if a message could be retrieved, else FALSE is returned.

name: dal.get.object
doc: Reads a record of the given table. In case the lock parameter is set to true, the record is locked for update. This function accepts a list of primary key field/value pairs. The sequence of the actions is as follows: In case this function is called in the context of a 4GL-Session for a table which is either defined as the maintable or a secondary table for this session, this function will check if the requested record is already present in the 4GL-Engine buffers. If so, the 4GL-Engine record buffer is fetched and will not be read from the database. This is especially useful when in a DAL script of a secondary table the corresponding maintable record is needed. The dal.get.object() function will return the table fields which are updated through the UI script or by the UI. However, in case these table fields are changed in a DAL script before the dal.get.object() function is called, the dal.get.object() will overwrite these changes.
syntax: function long dal.get.object (string tbl.name, long lock [, string key_field1] [, string key_value1], ...)
returns: 0 — Record is read or locked for update DALHOOKERROR — One of the hooks blocked the read action DALNOOBJPERM — No record level permission > 0 — The error code of the read action in case this failed (e.g. ENOREC). For a list of possible errormessages see the list of db-errormessages.

name: dal.get.property.flag
doc: Use this to retrieve the value of the has_changed flag (see Property hooks) for any database property dat.get.property.flag. The property must have been changed by the dal.set.property() function.
syntax: function long dal.get.property.flag (string tbl.name, long object_set, string prop_name)
returns: The function returns the value of the has_changed flag of the specified property. The possible values are: 0 — Property not changed. DAL_NEW — Change caused by inserting a new object. DAL_UPDATE — Change caused by updating an existing object. Properties with no check function in the DAL always return 0.

name: dal.is.copy.active
doc: DAL_NEW mode, to test whether the current record is being inserted, or being copied. You can use this in the field.update() to test whether the current record is being copied. true DUPL.OCCUR GLOBAL.COPY choice.
syntax: function boolean dal.is.copy.active ()
returns: true false in any other case.

name: dal.is.field.changed
doc: Use this to test whether a field has changed. It is equivalent to: dal.get.field.mode(fld.name, [ element ] ) <> 0
syntax: function boolean dal.is.field.changed (string fld.name [, long element])
returns: TRUE in case the field has changed, FALSE in case the field has not changed.

name: dal.new
doc: Use this to add a new record to the database. The function encapsulates the db.insert() function with the DAL hooks of the object set. If the before.save.object() hook fails, the database operation is cancelled.
syntax: function void dal.new (string tbl.name, long object_set, ref long retval, long prop_check [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: void

name: dal.new.object
doc: Use this to indicate the DAL that a new record is about to be inserted. This function set record defaults, by calling db.set.to.default() and the set.object.defaults() hook. After this call, fields can be set with dal.set.field(). And after that, the record can be saved with dal.save.object().
syntax: function long dal.new.object (string tbl.name)
returns: 0 — OK DALHOOKERROR — The DAL could not be opened

name: dal.parent.caused.update
doc: .update() hook. It checks whether this call to this hook was triggered by a change in field fld.name.
syntax: function boolean dal.parent.caused.update (string fld.name [, long element])
returns: true or false

name: dal.peek.error.message
doc: MSG.ERROR from the message buffer at position n. The message is not removed from the buffer.
syntax: function string dal.peek.error.message (long n)
returns: The message from the message buffer at position n, where n = 1 is the oldest message.

name: dal.peek.error.msgcode
doc: This retrieves the message code from the message buffer at position n. The message is not removed from the buffer.
syntax: function string dal.peek.error.msgcode (long n)
returns: The message code.

name: dal.peek.message
doc: MSG.ALL as the type, the type of the message is returned in the 5th argument.
syntax: function void dal.peek.message (long i.type, long i.index, ref string o.code, ref string o.text [, ref long o.type])
returns: void

name: dal.recall
doc: Makes a request to recall the checked-out business object that is identified by the current record. This is only possible for Pending objects.
syntax: function long dal.recall (const string tbl.name)
returns: 0 — The request for recall was successfully made. An error occurred. <> 0

name: dal.reject
doc: Rejects any changes and/or actions done to the current checked-out Business Object and sets the given reason for rejecting. This is possible for Pending objects, which become Rejected, and for objects for which a Recall has been requested, which will then become Pending again.
syntax: function long dal.reject (const string tbl.name, const string reason$)
returns: 0 — The request for reject was successfully made. An error occurred. <> 0

name: dal.require.field
doc: This function can be used to determine a specific order for the calls to the update hooks. The function only works properly if update hooks are triggered by the 4GL engine (amdll), and not called from the application itself.
syntax: function void dal.require.field (const string fieldname [, long element] [, ref boolean field.changed])
returns: void

name: dal.reset.error.messages
doc: MSG.ERROR from the message buffer.
syntax: function void dal.reset.error.messages (long amt)
returns: void

name: dal.reset.messages
doc: Removes the most recent messages of the given type from the DAL message buffer. The 2nd argument determines how many messages will remain in the buffer.
syntax: function void dal.reset.messages (long i.type, long i.count)
returns: void

name: dal.save.object
doc: Saves a record of the given table. In case a dal.new.object() or a dal.copy.object() was done, the record is inserted in the database. In case a dal.change.object() was done, the record is updated in the database. In case DAL2 Field dependencies have been defined in the DAL, this function takes care that dependent fields will be triggered in the right order so that they can update themselves. Note that this is done based on the values of the fields that have been set by calling dal.set.field() Before the record is saved all (changed) fields will be validated. The sequence of the actions is as follows:
syntax: function long dal.save.object (string tbl.name [, long error.flag])
returns: 0 — Record is saved DALHOOKERROR — One of the hooks blocked the save action DALDBERROR — A domain or reference error occurred (only in Integration context (e.g. via a BOL)) DALNOSETPERM — No table level permission DALNOOBJPERM — No record level permission > 0 — The error code of the db.insert() or db.update() function

name: dal.set.array.field
doc: Sets the value of the given array field and informs the DAL that the field is changed. This function assigns a complete array at once. If you want to set only one or a few array elements, use function dal.set.field(). The number of elements to set will be equal to the minimum of the array depth and the field depth. Example: This function is a shorthand for the following (pseudo) code: long i long depth depth = <the minimum value of the field depth and the array depth> if <array type is STRING> then for i = 1 to depth dal.set.field(fld.name, value(1,i), i) endfor else | Type is LONG or DOUBLE for i = 1 to depth dal.set.field(fld.name, value(i), i) endfor endif
syntax: function void dal.set.array.field (string fld.name, void value)
returns: void

name: dal.set.error.message
doc: Adds a message to the DAL message buffer of type MSG.ERROR. Short version of dal.set.message(). mess.or.code is a data dictionary message code or a literal string starting with @. Extra arguments fill sprintf$-style placeholders. Empty messages are not added. For dal.set.error.message(), messages are ignored while dal.set.messages.off() is in effect.
syntax: function void dal.set.error.message (string mess.or.code [, void arg ...])
returns: void

name: dal.set.field
doc: Sets the value of the given field and informs the DAL that the field is changed. This function does the same as: ret.val = dal.set.property(tbl.name, tbl.cursor, fld.name, value, mode) where tbl.name and tbl.cursor are provided automatically, and mode is DAL_NEW after dal.new.object() or dal.copy.object(), and otherwise DAL_UPDATE.
syntax: function void dal.set.field (string fld.name, void value [, long element])
returns: void

name: dal.set.info.message
doc: Adds a message to the DAL message buffer of type MSG.INFO. Short version of dal.set.message(). mess.or.code is a data dictionary message code or a literal string starting with @. Extra arguments fill sprintf$-style placeholders. Empty messages are not added.
syntax: function void dal.set.info.message (string mess.or.code [, void arg ...])
returns: void

name: dal.set.message
doc: Adds a message of the specified type to the DAL message buffer.
syntax: function void dal.set.message (long i.type, const string i.mess.or.code [, void arg ...])
returns: void

name: dal.set.messages.off
doc: Turns off dal.set.error.message(). After calling dal.set.messages.off(), any calls to dal.set.error.message() are ignored. To turn on dal.set.error.message() again, use dal.set.messages.on().
syntax: function void dal.set.messages.off ()
returns: void

name: dal.set.messages.on
doc: Turns on dal.set.error.message. To turn dal.set.error.message off, use dal.set.messages.off.
syntax: function void dal.set.messages.on ()
returns: void

name: dal.set.property
doc: In order to notify the DAL about a change to the value of a property, you must use this function to change the value. Using this function ensures that the relevant property hooks are executed when the value is changed. If you use an assignment or the db.* functions to change a property value, the DAL is not notified of the change. Consequently, the property checks in the DAL are not executed.
syntax: function long dal.set.property (string tbl.name, long object_set, string prop_name, void value, long mode)
returns: Always 0

name: dal.set.property.with.check
doc: In order to notify the DAL about a change to the value of a property, you must use this function to change the value. Using this function ensures that the relevant property hooks are executed when the value is changed. If you use an assignment or the db.* functions to change a property value, the DAL is not notified of the change. Consequently, the property checks in the DAL are not executed.
syntax: function long dal.set.property.with.check (string tbl.name, long object_set, const string proper_name, void value)
returns: The return value of the property check.

name: dal.set.warning.message
doc: Adds a message to the DAL message buffer of type MSG.WARNING. Short version of dal.set.message(). mess.or.code is a data dictionary message code or a literal string starting with @. Extra arguments fill sprintf$-style placeholders. Empty messages are not added.
syntax: function void dal.set.warning.message (string mess.or.code [, void arg ...])
returns: void

name: dal.skip.never.applicable.checks
doc: By default, the 4GL engine will check fields that are defined as never applicable. You can skip these checks by calling this function in the before.open.object.set() hook in the DAL.
syntax: function void dal.skip.never.applicable.checks ( [boolean keep_old_data])
returns: void

name: dal.start.business.method
doc: This starts a specified business method. The business method must be implemented as a function of type EXTERN LONG. If this is the first call to a particular class (that is, table), the before.open.object.set() hook is automatically called before the business method is called.
syntax: function void dal.start.business.method (string set_id, string name, ref long retval [, ...])
returns: void

name: dal.submit
doc: Assigns the Pending status to the checked-out Business Object that is identified by the current record. Only Draft, Draft (Revision), and Rejected business objects can be submitted.
syntax: function long dal.submit (const string tbl.name)
returns: 0 — The submit was successful. An error occurred. <> 0

name: dal.undo.check.out
doc: DBCM_STATUS_DRAFT DBCM_STATUS_DRAFT_REV DBCM_STATUS_REJECTED .
syntax: function long dal.undo.check.out (const string tbl.name)
returns: 0 — In case of success. An error occurred. <> 0

name: dal.update
