doc: Use this to update an existing database record. The function encapsulates the db.update() function with the DAL hooks of the object set. If the before.save.object() hook fails, the database operation is cancelled.
syntax: function void dal.update (string class_name, long object_set, ref long retval, long prop_check [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: void

name: data.input
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This reads data from the keyboard. If the function specifies a default value, that value is displayed on screen. The value is accepted when the user presses ENTER. However, if the user enters a character at the first position in the field, the default value is deleted. Normally, characters typed by the user are inserted before the current cursor position. However, if option 'C' is included in the options argument, characters typed by the user are inserted at the current cursor position. Users can edit the default value or make minor corrections to the string entered (before they press ENTER) by using the following keys: RIGHT ARROW — Scroll right. LEFT ARROW — Scroll left. DEL — Delete character at cursor position. Characters to the right of the deleted character are moved one position to the left. If the cursor is positioned beyond the last character, this character is deleted and the cursor moves one position to the left. Pressing DEL in an empty field redisplays the default value. CTRL+X — Clear field. TAB — Delete all characters from the cursor position to the end of the field.
syntax: function void data.input (string options(.), ref string result(.), string default(.), ref long event(EVTMAXSIZE), ref long char_value)
returns: void

name: date.num
doc: This returns the number of days from 01-01-0001 to the system date. The applicable timezone can be found with the function get.time.zone().
syntax: function long date.num ()
returns: >= 0 — The number of days from 01-01-0001 to the system date. -1 — Error.

name: date.to.date
doc: This converts a date and time in one time zone to the corresponding date and time in a different time zone.
syntax: function long date.to.date (long in_date, long in_time, const string in_zone, const string out_zone, ref long out_date, ref long out_time)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error.

name: date.to.inputstr$
doc: This converts a specified number of days since 01-01-0001 to a date input string.
syntax: function string date.to.inputstr$ (long dayno, string format(7), long length)
returns: The formatted input string. An empty string if an error occurs.

name: date.to.iso
doc: This converts a local date to an ISO 8601 date string. This is a string with the format: yyyy-mm-dd
syntax: function string date.to.iso (long local.date)
returns: The string representation of the local date in ISO 8601 format. If an invalid local date is specified, the following string is returned: "0000-00-00"

name: date.to.num
doc: This returns the number of days since 01-01-0001 for a specified year, month, and day of the month.
syntax: function long date.to.num (long yearno, long monthno, long month_dayno)
returns: 0 — The number of days since 01-01-0001. -1 — Error.

name: date.to.utc
doc: This converts the specified local date and time to UTC long format. Input values must be in the signed 32-bit value range.
syntax: function domain ttutc date.to.utc (long yearno, long monthno, long month_dayno, long hours, long minutes, long seconds)
returns: >= 0 — The UTC long format value. -1 — Error. The exact result is negative or greater than the maximum value 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) - 1 of the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range.

name: date.with.timezone.info.to.utc
doc: This converts the specified local date and time to UTC long format. For this conversion it will NOT use the timezone of the user, but the difference in seconds to UTC as supplied in the variable utcdiff. Input values must be in the signed 32-bit value range.
syntax: function domain ttutc date.with.timezone.info.to.utc (long yearno, long monthno, long month_dayno, long hours, long minutes, long seconds, long utcdiff)
returns: >= 0 — The UTC long format value. -1 — Error. The exact result is negative or greater than the maximum value 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) - 1 of the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range.

name: db.after.delete
doc: dal.destroy.object() dal.destroy() is called. db.delete() is done. db.delete() If this hook is called via a DAL function then the variable initiated.by.dal = true. If called via a DB function then this variable is false.
syntax: function extern long db.after.delete ()
returns: This hooks returns 0 if deleting the record is permitted. It should return a negative value like DALHOOKERROR, in case of an error.

name: db.after.insert
doc: dal.new.object() dal.new() is called. db.insert() is done. db.insert() If this hook is called via a DAL function then the variable initiated.by.dal = true If called via a DB function then this variable is false.
syntax: function extern long db.after.insert ()
returns: This hooks returns 0 if deleting the record is permitted. It should return a negative value like DALHOOKERROR, in case of an error.

name: db.after.update
doc: dal.save.object() dal.update() is called. db.update() is done. db.update() If this hook is called via a DAL function then the variable initiated.by.dal = true. If called via a DB function then this variable is false.
syntax: function extern long db.after.update ()
returns: This hooks returns 0 if deleting the record is permitted. It should return a negative value like DALHOOKERROR, in case of an error.

name: db.before.delete
doc: dal.destroy.object() dal.destroy() is called. db.delete() is done. db.delete() operation. If this hook is called via a DAL function then the variable initiated.by.dal = true. If called via a DB function then this variable is false.
syntax: function extern long db.before.delete ()
returns: This hooks returns 0 if deleting the record is permitted. It should return a negative value like DALHOOKERROR, in case of an error.

name: db.before.insert
doc: dal.new.object() dal.new() is called. db.insert() is done. db.insert() operation. If this hook is called via a DAL function then the variable initiated.by.dal = true. If called via a DB function then this variable is false.
syntax: function extern long db.before.insert ()
returns: This hooks returns 0 if deleting the record is permitted. It should return a negative value like DALHOOKERROR, in case of an error.

name: db.before.update
doc: dal.update() . db.update() is done. db.update() operation. If this hook is called via a DAL function then the variable initiated.by.dal = true. If called via a DB function then this variable is false.
syntax: function extern long db.before.update ()
returns: This hooks returns 0 if deleting the record is permitted. It should return a negative value like DALHOOKERROR, in case of an error.

name: db.bind
doc: This creates a pointer to a specified table. It returns a table ID that you use in other database calls to identify the table. The pointer is to a table with a particular company number and record buffer. You can create additional pointers to the same table by calling the function with a different company number and/or record buffer.Every call to db.bind()returns a unique pointer.
syntax: function long db.bind (string table_name(9) [, ref string buffer(.)] [, long comp_nr])
returns: 0 — Error. > 0 — Success; pointer is returned.

name: db.blob.append
doc: This function appends data to the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.append(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. It is required to lock the record. if the lock is a delayed lock then db.blob.append() will promote the delayed lock to a lock in the database automatically (limitation: without EROWCHANGED check on the BLOB data). A call to db.blob.append() causes a flush of buffered updates. Such a flush can cause a jump to the retry point. Errors that occur in db.blob.append() itself do not cause a jump to the retry point. For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, and then appends data to the BLOB: long num.bytes long ret string blobdata(100) blobdata = "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" num.bytes = len(blobdata) select dbtst000.photo from dbtst000 for update where dbtst000.item = "001" selectdo ret = db.blob.append(dbtst000.photo, num.bytes, blobdata) endselect commit.transaction()
syntax: function long db.blob.append (const string blob.locator, long num.bytes, const string bytes.array [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.blob.append.xml
doc: This function appends data from an XML tree to the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.append.xml(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. It is required to lock the record. if the lock is a delayed lock then db.blob.append.xml() will promote the delayed lock to a lock in the database automatically (limitation: without EROWCHANGED check on the BLOB data). A call to db.blob.append.xml() causes a flush of buffered updates. Such a flush can cause a jump to the retry point. Errors that occur in db.blob.append.xml() itself do not cause a jump to the retry point.
syntax: function long db.blob.append.xml (const string blob.locator, long xml.node [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error. — for some negative return values additional information can be found with function xmlWrite().

name: db.blob.clear
doc: This function clears the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.clear(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. It is required to lock the record. if the lock is a delayed lock then db.blob.clear() will promote the delayed lock to a lock in the database automatically (limitation: without EROWCHANGED check on the BLOB data). For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, and then clears the BLOB: long num.bytes long ret select dbtst000.photo from dbtst000 for update where dbtst000.item = "001" selectdo ret = db.blob.clear(dbtst000.photo) endselect commit.transaction()
syntax: function long db.blob.clear (const string blob.locator [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.blob.read
doc: This function reads data from the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.read(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, and then retrieves the first 256 bytes of the picture: string bytes.array(256) long num.bytes long ret select dbtst000.photo from dbtst000 where dbtst000.item = "001" selectdo ret = db.blob.read(dbtst000.photo, 1, 256, bytes.array, num.bytes) endselect
syntax: function long db.blob.read (const string blob.locator, long offset, long num.bytes, ref string bytes.array, ref long num.bytes.read)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.blob.read.xml
doc: This function reads data from the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers, and parses it to an XML tree. Before calling db.blob.read.xml(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, and then retrieves the first 256 bytes of the picture: string bytes.array(256) string error(120) long bytes.read long xml.node long ret select dbtst000.photo from dbtst000 where dbtst000.item = "001" selectdo ret = db.blob.read.xml(dbtst000.photo, 1, bytes.read, xml.node, error, XmlPreserveWhiteSpace) endselect Note: A parse error is returned when the BLOB is empty; this is similar to parsing an empty string using XmlReadFromString().
syntax: function long db.blob.read.xml (const string blob.locator, long offset, ref long bytes.read, ref long xml.node, ref string error, long whitespacehandling)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error, e.g. E_BDB_INVALID_BLOB or E_BDB_XML_PARSE_ERROR

name: db.blob.read.xml.ns
doc: This function reads data from the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers, and parses it to an XML tree. Before calling db.blob.read.xml.ns(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, and then retrieves the first 256 bytes of the picture: string bytes.array(256) string error(120) long bytes.read long xml.node long ret select dbtst000.photo from dbtst000 where dbtst000.item = "001" selectdo ret = db.blob.read.xml.ns(dbtst000.photo, 1, bytes.read, xml.node, error, XmlPreserveWhiteSpace) endselect Note: A parse error is returned when the BLOB is empty; this is similar to parsing an empty string using XmlReadFromString(). This function supports XML namespaces, and will create namespace declarations carried by the respective XML nodes, and put XML nodes in their appropriate namespace.
syntax: function long db.blob.read.xml.ns (const string blob.locator, long offset, ref long bytes.read, ref long xml.node, ref string error, long whitespacehandling)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error, e.g. E_BDB_INVALID_BLOB or E_BDB_XML_PARSE_ERROR

name: db.blob.size
doc: This function retrieves the size of the BLOB, to which the BLOB locator refers. Before calling db.blob.size(), the BLOB locator must be read from the database. For example, the following code retrieves the BLOB locator that refers to a certain picture from a table, and then retrieves the size of the picture: long num.bytes long ret select dbtst000.photo from dbtst000 where dbtst000.item = "001" selectdo ret = db.blob.size(dbtst000.photo, num.bytes) endselect
syntax: function long db.blob.size (const string blob.locator, ref long num.bytes)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.change.order
doc: This makes a specified index the current index. After this action, the record pointer is undefined.
syntax: function long db.change.order (long table_id, long index_nr [, long compnr])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.check.restricted
doc: In a table definition, it is possible to set restrictions on update and/or delete actions for records that are referenced by other tables. These restrictions mean that you cannot delete and/or update the primary key that is referenced by another table. This function checks whether there are references to the current record with delete and/or update restrictions. This function can take a long time to complete if no reference counter is kept (lookup mode).
syntax: function long db.check.restricted (long table_id, long mode, ref string message(256))
returns: 0 — No reference found. 1 — One or more references found. -1 — Error.

name: db.check.row.changed
doc: This function checks whether a record that has been delayed locked and changed by the current process has been changed by another process ("user"). It does not check whether the row has been modified in the current process. In a way it answers the question: "If I would update the current record now, would I get the infamous EROWCHANGED error?"
syntax: function long db.check.row.changed (long table_id)
returns: 0 — Record has not been changed by another process. <> 0 — Error. EROWCHANGED — Record has been changed by another process. ENOCURR — No current record set. The db-call interface (e.g. db.eq( ..., db.delayed)) must be used to set a current record, before calling the db.check.row.changed() function. ENOTLOCKED — Record has not been (delayed) locked.

name: db.check.row.dlocked
doc: This checks whether the row, identified by its primary key columns is delayed locked or not. If the row is already locked, the function returns the dlock number of the row. This function can result in a considerable performance gain as it eradicates the need for multiple reads of the same record.
syntax: function long db.check.row.dlocked (long table_id)
returns: 0 — Row is not locked n — The dlock number, implying that row is locked < 0 — Error.

name: db.check.row.domains
doc: This checks whether the current record of a specified table conforms to the domain definitions in the data dictionary. All fields of the record are checked in turn until an error occurs. The function returns when the first error is encountered.
syntax: function long db.check.row.domains (long table_id, ref string fld_name)
returns: 0 — No errors. -1 — Invalid table ID. ENOTINRANGE — Error in a field. If an error is returned, you can retrieve information about the specific error using db.error.message().

name: db.clear.table
doc: This deletes all data from a specified table. Reference counters are automatically updated. By default (WITH.ROLLBACK) , all deleted records are saved in rollback segments. Consequently, using this function to clear a large table can result in reduced performance and, in some cases, can cause overflow of the internal rollback segments. Note that this function cannot be used within a transaction if the option NO.ROLLBACK is given; see Transaction handling.
syntax: function long db.clear.table (long table_id [, long flag] [, long comp_nr])
returns: 0: success <> 0: error

name: db.columns.to.record
doc: The record buffer of a table is used for reading records from, or writing records to, that table. When you bind to a table (see db.bind()) and specify that the default record buffer is to be used, the contents of the table fields are automatically copied to the buffer. This does not happen when you specify a record buffer other than the default buffer. Therefore, when a record buffer is used which is not the default record buffer, the record buffer may not contain the same field values as the table fields. This function can be called to copy the field values from the table fields to the record buffer. The record buffer must contain the correct field values before reading from, or writing to, the database.
syntax: function long db.columns.to.record (long table_id)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.create.table
doc: This creates a new database table. Note that this function cannot be used within a transaction; see Transaction handling.
syntax: function long db.create.table (long table_id, long compnr)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.curr
doc: This reads the current record from a specified table.
syntax: function long db.curr (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.delete
doc: This deletes the current record. The record pointer is not changed, so the current record is undefined after the record has been deleted.
syntax: function long db.delete (long table_id [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.drop.table
doc: This deletes a specified table. Data and indices associated with the table are also deleted. Reference counters are automatically updated. Note that this function cannot be used within a transaction; see Transaction handling.
syntax: function long db.drop.table (long table_id [, long flag] [, long comp_nr])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.eq
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value equals a certain predefined value. Before calling db.eq(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example, the following code retrieves the item with item number 001 from the items table: tiitm001.item = "001" db.eq( ttiitm001 )
syntax: function long db.eq (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.error
doc: Use this to retrieve the error code returned by the most recent database action. If you specify a table ID, the function retrieves the most recent error code returned by an action on that table.
syntax: function long db.error ( [long table_id])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: db.error.message
doc: Some errors returned by a database action have an associated error message. This message provides additional information about the error. Use the db.error.message() function to retrieve the error message (if any) associated with the most recent error code returned by a database action.
syntax: function string db.error.message ()
returns: The error message associated with the most recent error that occurred. Or an empty string if no message is associated with the error.

name: db.first
doc: This reads the first record from a specified table. It uses the current index to search the table.
syntax: function long db.first (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.flush
doc: All buffered actions are flushed to the database.
syntax: function long db.flush ()
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.ge
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value is greater than or equal to a certain predefined value. Before calling db.ge(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example: tiitm001.item = "001" db.ge( ttiitm001 )
syntax: function long db.ge (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.get.error.bypass
doc: This function returns the current value of error.bypass and, optionally, the current value of error.bypass.with.retry. It is allowed to call this function without having called the db.set.error.bypass.on() function.
syntax: function boolean db.get.error.bypass ( [ref boolean with.retry])
returns: The current value of error.bypass.

name: db.get.physical.compnr
doc: Use this to retrieve the physical company number for the specified table ( tblname) and logical company number ( logical.compnr).
syntax: function long db.get.physical.compnr (string tblname, long logical.compnr)
returns: >= 0 — Success: the company number. -1 — Error. The tblname or the logical.compnr is not correct. (e is set to E_BADARG)

name: db.gt
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value is greater than a certain predefined value. Before calling db.gt(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example: tiitm001.item = "001" db.gt( ttiitm001 )
syntax: function long db.gt (long table_id, long lock)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.indexinfo
doc: This returns information about the parts of a specified index.
syntax: function long db.indexinfo (long table_id, long index_nr, ref long index_info(32, 3), ref long indexparts, ref boolean indexdups, ref boolean indexactive)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.insert
doc: This adds a new record to a specified table. The record pointer does not change.
syntax: function long db.insert (long table_id [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.last
doc: This reads the last record from a specified table. It uses the current index to search the table.
syntax: function long db.last (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.le
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value is less than or equal to a certain predefined value. Before calling db.le(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example: tiitm001.item = "001" db.le( ttiitm001 )
syntax: function long db.le (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.lock.table
doc: This locks a specified table. Other users cannot then write to or delete the table or any parts of the table. Nor can they lock the table or any parts of the table. The lock is released by commit.transaction() or abort.transaction() Note that this function cannot be used within a transaction; see Transaction handling.
syntax: function long db.lock.table (long table_id)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.lt
doc: This reads from a specified table the record whose key value is less than a certain predefined value. Before calling db.lt(), you must assign the required value to the key field. For example: tiitm001.item = "001" db.lt( ttiitm001 )
syntax: function long db.lt (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.max.retry
doc: This function returns the value of the MAX_RETRY resource setting, which indicates how often the system may return to a retry point as a result of an abort in an update action. This is a better alternative for getenv$("MAX_RETRY").
syntax: function long db.max.retry ()
returns: The value of the MAX_RETRY resource.

name: db.next
doc: This reads the next record from a specified table. It uses the current index to search the table. If there is no current record, the function returns an error message.
syntax: function long db.next (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.nr.indices
doc: This returns the number of indices that exist on a specified table.
syntax: function long db.nr.indices (long table_id, ref long nr_indices)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.nr.rows
doc: This returns the number of rows that a specified table contains.
syntax: function long db.nr.rows (long table_id, ref long nr_rows [, long comp_nr])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.permission
doc: Use this to check the access permissions that a user has to a specified table or table field.
syntax: function long db.permission (long table_id, string field [, ref string buffer])
returns: The function returns a long that indicates the permissions that the user has on the table or on a specified field of that table. The return value consists of one of, or a combination of, the following codes: NO.PERMISSION 1 PERM.READ 2 PERM.MODIFY 4 PERM.WRITE 8 PERM.DELETE 16 NO.RESTRICTION (PERM.READ+PERM.MODIFY+PERM.WRITE+PERM.DELETE) PERM.UNKNOWN 32 So, if the value 6 is returned, the user is permitted to both read and modify the specified table or table field.

name: db.prev
doc: This reads the previous record from a specified table. It uses the current index to search the table. If there is no current record, the function returns an error message.
syntax: function long db.prev (long table_id [, long lock])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.record.changed
doc: Tests whether the current value of the record buffer belonging to the given table id has changed since the last call of db.store.record(). First, a db.columns.to.record() is done in order to copy the table field values to the record buffer. Then this record buffer is compared to the one stored with db.store.record(). db.record.changed() is implemented as a macro. This is the actual implementation: #define db.record.changed(tbl) ^ (db.columns.to.record(tbl) <> 0 or changed(rcd.##tbl, KEEP.CHANGED.FLAG.RAISED)) The optional argument size can be used from TIV level 2120 Usage example |* example of using db.store.record / db.change.record with size argument long size long ret long dummy table ttcmcs003 ret = rdi.table("tcmcs003", dummy, dummy, dummy, size) |Size is the length of a row in the table without the internal data db.store.record(ttcmcs003, size) ret = switch.to.company(0) |This will change tccom003._compnr stored in the internal data if db.record.changed(ttcmcs003, size) then |record is changed (This happens when you call one of the functions without size) else |record is not changed (Using size the internal record data like _compnr is not compared) endif
syntax: function boolean db.record.changed (long table_id [, long size])
returns: true — Record was changed since the last call to db.store.record() false — Record was not changed

name: db.record.to.columns
doc: When you bind to a table (see db.bind() and specify that the default record buffer is to be used, the contents of the buffer are automatically copied to the table fields in your program script. This does not happen when you specify a record buffer other than the default buffer. Therefore, when a record buffer is used which is not the default record buffer, the table fields will be invalid after the record buffer has changed and this function must be called to copy the field values from the record buffer to the table fields.
syntax: function long db.record.to.columns (long table_id)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.ref.handle.mode
doc: Use this to check whether a full table scan (FTS) is necessary during delete or update operations. Delete and update operations can take a long time to complete when the table is referenced by other tables but no reference counter is kept (cascade, nullify, or lookup mode). When there is no index on the foreign key in the child table, normally a full table scan is required to search for referring records.
syntax: function long db.ref.handle.mode (string table_name, long mode)
returns: 0 — Full table scan is not necessary. 1 — Full table scan is necessary.

name: db.restore.record
doc: This restores the record of the given table that was stored previously with db.store.record(). Also the table's field values will be restored. db.record.changed() is implemented as a macro. This is the actual implementation: #define db.restore.record(tbl) ^ not.curr(rcd.##tbl) ^ db.record.to.columns(tbl)
syntax: function void db.restore.record (long table_id)
returns: void

name: db.retry.hit
doc: Use this to check whether the client database layer has returned to a retry point. You must set the retry point by using db.retry.point() before you call db.retry.hit(). See also Database handling overview.
syntax: function long db.retry.hit ()
returns: 0 — Retry point defined but not returned to. > 0 — System returned to retry point. -1 — No Retry point defined -2 — Stack Error (Programming error in script. A db.retry.point() was done at a deeper stack level)

name: db.retry.point
doc: This sets a retry point for the current transaction. The program returns to this point if an error occurs during the transaction; the transaction is then retried. When you include a retry point for a transaction, you must set it before the start of the transaction. When a retry occurs, all messages that were set with dal.set.error.message are also reset. Messages that were set before the retry point will be retained.
syntax: function void db.retry.point ()
returns: void

name: db.row.length
doc: Use this to retrieve the length of records in a specified table.
syntax: function long db.row.length (long table_id, ref long row_length)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.set.error.bypass.off
doc: This function resets the values of error.bypass and error.bypass.with.retry to the previous values. The function must be called exactly once for each time the function db.set.error.bypass.on() is called. Calling this function more often than calling db.set.error.bypass.on() is a programming error and results in a fatal error.
syntax: function void db.set.error.bypass.off ()
returns: void

name: db.set.error.bypass.on
doc: This function flushes all buffered database actions in the current transaction before setting the error.bypass and error.bypass.with.retry flags. If any of the database actions results in a retryable error a jump is made to the db.retry.point(). If any of the actions results in a fatal error, then the process is terminated. If any error occurs then the values of error.bypass and error.bypass.with.retry are not modified. After successful flush, sets the value of error.bypass to true. The value of error.bypass.with.retry is set to the value specified by the with.retry argument, or to false if the argument is not given. Note that not all errors can be handled by using this function. See Error Handling in Database operations overview.
syntax: function long db.set.error.bypass.on ( [boolean with.retry])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.set.to.default
doc: This sets bound variables in the program script to the default values defined in the data dictionary.
syntax: function long db.set.to.default (long table_id)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.store.record
doc: Creates a copy of the current value of the record buffer belonging to the given table id. Later on this copied value can be restored by calling db.restore.record(). db.store.record() . db.record.changed() is implemented as a macro. This is the actual implementation: #define db.store.record(tbl) ^ db.columns.to.record(tbl) ^ on.change.check(rcd.##tbl) The optional argument size can be used from TIV level 2120 Usage example |* example of using db.store.record / db.change.record with size argument long size long ret long dummy table ttcmcs003 ret = rdi.table("tcmcs003", dummy, dummy, dummy, size) |Size is the length of a row in the table without the internal data db.store.record(ttcmcs003, size) ret = switch.to.company(0) |This will change tccom003._compnr stored in the internal data if db.record.changed(ttcmcs003, size) then |record is changed (This happens when you call one of the functions without size) else |record is not changed (Using size the internal record data like _compnr is not compared) endif
syntax: function void db.store.record (long table_id [, long size])
returns: void

name: db.unbind
doc: This deletes the specified table pointer.
syntax: function long db.unbind (long table_id)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: db.update
doc: This rewrites the current record. When updating a record with this function, you are permitted to update the primary key of the record.
syntax: function long db.update (long table_id [, long mode] [, long eflag])
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error.

name: dbcm.checked.out.objects.present
doc: Checks if checked-out objects exist in given company and (if provided) given table.
syntax: function boolean dbcm.checked.out.objects.present (long comp [, string tbl.name$])
returns: true — Checked out objects are present in given company (and table). false — In any other case.

name: dbcm.find.object.by.workflow.id
doc: Finds a checked-out business object using the given workflow instance id. When the object is found, the Typed Object Id is returned. This function is typically used in the communication between ION Workflow and Infor LN when processing BODs.
syntax: function long dbcm.find.object.by.workflow.id (const string wf.id$, ref string toid$)
returns: 0 — The object was found successfully. ENOREC (111) — The object was not found; probably the object is not checked out. Another database error. <> 0

name: dbcm.get.cm.action$
doc: Retrieves the Change Management action id of the Object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.cm.action$ (const string toid$)
returns: The action id of the Object as string; or an empty string in case the Object is not checked-out. For the standard actions UI Create, UI Change and UI Delete, the action ids are predefined: DBCM_ACTION_CREATE DBCM_ACTION_CHANGE DBCM_ACTION_DELETE

name: dbcm.get.cm.status
doc: Retrieves the Change Management status of the Object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id.
syntax: function enum dbcm.get.cm.status (const string toid$)
returns: Constant — Value — Description DBCM_STATUS_DRAFT 1 — The Object is in the Draft state; it is checked-out, it can be modified and any changes can be submitted, or any changes can be undone by doing a Revert to Approved. DBCM_STATUS_DRAFT_REV 2 — The Object is in the Draft state, for a second time; this state is equal to the DBCM_STATUS_DRAFT state, except that an Object can only enter this state after a Recall of any submitted changes was successful. DBCM_STATUS_PENDING 3 — The Object is in the Pending state; this means any changes to the Object have been submitted and the user must wait until the changes are Approved or Rejected. The Object cannot be modified. DBCM_STATUS_RECALL_REQ 4 — The Object is in the Recall Requested state; the user made a request to ignore any submitted changes, as he e.g. wants to make more changes to the Object. The Object cannot be modified. DBCM_STATUS_REJECTED 5 — The Object is in the Rejected state; any submitted changes were not approved. The user must either make other changes and re-submit them, or perform a Revert to Approved. The Object can be modified. DBCM_STATUS_APPR_RECVD 6 — The Object is in the Approval Received state; usually this state will not be visible to the user. It can only be visible if somehow, after receiving an Approval, the Object cannot be checked-in. In this situation an Admin must be involved in order to force a check-in, or to discard any changes and perform a Revert to Approved. The Object can be modified. DBCM_STATUS_APPROVED 7 — The Object is in the Approved state; any submitted changes have been Approved, and the Object has been checked-in. The Object can be modified.

name: dbcm.get.functional.id$
doc: Retrieves the functional object id for a checked-out object. The functional id is a concatenation of the values of all primary key parts, separated with commas. E.g. "SLS000368, 10" for Line 10 of Sales Order SLS000368.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.functional.id$ (const string toid$ [, long comp])
returns: The functional id as string (key parts are concatenated using commas); or an empty string in case of an error.

name: dbcm.get.object.action$
doc: Returns the currently selected object action (as selected with dbcm.select.object.action()), or an empty string in case no object action has been selected.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.object.action$ ()
returns: The currently selected object action, or an empty string in case no object action is set.

name: dbcm.get.object.id$
doc: Returns the id of the currently selected object instance (as selected with dbcm.select.object.instance()), or an empty string in case no object instance is selected or if a previously selected object instance is out of scope.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.object.id$ ()
returns: The id of the currently selected object instance, or an empty string in case no object instance is set.

name: dbcm.get.object.type$
doc: Returns the currently selected object type (as selected with dbcm.select.object.type()), or an empty string in case no object type is selected or if the previously selected object type is out of scope.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.object.type$ ()
returns: The currently selected object type, or an empty string in case no object type is set.

name: dbcm.get.rcd.action
doc: Retrieves the CM Action of the current record of the given table id. The CM Action of a record is set when the checked-out version of that particular record is different from the checked-in version.
syntax: function long dbcm.get.rcd.action (long tbl.id)
returns: There is no checked-out version of this record. Note that this particular may still be part of a checked-out business object. Conceptually, the complete business object is checked-out, however on individual record level, some records may still be unchanged, compared to the checked-in version. CMAC_NONE (0) The record has been inserted. This means that there is only a checked-out version of this record and no checked-in version. CMAC_INSERT (1) The record has been updated. This means that there two versions of this record, a checked-in and a checked-out one, which differ from each other. CMAC_UPDATE (2) The record has been deleted. This means that physically there are two versions of this record, a checked-in and a checked-out one. However, the checked-out one cannot be retrieved from the database with a query. So conceptually, this record has been deleted from the checked-out business object. CMAC_DELETE (3) Very short lived value that can be visible using a dirty read database CMAC_GHOST (11)

name: dbcm.get.rcd.prst
doc: Retrieves the checked-in value of the workflow application status field (identified by dbcm.get.app.status.field())of business object related to the current record buffer.
syntax: function enum dbcm.get.rcd.prst (long tbl.id)
returns: The current record buffer is not a record of the root table of any object type or the object type does not have workflow application status field or no checked-in version of the business object related to this current record buffer. empty the current record buffer is a record of the root table and the related object type has a workflow application status field. <> empty

name: dbcm.get.rcd.toid$
doc: Retrieves the Typed Object ID of the current record of the given table id.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.rcd.toid$ (long tbl.id)
returns: The Typed Object ID, or an empty string in case no Typed Object ID could be found.

name: dbcm.get.root.table$
doc: Returns the root table of an either an Object or an Object Type. In case a Type Object Id is specified (which identifies a specific instance of a certain Object Type), first the Object Type is determined. Then, for that Object Type, the root table is returned.
syntax: function string dbcm.get.root.table$ (const string toid.or.obj.type$)
returns: The root table code, or an empty string in case of an error.

name: dbcm.get.type.name
doc: Returns the object type for the given table, as defined in the Object Configuration Management model for the current package combination.
syntax: function long dbcm.get.type.name (const string tbl.name$, ref string obj.type$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. -1 — In case of an error; variable e contains the error code. See Database Change Management (DBCM) error codes for more information about the error codes and their meaning. 1 — The given table occurs in more than one object type (ie. the table is a shared table); an example of this may be table tcibd420.

name: dbcm.get.user
doc: Retrieves the user who last 'touched' the Business object which is identified by the specified type object id. In case the Business Object is Draft, this is the user who caused the check-out of this Object. Once the Business Object is Submitted, this is the user who did Submit the changes.
syntax: function long dbcm.get.user (const string toid$, ref string user$)
returns: 0 — The user code is retrieved successfully. ENOREC — The object cannot be found; probably the object is not checked-out. <> 0 — Any other database error.

name: dbcm.get.workflow.definition
doc: Retrieves the workflow definition id of the checked-out business object which is identified by the specified Typed Object Id.
syntax: function long dbcm.get.workflow.definition (const string toid$, ref string wf.def$)
returns: 0 — The workflow definition id is retrieved successfully. ENOREC — The object cannot be found; probably the object is not checked-out. <> 0 — Any other database error.

name: dbcm.get.workflow.id
doc: Retrieves the workflow instance id of the checked-out business object which is identified by the specified Typed Object Id.
syntax: function long dbcm.get.workflow.id (const string toid$, ref string wf.id$)
returns: 0 — The workflow definition id is retrieved successfully. ENOREC — The object cannot be found; probably the object is not checked-out. <> 0 — Any other database error.

name: dbcm.get.workflow.status.description
doc: Returns the workflow status description of an object instance for the given table in the current company based on a list of field/value pairs or the primary key field values of the current record buffer.
syntax: function long dbcm.get.workflow.status.description (const string tbl.name$, ref string wf.status.desc$ [, const string fld.name] [, void fld.value] [, ...])
returns: 0 — In case of success, wf.status.desc$ contains the workflow status description. -1 — Invalid number of arguments -2 — Invalid table specified in tbl.name$ -3 — tbl.name$ is not a root table of any object type -4 — Cannot read Runtime DD of tbl.name$ -5 — Cannot determine the object type for tbl.name$ -6 — Cannot select the object type for tbl.name$ -7 — Cannot construct a valid query to find the object instance -8 — Cannot execute the query to find the object instance -9 — Cannot find matching object instance -10 — Multiple object instances found

name: dbcm.is.action.active
doc: Tests whether the currently selected object action (as selected with dbcm.select.object.action()) is active according to the Object Configuration Management deployment.
syntax: function boolean dbcm.is.action.active ()
returns: true — The currently selected object action is active. false — In any other case.

name: dbcm.is.cm.active
doc: Tests whether Change Management is active for the given table (and optionally the company number), as defined in the Object Configuration Management deployment for the current package combination.
syntax: function boolean dbcm.is.cm.active (const string tbl.name$ [, long comp])
returns: true — In case Change Management is active for the given table (and company). false — In any other case.

name: dbcm.is.root.table
doc: Tests whether the given table is an Object Type root table, as defined in the Object Configuration Management model for the current package combination.
syntax: function boolean dbcm.is.root.table (const string tbl.name$)
returns: true — In case the given table is a root table. false — In any other case.

name: dbcm.object.check.out.is.being.undone
doc: Checks if the check-out of the specified object is being undone. That is, if the dbcm.undo.check.out.object() function is in progress.
syntax: function boolean dbcm.object.check.out.is.being.undone (const string toid$)
returns: true — The check-out is being undone. false — In any other case.

name: dbcm.object.is.being.checked.in
doc: Tests whether the business object identified by the specified Typed Object Id is being checked-in. This function can be used in DALs to decide whether or not to update related tables which do not belong to the currently selected Object Type. These tables may only be updated during check-in of the business object.
syntax: function boolean dbcm.object.is.being.checked.in (const string toid$)
returns: true — The business object is being checked-in. false — In any other case.

name: dbcm.object.is.checked.in
doc: Tests whether the business object identified by the specified Typed Object Id is checked-in.
syntax: function boolean dbcm.object.is.checked.in (const string toid$)
returns: true — The business object is checked-in. false — In any other case.

name: dbcm.object.is.checked.out
doc: Tests whether the business object identified by the specified Typed Object Id is checked-out.
syntax: function boolean dbcm.object.is.checked.out (const string toid$)
returns: true — The business object is checked-out. false — In any other case.

name: dbcm.object.remains.checked.in
doc: Tests whether the business object related to the current record buffer remains checked in.
syntax: function long dbcm.object.remains.checked.in (ref long tbl.id, long cmac, ref boolean b.eval)
returns: 0 — In case of success. <> 0 — In case an error occurred such as: table id is invalid, object could not be determined or CheckOutCondition could not be evaluated.

name: dbcm.read.object
doc: Reads and makes the business object current, based on the the given typed object id. In case the business object consists of multiple tables, the root table is accessed. When this function is finished the business object's properties can be accessed by means of the table fields of the root table.
syntax: function long dbcm.read.object (const string toid$ [, long comp])
returns: 0 — The database read was successful. An error occurred. cDbcm_UnknownTable (7) is returned in case no root table can be determined, or in case Change Management is not active for the root table. ENOREC (111) is returned in case no record can be found. <> 0

name: dbcm.reject
doc: Rejects any changes and/or actions done to the checked-out business object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id and sets the given reason for rejecting. This is possible for Pending objects (which will then become Rejected), and for objects having the status Recall Requested (which will then become Pending again). This function is typically used in the communication between ION Workflow and Infor LN when processing BODs.
syntax: function long dbcm.reject (const string toid$, const string reason$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. DBCM_INVALID_STATE (-1) — The object is in a state in which it is not allowed to perform a reject. A database error occurred. > 0

name: dbcm.select.checked.in.mode
doc: Sets the checked in mode Use this to ignore checked-out objects when querying and manipulating tables for which DBCM is active. This function is only meant for SPT libraries used by the Data Upgrade Engine.
syntax: function long dbcm.select.checked.in.mode (boolean value)
returns: 0 — In case of success. <> 0 — In case of an error; variable e contains the error code. See Database Change Management (DBCM) error codes for more information about the error codes and their meaning.

name: dbcm.select.object.action
doc: Selects the specified object action. The specified action is used to determine whether any changes made to the object require auto-check-in when these changes are submitted for Workflow approval. This works as follows: on.submit hook in the DAL of the object's root table. Typically, this hook will publish a Workflow BOD which is to be processed by ION Workflow. Only after the changes have been approved, the object will be checked-in. When it appears that the specified action is not active, submitting any changes will cause an immediate check-in of the object. In contrast to how dbcm.select.object.instance() works, a selected object action is not reset on return of a function.
syntax: function long dbcm.select.object.action (const string action.id$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. <> 0 — In case of an error; variable e contains the error code. See Database Change Management (DBCM) error codes for more information about the error codes and their meaning.

name: dbcm.select.object.instance
doc: Selects the specified Object instance. When a particular Object instance is selected, only that particular checked-out object is taken into account when the database is accessed. Other checked-out instances of the same Object Type or checked-out instances of other Object Types are not taken into account. dbcm.select.object.instance() is called. See the examples below for how this works.
syntax: function long dbcm.select.object.instance (const string toid$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. <> 0 — In case of an error; variable e contains the error code. See Database Change Management (DBCM) error codes for more information about the error codes and their meaning.

name: dbcm.select.object.type
doc: Selects the specified Object Type. When a particular Object Type is selected, checked-out objects of that type are taken into account, when the database is accessed. dbcm.select.object.type() is called. See the examples below for how this works.
syntax: function long dbcm.select.object.type (const string obj.type$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. <> 0 — In case of an error; variable e contains the error code. See Database Change Management (DBCM) error codes for more information about the error codes and their meaning.

name: dbcm.set.approved
doc: Assigns the Approval Received status to the checked-out Business Object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id. Afterwards the business object will be checked-in. This is only allowed for objects that have the Pending status. This function is typically used in the communication between ION Workflow and Infor LN when processing BODs.
syntax: function long dbcm.set.approved (const string toid$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. DBCM_INVALID_STATE (-1) — The object is in a state in which it is not allowed to perform this function. A database error occurred. > 0

name: dbcm.set.draft
doc: Assigns the Draft status to the checked-out Business Object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id. This is only allowed for objects that have the Approval Received or Rejected status. This function is typically used in the communication between ION Workflow and Infor LN when processing BODs.
syntax: function long dbcm.set.draft (const string toid$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. DBCM_INVALID_STATE (-1) — The object is in a state in which it is not allowed to perform this function. A database error occurred. > 0

name: dbcm.set.not.started
doc: Assigns the Not Started status to the checked-in Business Object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id and has the Approved status. This indicates that a previous request to recall the already started workflow process has been processed and acknowledged. This function is primarily intended for an object with the status Approved. However, it can also be called for an object with the status Not Applicable. In that case the function does change the status of the object but will still return value 0. This function is typically used in a UI-session.
syntax: function long dbcm.set.not.started (const string toid$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. DBCM_INVALID_STATE (-1) — The object is in a state in which it is not allowed to perform this function. A database error occurred. > 0

name: dbcm.set.object.type
doc: Sets the specified Object Type in a 4GL session. This function allows you to overrule the Object Type that would normally be selected when the session starts. Normally the Object Type that is returned by the function dbcm.get.type.name()) will be selected. Use this function only in the before.program section.
syntax: function long dbcm.set.object.type (const string obj.type$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. <> 0 — In case of an error; variable e contains the error code. See Database Change Management (DBCM) error codes for more information about the error codes and their meaning.

name: dbcm.set.rcd.toid
doc: Sets the given Typed Object ID in the (default) record buffer the given table.
syntax: function void dbcm.set.rcd.toid (long tbl.id, const string toid$)
returns: void

name: dbcm.set.recalled
doc: Assigns the Draft (Revision) status to the checked-out Business Object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id. This indicates that a previous request to recall the already started workflow process has been processed and acknowledged. This function should only be called in case the status of the object is Recall Requested. This function is typically used in the communication between ION Workflow and Infor LN when processing BODs.
syntax: function long dbcm.set.recalled (const string toid$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. DBCM_INVALID_STATE (-1) — The object is in a state in which it is not allowed to perform this function. A database error occurred. > 0

name: dbcm.set.submitted
doc: Sets the workflow instance id of the checked-out business object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id. This indicates that a previous submit has been confirmed and that the Workflow has been started. This function should only be called in case the status of the object is Pending. This function is typically used in the communication between ION Workflow and Infor LN when processing BODs.
syntax: function long dbcm.set.submitted (const string toid$, const string wf.id$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. DBCM_INVALID_STATE (-1) — The object is in a state in which it is not allowed to perform this function. A database error occurred. > 0

name: dbcm.set.workflow.definition
doc: Sets the workflow definition id of the checked-out business object that is identified by the given Typed Object Id. This id is a reference to a Workflow Process Definition in ION Workflow. On submit (and in case ION Workflow should be involved), an instance of this process will be started in ION Workflow. This function should only be called in case the status of the object is Draft, Draft (Revision), or Rejected. This function is typically used in the communication between ION Workflow and Infor LN when publishing BODs.
syntax: function long dbcm.set.workflow.definition (const string toid$, const string wf.def$)
returns: 0 — In case of success. DBCM_INVALID_STATE (-1) — The object is in a state in which it is not allowed to perform this function. A database error occurred. > 0

name: decompress.pixmap
doc: This converts a picture in .gif format to a colormap and pixmap. The long array returned by the colormap argument can subsequently be used as the DsNcolorTable attribute of a DsCcolormap object. The string array returned by the pixmap argument can subsequently be used as the DsNdata attribute for a DsCpixmap object.
syntax: function long decompress.pixmap (string buffer, ref long colormap, ref string pixmap)
returns: TRUE (<> 0): success FALSE (0): error

name: defaults.saved
doc: Determines if there are saved defaults for the current user/company/session combination.
syntax: function boolean defaults.saved ()
returns: FALSE user defaults not found TRUE user defaults found

name: del.window
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This deletes the specified window. When you delete the current window, the next window in the internal window stack becomes the current one. The screen is not refreshed automatically.
syntax: function void del.window (long wind_id)
returns: void

name: delch$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to delete num_expr characters, from the current cursor position to the right. The text following the deleted characters shifts num_expr positions to the left.
syntax: function string delch$ (long num_expr)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: delete.keyfields.collection
doc: Delete the indicated key fields collection including all key field objects which are currently stored in this collection
syntax: function void delete.keyfields.collection (long object)
returns: void

name: delete.keyfields.object
doc: Delete the indicated key fields object. When this object is currently part of a collection it will also be removed from this collection.
syntax: function void delete.keyfields.object (long object)
returns: void

name: deleteln$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to delete num_expr lines, from the current line down. Lines below the deleted ones are moved up.
syntax: function string deleteln$ (long num_expr)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: destroy.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This removes the specified object and all its children (if any).
syntax: function void destroy.object (long object_id)
returns: void

name: destroy.progress.indicator
doc: Destroys the progress indicator.
syntax: function void destroy.progress.indicator ()
returns: void

name: destroy.sub.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This removes the specified subobject.
syntax: function void destroy.sub.object (long object, long sub_object_id)
returns: void

name: destroy.tree
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This ends the Structure Chart Manager for the specified tree.
syntax: function void destroy.tree (string tree_name [, long process_id])
returns: void

name: dialog.add.button
doc: Creates a button on the dialog.
syntax: function long dialog.add.button (long dlg, const string btnFunction(), const string btnLabel)
returns: The id of the button. Negative value indicates an error.

name: dialog.add.chart
doc: Note that this function only effects the WebUI and LN UI User Interface. Add a chart to the indicated dialog. Chart data and other attributes must be set using other chart functions. The initial chart type is set with argument initial.type. The user can modify this type when the dialog is shown. Below an illustration of each supported type is given.
syntax: function long dialog.add.chart (long dlg, long initial.type [, long allowed.types])
returns: This function returns a chart id which must be used in further chart calls. In case of an error the value 0 is returned.

name: dialog.add.field
doc: This function creates a new field on the dialog.
syntax: function long dialog.add.field (long dlg, const string fldName(), const string fldLabel() [, long attribute, value,...])
returns: 0 — Success < 0 — The negative sequence number of the erroneous argument. E.g. a return value of -7 indicates an error in the 7th argument.

name: dialog.add.listbox
doc: This function creates a dynamic list box (not representing an enum domain) on the dialog. If there is an enum domain, use the function dialog.add.field().
syntax: function long dialog.add.listbox (long dlg, const string fldName(), const string fldLabel(), const long no.items, long enum.vals(), string enum.desc(,) [, string attribute, value,...])
returns: None.

name: dialog.add.text
doc: This function creates static texts on the dialog. Purpose of this text can be for explanation or additional help.
syntax: function long dialog.add.text (long dlg, string text() [, long attribute, value, ...])
returns: None.

name: dialog.new
doc: Creates a new dialog. dialog.name will be used for the title bar of the new dialog. Possible attributes are:
syntax: function long dialog.new (string dialogName [, long attribute, value, ...])
returns: The id of the created dialog. This id identifies the dialog in further dialog calls. It is the id of an XML tree that can be debugged during the whole process.

name: dialog.refresh.field
doc: Refreshes the value of a field. This function can be used in a button function if the value for a field has changed.
syntax: function long dialog.refresh.field (long dlg, const string fldName())
returns: 0 — OK -1 — The dialog doesn't exist -2 — The field doesn't exist.

name: dialog.show
doc: Displays the created dialog and start interaction with the user. This function returns when the user clicks the OK or Cancel button. Created dialogs can be used multiple times.
syntax: function long dialog.show (long dlg [, long previous_window] [, long load_defaults])
returns: END.PROGRAM — The user pressed the OK (or Finish) button 0 — The user pressed the Cancel button NEXT.FRM — The user pressed the Next button PREV.FRM — The user pressed the Back button

name: digest.finalize
doc: After the last data has been fed into the hash-algorithm using digest.update(), the digest.finalize function can be used to retrieve the resulting hash value.
syntax: function long digest.finalize (long handle, ref string result)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error. The specifics of the error are logged by the Bshell. The problem can be caused by the underlying OpenSSL function, a result string that is too small to hold the result or an invalid handle.

name: digest.initialize
doc: Initializes the state of the Secure Hash Algorithm and selects the apropriate Secure Hash algorithm. Note: the older DIGEST_SHA algorithm (also known as SHA-0) has been removed from the bshell version 9.1c, TIV 2140, as versions of OpenSSL starting with 1.1.0c do not support the SHA digest anymore. The SHA-0 algorithm has been considered insecure ever since 1995. If you use the DIGEST_SHA name, you will get a runtime error for compiled objects if this method is used and an intentional compilation error of 3GL objects when you try to compile a source containing it. You will have to alter your software to use one of the newer digest algorithms.
syntax: function long digest.initialize (long digest.type)
returns: A handle for this digest operation that must be used in subsequent calls to digest.update() and digest.finalize()). The value -1 is returned upon error. Details of the error are logged by the bshell. The returned Id can only be used in the original process where digest.initialize was called, and is useless in other processes in the same bshell. The allocated memory is freed explicitly by passing the Id to digest.finalize(). The allocated memory is freed implicitly when the process exits. Any number of Secure Digest Algorithm states may be in use concurrently.

name: digest.update
doc: Feeds data to the hash algorithm. This function can be called as many times as required to process the entire message. The third parameter can be used to explicitly specify the length of a binary string (when omitted, the logical length of the string argument is used). When all your data has been fed into the update routine, use digest.finalize()) to obtain the resulting hash value.
syntax: function long digest.update (long handle, string data, long data.size)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error. The specifics of the error are logged by the Bshell. The problem can be caused by the underlying OpenSSL function, an invalid buffer length (bigger than the actual length of string) or an invalid handle.

name: dir.close
doc: This closes a specified directory and frees all memory allocated to it. The dfd argument is the pointer to the directory returned by dir.open() or dir.open.tree() when the directory was opened.
syntax: function long dir.close (long dfd)
returns: >= 0 — Success. -1 — Error; The system dependent error value is put in the e variable.

name: dir.entry
doc: This retrieves entries from a previously opened directory. It retrieves the entries sequentially.
syntax: function string dir.entry (long dfd, long read_type [, ref long return_type] [, ref long filesize] [, ref long mode])
returns: The directory entry. Or an empty string if the end of the entry list has been reached.

name: dir.open
doc: This reads the specified directory into memory. The path argument can have a maximum length of 512 characters. The function returns a pointer ( dfd) to the directory data. dir.entry(), dir.rewind(), and dir.close() use this pointer to access the directory.
syntax: function long dir.open (const string path [, long read_type])
returns: > 0 — Success; A pointer to the directory data. <= 0 — Error; The negative error value may be system dependent.

name: dir.open.tree
doc: This is similar to dir.open() in that it reads a specified directory into memory. However, dir.open.tree() can retrieve up to 256 directory levels. The function returns a pointer ( dfd) to the directory data. dir.entry(), dir.rewind(), and dir.close() use this pointer to access the directory.
syntax: function long dir.open.tree (const string path [, long nlevels] [, long read_type])
returns: > 0 — Success; A pointer to the directory data. <= 0 — Error; The negative error value may be system dependent.

name: dir.rewind
doc: This resets the read pointer of the specified directory to the beginning of the directory entry list. The dfd argument is the pointer to the directory returned by dir.open() or dir.open.tree() when the directory was opened.
syntax: function long dir.rewind (long dfd)
returns: > 0 — Success; A pointer to the directory data. -1 — Error. Bad directory descriptor.

name: dir.select.dialog.local
doc: Deprecated. This shows the Windows Browse For Folder dialog, to allow the user to select one new or existing folder (directory) on the client.
syntax: function long dir.select.dialog.local (ref string dirname)
returns: 1 — A directory selected by the user 0 — No directory selected. Folder browser dialog canceled by the user. -1 — Error occurred

name: disable.checkmark
doc: This disables single-occurrence and multi-occurrence checkmarks on a form. Field will be displayed as checkbox after this function is applied. Because the information is not available, you can not use this function in the before.program section.
syntax: function void disable.checkmark (string field [,occurrence],...)
returns: void

name: disable.commands
doc: This disables the specified standard and/or form command(s). Standard commands are identified by their Standard commands. Form commands are identified either by a function name, a session code, or a menu code.
syntax: function void disable.commands (const string command, const string ...)
returns: void

name: disable.db.dll
doc: This disables the call of the db hooks in the db dll. (db.before.insert, db.before.update, db.before.delete, db.after.insert, db.after.update, db.after.delete)
syntax: function void disable.db.dll ()
returns: void

name: disable.fields
doc: This disables single-occurrence and multi-occurrence fields on a form. To disable all fields of a group, see disable.group(). Because the information is not available, you cannot use this function in the before.program or after.form.read section.
syntax: function void disable.fields ( [long mode], string field [,occurrence],...)
returns: void

name: disable.group
doc: This disables all the fields of the specified (dynamic) group. See disable.fields(). There is a second, optional, argument that can have two possible values: DISABLE — The default mode, it does not need to be specified. READONLY — In this mode the fields become read-only and cannot be edited by the user. This function is relevant to dynamic forms only.
syntax: function void disable.group (long group.nr [, long type] [, long occurrence])
returns: void

name: disable.pagemode
doc: This disables pagemode for this session, even when the user runs in pagemode.
syntax: function void disable.pagemode ()
returns: void

name: disable.personalize.view
doc: This disables the personalize view option.
syntax: function void disable.personalize.view ()
returns: void

name: disable.quick.flow
doc: This function can be used in e.g. the after.choice of choice.mark.occur to disable the quick.flow for one or more form commands. In this way the application script can decide to disable quick.flow based on values in the marked record.
syntax: function void disable.quick.flow (const string frmcmd, const string ...)
returns: void

name: disable.satellite
doc: This disables the specified satellite. The TAB on which the satellite is shown will become disabled. When this TAB is currently active, another TAB will be selected. Initially all satellite TAB buttons are enabled. This function is relevant in multi-main table controller sessions only.
syntax: function void disable.satellite (const string session.code)
returns: void

name: disable.table.extension
doc: This macro will disable the calling of ue hooks and table extension hooks. The actual state of the enabling is saved and will be used during enable.table.extension()
syntax: function void disable.table.extension ()
returns: void

name: disable.ue.dll
doc: This macro will disable the calling of ue hooks and table extension hooks. The actual state of the enabling is saved and will be used during enable.ue.dll
syntax: function void disable.ue.dll ()
returns: void

name: disable.zoom.buttons
doc: This disables single-occurrence and multi-occurrence zoom buttons on a form. This function can not be used in the before.program section. The zoom button will only get disabled if the field is enabled. The state of the zoom button can only be changed if the field is enabled.
syntax: function void disable.zoom.buttons (string field [,occurrence],...)
returns: void

name: discard.changed.image
doc: This function will discard an image which was possibly dropped on an image control and discard the saved backup image after a delete. This function is usually called from the after.choice section of choice: recover.set.
syntax: function void discard.changed.image (string fieldname)
returns: void

name: display
doc: Use this function to display a specified field on a form. Usually, the 4GL engine displays fields automatically, either when the form is opened or when data in a related input field is changed. However, there are situations when you need to use these functions to display fields. For example, to display stand-alone fields, to display fields that are not in the input field TAB sequence, or to send data to the form during batch processes. display() — Displays a single-occurrence field. You cannot use this to display a field for all occurrences.
syntax: function void display (string field)
returns: void

name: display.all
doc: Use this function to display all fields on a form. Usually, the 4GL engine displays fields automatically, either when the form is opened or when data in a related input field is changed. However, there are situations when you need to use these functions to display fields. For example, to display fields that are not in the input field TAB sequence, or to send data to the form during batch processes. display.all() — Displays all fields of all occurrences.
syntax: function void display.all ()
returns: void

name: display.curr.occ
doc: Use this function to display all fields of the current occurrence on a form. Usually, the 4GL engine displays fields automatically, either when the form is opened or when data in a related input field is changed. However, there are situations when you need to use these functions to display fields. For example, to display fields that are not in the input field TAB sequence, or to send data to the form during batch processes. display.curr.occ() — Displays all fields of the current occurrence.
syntax: function void display.curr.occ ()
returns: void

name: display.fld
doc: Use this function to display a specified field of a specific occurrence on a form. Usually, the 4GL engine displays fields automatically, either when the form is opened or when data in a related input field is changed. However, there are situations when you need to use these functions to display fields. For example, to display stand-alone fields, to display fields that are not in the input field TAB sequence, or to send data to the form during batch processes. Displays a specified field of a specified occurrence. To display a field for all occurrences, use the following construction: for i= 1 to filled.occ display.fld( i, field ) endfor display.fld()
syntax: function void display.fld (long occurrence, string field)
returns: void

name: display.occ
doc: Use this function to display the fields of a specific occurrence on a form. Usually, the 4GL engine displays fields automatically, either when the form is opened or when data in a related input field is changed. However, there are situations when you need to use these functions to display fields. For example, to display fields that are not in the input field TAB sequence, or to send data to the form during batch processes. display.occ() — Displays all fields of a specified occurrence.
syntax: function void display.occ (long occurrence)
returns: void

name: display.total.fields
doc: When a total line is included in a form, this function displays total values for specified fields in the grid. The function takes one or more pairs of arguments. In each pair, the first argument is the field name; the second argument is the total value for that field. The fields must be defined on the form as multioccurrence form fields. They must also be declared in the UI script. Alternately, the fields can be table fields. To add a total line to a grid, add the following code to the UI script: before.program: fattr.total.line = true Preferably call this function from the program section on.display.total.line. Alternatively for every update that effects the total fields, call display.total.fields() to display the new totals. The total line can display an enum value. To do this, the description of the enum must be passed using enum.descr$(). For example: display.total.fields( "tffbs.dbcr", enum.descr$( "tfgld.dbcr", tfgld.dbcr.debit ) )
syntax: function void display.total.fields (string fieldname1, void value1, string fieldname2,..., void value2,...)
returns: void

name: do.all.occ
doc: This executes the specified function for all occurrences on the current form. When included in the before.choice subsection of a choice.update.db section, the function is executed only for occurrences that are pending to be saved. If the update.status has not yet been set, then do.all.occ() will first lock all records. After the function has been executed for all occurrences, all fields of all occurrences are redisplayed.
syntax: function void do.all.occ (function_name function_name, function_name ...)
returns: void

name: do.occ
doc: This locks the specified occurrence (delayed lock) and executes the specified function for that occurrence. After the function has been executed all fields of the specified occurrence are redisplayed.
syntax: function void do.occ (long occurrence, function_name function_name, function_name ...)
returns: void

name: do.occ.without.update
doc: This executes the specified function for a specified occurrence, without any locking or update actions. After the function has been executed all fields of the specified occurrence are redisplayed.
syntax: function long do.occ.without.update (long occurrence, function_name function_name, function_name ...)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: do.parent.selection
doc: This function can be used to process records selected in a parent session. For example: in a print session only print the records that are selected in the parent. If updating the records is needed, then this should be done in the function "function_name". The function "function_name" is executed once for each marked record in the parent. At the moment the function is called, the primary keyfields of the marked records will be restored. If the function returns a value not equal to 0, then no more records are selected and do.parent.selection returns.
syntax: function void do.parent.selection (long function_name [, ...])
returns: void

name: do.selection
doc: This executes the specified function for all marked occurrences. Depending on the mode parameter, this executes either do.occ() or do.occ.without.update() on the currently marked records.
syntax: function void do.selection (long mode, function_name function_name [, function_name ...])
returns: void

name: domainof
doc: This compile time function returns the name of the domain of the supplied variable.
syntax: function string domainof (string variable)
returns: The name of the domain of the supplied variable.

name: double.cmp
doc: See syntax: function long double.cmp (double double1, double double2, double tolerance)
syntax: function long double.cmp (double double1, double double2, double tolerance)
returns: 0 the difference between the doubles is less than the tolerance. -1 double1 is less than double2 (the difference is greater than the tolerance). 1 double1 is greater than or equal to double2 (the difference is greater than the tolerance).

name: DsCbarMenu
doc: A DsCbarMenu object defines a menu bar and associated drop-down and cascaded menus. The menu bar is displayed across the top of a main window (DsCmwindow), below the title bar. An application creates the entire menu with a single create.object() call. Subsequently, it can use change.object() toadd, remove, change, enable, and disable menu items. Remember to specify the identification number of the DsCbarMenu object in the DsNbarMenu attribute of the parent window.
syntax: object type DsCbarMenu
returns: n/a (UI object type; use with create.object / change.object)

name: DsCcheckBox
doc: A check box represents a choice that has two states (selected or not selected). It appears as a square box with an accompanying label. When the choice is selected, a check mark appears in the box. When the choice is not selected, the box is empty. Users can toggle a check box on and off with the mouse or keyboard keys. Check boxes are typically used in a group to provide a multiple-choice field. Within a group, they represent independent choices that are not mutually exclusive.
syntax: object type DsCcheckBox
returns: n/a (UI object type; use with create.object / change.object)

name: DsCcolorCell
doc: A color cell is a rectangular child window that displays a color. If possible, a color cell uses only one palette entry and so saves resources. Otherwise, the number of colors used increases with every change.
syntax: object type DsCcolorCell
returns: n/a (UI object type; use with create.object / change.object)

name: DsCcolormap
