name: get.arg.type
doc: This function returns the type of the specified argument.
syntax: function long get.arg.type (long arg_no)
returns: The function can return any of the following values: VAR.TYPE.LONG — The specified argument is of type long or boolean. VAR.TYPE.DOUBLE — The specified argument is of type double. VAR.TYPE.STRING — The specified argument is of type string. VAR.TYPE.MULTIBYTE — The specified argument is of type multi-byte string. VAR.TYPE.UNKNOWN — arg_no is out of range, or the specified argument is not of one of the allowed types. For historic reasons, these values are defined in terms of other named constants. The definitions are available when the tiv level is at least 2010 or when USE_VAR_TYPE_DEFINES is defined to a non-zero value. #if ES_TIV_LEVEL >= 2010 or USE_VAR_TYPE_DEFINES #define VAR.TYPE.LONG DB.LONG #define VAR.TYPE.DOUBLE DB.DOUBLE #define VAR.TYPE.STRING DB.STRING #define VAR.TYPE.MULTIBYTE DB.MULTIBYTE #define VAR.TYPE.UNKNOWN (-1) #endif

name: get.argc
doc: This function returns the number of arguments supplied to the currently executing function (i.e. the function in which get.argc() is called). Once you know this number, you can read from and write to particular arguments using the other functions.
syntax: function long get.argc ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: get.bi.server.location
doc: This function returns the location of the BI Server linked to the current package combination. If the current package combination has no specific BI server linked to it, the function returns the BI server that is not linked to any package combination.
syntax: function string get.bi.server.location ()
returns: filled — URL of the BI Server. empty — If BI Server not configured.

name: get.boolean.arg
doc: The function get.boolean.arg() returns the value of the specified argument, converted to a boolean.
syntax: function boolean get.boolean.arg (long arg_no)
returns: The value of the specified argument, converted to a boolean. Implicit conversion of the value of the specified argument from its original type to type boolean is performed. If arg_no is out of range, the value false is returned.

name: get.bw.hostname
doc: This returns the hostname of the bw client (if available)
syntax: function long get.bw.hostname (ref string hostname)
returns: 1 (TRUE) Function succeeded, hostname is filled 0 (FALSE) Function failed, hostname is unchanged

name: get.bw.ip.address
doc: This returns the ip-address of the system of the BW, WebUI or LN UI client (if available)
syntax: function string get.bw.ip.address ()
returns: Return value Function succeeded, return value is the requested ip-address Empty string Information is not available

name: get.bw.username
doc: This returns the Windows username of the user that started the BW client
syntax: function long get.bw.username (ref string username)
returns: 1 (TRUE) Function succeeded, username is filled 0 (FALSE) Function failed, username is unchanged

name: get.client.directory
doc: Deprecated. This function returns the folder, on the local client, related to a given id. In case of Baan Windows this is the folder that is defined by the ${id} environment variable on the local client. In case of WebUI, this is a folder, on the client machine on which the Internet Browser is running, related to the id.
syntax: function string get.client.directory (const string id)
returns: The folder related to the given id. In case of Baan Windows, the return value contains the value of the ${BSE_TMP} client environment variable. In case of WebUI, the return value contains the name of the default temporary folder on the client machine. The return value is empty when an id is used for which no folder was defined.

name: get.client.hostname
doc: This returns the hostname of the local client (if available). In case of Baan Windows this is the client machine on which BW is running. In case of WebUI, this is the client machine on which the Internet Browser is running.
syntax: function long get.client.hostname (ref string hostname)
returns: true — Function succeeded, hostname is filled. false — Function failed, client hostname is unknown.

name: get.client.ip.address
doc: Get the IP address of the local client. In case of Baan Windows this is the client machine on which BW is running. In case of WebUI, this is the client machine on which the Internet Browser is running
syntax: function long get.client.ip.address (ref string ip.address)
returns: true — Function succeeded, IP adress is filled. false — Function failed, client IP address is unknown.

name: get.client.timezone
doc: This returns the current Windows Timezone name of the local client (if available). In case of LN UI the local client is not accessible. For backward compatibility the timezone of the back-end user is converted to the Windows Timezone. In case of Baan Windows this is the client machine on which BW is running. In case of WebUI, this is the client machine on which the Internet Browser is running when running on a Windows system. When the WebUI runs on a non-Windows operating system an empty string is returned. The following time-zones are not supported by Microsoft: These time-zones are matched with a near known time-zone. The conversion can be found in timezone table (session ttaad0160m000).
syntax: function string get.client.timezone ()
returns: The current Windows Timezone name of the client. The maximum length is 32 characters.

name: get.col
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This retrieves the number of the column where the cursor is currently positioned. The function uses get.cp(), so it is slower than that function.
syntax: function long get.col ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: get.company
doc: This returns the name of the current company.
syntax: function string get.company ()
returns: This returns the name of the current company.

name: get.compnr
doc: This returns the ID number of the current company.
syntax: function long get.compnr ()
returns: This returns the ID number of the current company.

name: get.cp
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This stores the coordinates of the current cursor position in the x and y arguments.
syntax: function void get.cp (ref long x, ref long y)
returns: void

name: get.current.field.label
doc: This retrieves the current label text associated with the specified field. The function is relevant to dynamic forms only. The current label can only differ from the initial label if the function change.field.label() has been used.
syntax: function long get.current.field.label (const string fname, long element, ref string label1 to label3)
returns: &0 label of field found -1 session is not dynamic -2 field not found

name: get.display.data
doc: This retrieves information about the display server. It stores the information in the array server_data. The predefined constant SRVMAXSIZE indicates the maximum size of the array. You can retrieve the information using a set of predefined variables: Information — Variable typesrv.type(server_data) DSNOSERVER DSBX DSBA DSBW Server type Display width — srv.display.width(server_data) Display height — srv.display.height(server_data) Display width in millimeters — srv.display.width.mm(server_data) Display height in millimeters — srv.display.height.mm(server_data) Number of colors — srv.display.colors(server_data) srv.display.os.type(server_data) DSBW_WIN_311 DSBW_WIN_NT DSBW_WIN_95 NT4 Microsoft operating system
syntax: function long get.display.data (ref long server_data(SRVMAXSIZE))
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: get.double.arg
doc: The function get.double.arg() returns the value of the specified argument, converted to a double.
syntax: function double get.double.arg (long arg_no)
returns: The value of the specified argument, converted to a double. Implicit conversion of the value of the specified argument from its original type to type double is performed. If arg_no is out of range, the value 0.0 is returned.

name: get.field.label
doc: This retrieves the label text associated with the specified field. The function is relevant to dynamic forms only. NOTE: For historical reasons this function sometimes returns the initial label, and sometimes the current label (as changed using change.field.label()). The initial label is returned for grid fields, and the current label is returned for non-grid-fields. Therefore this function is deprecated. Please use get.initial.field.label() or get.current.field.label() instead.
syntax: function long get.field.label (const string fname, long element, ref string label1 to label3)
returns: &0 label of field found -1 session is not dynamic -2 field not found

name: get.financial.compnr
doc: This returns the ID number of the current financial company.
syntax: function long get.financial.compnr ()
returns: This returns the ID number of the current financial company.

name: get.first.keyfields.object
doc: Get the first key fields object in this collection.
syntax: function long get.first.keyfields.object (long object)
returns: <> 0 — The id of the first key fields object 0 — When this collection does not contain any objects

name: get.image.path
doc: This function will get the full path for an image.
syntax: function string get.image.path (string guid, long sequ [, string tablename] [, long width] [, long height])
returns: The path for the requested image, empty string if the requested image cannot be found.

name: get.indexed.var
doc: This retrieves the value of the specified variable. It is the same as get.var() except that it enables retrieval of individual array elements.
syntax: function [long] get.indexed.var (long processno, string variable_name, ref void destination, long dim1 [, dim2, dim3, dim4 ])
returns: 0 — success 1 — general error 2 — incorrect number of dimensions 3 — variable not found 4 — array element not available

name: get.initial.field.label
doc: This retrieves the initial label text associated with the specified field. The function is relevant to dynamic forms only.
syntax: function long get.initial.field.label (const string fname, long element, ref string label1 to label3)
returns: &0 label of field found -1 session is not dynamic -2 field not found

name: get.keyfields.table
doc: Return the name of the table associated with the passed key fields object.
syntax: function string get.keyfields.table (long object)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: get.local.filename
doc: Deprecated. This function returns the last client filename used by the function server2client() or client2server(). When the last server2client() or client2server() function failed, this function will return an empty string.
syntax: function string get.local.filename ()
returns: The client filename or an empty string

name: get.logistic.compnr
doc: This returns the ID number of the current logistic company.
syntax: function long get.logistic.compnr ()
returns: This returns the ID number of the current logistic company.

name: get.long.arg
doc: The function get.long.arg() returns the value of the specified argument, converted to a long.
syntax: function long get.long.arg (long arg_no)
returns: The value of the specified argument, converted to a long. Implicit conversion of the value of the specified argument from its original type to type long is performed. If arg_no is out of range, the value 0 is returned.

name: get.long.byte.count
doc: This function returns the value BitCountOfLong/8, that is the amount of bytes used to store a variable of type long.
syntax: function long get.long.byte.count ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: get.next.keyfields.object
doc: Get the next key fields object in a collection.
syntax: function long get.next.keyfields.object (long object)
returns: <> 0 — The id of the next key fields object 0 — When this collection does not contain more objects

name: get.num.keyfields.object
doc: Get the number of key field objects in this collection.
syntax: function long get.num.keyfields.object (long object)
returns: >= 0 — the number of child nodes. < 0 — when an invalid collection id is passed

name: get.numformat.symbols
doc: Determine which decimal sign and thousand separator are currently being used.
syntax: function long get.numformat.symbols (ref string decimal$, ref string grouping$)
returns: 0 — The returned decimal sign and thousand separator have the original, user defined, values. 1 — The returned decimal sign and thousand separator have been set with the function set.numformat.symbols()

name: get.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This retrieves information about a specified object.
syntax: function long get.object (long object_id, long attribute, void value, long size)
returns: TRUE success FALSE error

name: get.os.user
doc: Retrieves the current OS user of the bshell
syntax: function string get.os.user ()
returns: Success returns the name of the OS user Error An empty string is returned

name: get.pgrp
doc: This returns the identification number of the process group to which the specified process belongs. If you specify an unknown process ID, -1 is returned.
syntax: function long get.pgrp (long process_id)
returns: This returns the identification number of the process group to which the specified process belongs.

name: get.pixmap.info
doc: This retrieves information about a picture, in .gif format, that has been read with the seq.read() function. It returns the number of colors in the picture and the picture's width and height. When a picture is used in an object, the width and height values are necessary for determining the amount of memory that must be allocated for the picture.
syntax: function long get.pixmap.info (ref string buffer, ref long num_colors, ref long width, ref long height)
returns: TRUE success FALSE error

name: get.prev.value
doc: This function retrieves the field's previous value. The previous value is converted to the type of the output parameter. This function only works on the current field
syntax: function boolean get.prev.value (long value)
returns: true when successful, otherwise false.

name: get.resource$
doc: This function returns the value associated with the given bshell resource of the current user. Resources are specified in the u<user> file in the '$BSE/lib/user' directory, but also in the files '$BSE/lib/defaults/<logical_name_of_bshell>' and '$BSE/lib/defaults/all'. The logical name of the bshell is the name you specify for the Bshell in BW. A string containing the resource value will be returned. If the resource can't be found, an empty string will be returned (please note that an existing resource may also be empty!).
syntax: function string get.resource$ (string resource_name)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: get.row
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This retrieves the number of the row where the cursor is currently positioned. The function uses get.cp(), so it is slower than that function.
syntax: function long get.row ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: get.screen.defaults
doc: The save.defaults standard command enables users to save the current field values of a session as the default values for that session. The get.screen.defaults() function displays the default values for all fields on all forms of the current session. It is often used at the start of update or print programs, where the user must specify some parameters before executing the session. If no user defaults are defined, set.fields.default() is executed automatically.
syntax: function void get.screen.defaults ()
returns: void

name: get.session.permission
doc: Retrieves the permission of the session ( session) in a bit pattern (see return values). Each of the listed 'return values' represents one bit. Multiple values can be bitwise OR-ed into one pattern and returned by the function. In cases of internal errors in the function, the value SESSION_NO_PERMISSION will be returned.
syntax: function long get.session.permission (string session(13))
returns: SESSION_NO_PERMISSION SESSION_DELETE_PERMISSION SESSION_INSERT_PERMISSION SESSION_MODIFY_PERMISSION SESSION_DISPLAY_PERMISSION SESSION_PRINT_PERMISSION

name: get.size.in.bytes
doc: This function returns the number of bytes available for the specified variable. NOTE: This function only works for non-array variables.
syntax: function long get.size.in.bytes (void var)
returns: When var is a string, the number of bytes available for the caller is returned. When var is a long or a double, the underlying size of the object is returned. For example, for a 64-bit long 8 is returned, for a 32-bit long 4. When var is an array, -1 is returned. When var is an empty based string, the value 0 is returned.

name: get.string.arg
doc: The function get.string.arg() returns the value of the specified argument, converted to a string.
syntax: function string get.string.arg (long arg_no)
returns: The value of the specified argument, converted to a string. Implicit conversion of the value of the specified argument from its original type to type string is performed. If arg_no is out of range, the empty string is returned.

name: get.sub.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This retrieves information about a specified subobject.
syntax: function long get.sub.object (long object, long sub_object_id [, long attribute] [, ref void value] [, ref long size])
returns: TRUE success FALSE error

name: get.tenant.id
doc: Returns the tenant id of the tenant under which the user is logged in. If the user is not logged in under a tenant then id "infor" is returned.
syntax: function string get.tenant.id ()
returns: String containing tenant id — The tenant id of the tenant under which the user is logged in infor — The user is not logged in under a tenant

name: get.time.zone
doc: Returns the current time zone. The program must supply a buffer of at least a size of 50 to store the result, otherwise the result is truncated.
syntax: function long get.time.zone (ref string time_zone())
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error.

name: get.tree.default
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. When the client receives a bucket message that cannot be retrieved with get.tree.node.press(), get.tree.node.dpress() or get.tree.push.button(), call this function to remove the bucket message from the internal stack.
syntax: function void get.tree.default ()
returns: void

name: get.tree.node.dpress
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this function to retrieve data from the Structure Chart Manager after an EVTBUCKETMESSAGE-type event, with a MSG.NODE.DPRESS command, has been received.
syntax: function void get.tree.node.dpress (ref long event, ref long process_id, ref string node_id)
returns: void

name: get.tree.node.press
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this function to retrieve data from the Structure Chart Manager after an EVTBUCKETMESSAGE-type event, with a MSG.NODE.PRESS command, has been received.
syntax: function void get.tree.node.press (ref long event, ref long process_id, ref string node_id)
returns: void

name: get.tree.push.button
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this function to retrieve data from the Structure Chart Manager after an EVTBUCKETMESSAGE-type event, with a MSG.PUSH.BUTTON command, has been received.
syntax: function void get.tree.push.button (ref long event, ref long process_id, ref string button_id, ref string node_id)
returns: void

name: get.ui.mode
doc: This returns a long value that indicates the UI mode in which this session is running. The possible values are: NO_UI — without a User Interface BW_UI — UI is bw client WEBUI_CLASSIC — UI is thin-client in classic mode WEBUI_COMMONUI — UI is thin-client in commonUI mode HTML_UI — UI is thin-client running in HTMLUI mode (LN UI) SOHO_XI — UI is thin-client running in SoHo Xi mode
syntax: function long get.ui.mode ()
returns: This returns a long value that indicates the UI mode in which this session is running.

name: get.user.default
doc: Returns the default value for the passed sessioncode, field combination. The default is retrieved using the current user and current company.
syntax: function boolean get.user.default (const string session.code, const string field, ref string field.value)
returns: FALSE default not found TRUE default found

name: get.utc.byte.count
doc: This function returns the value ByteCountOfUtc, that is the amount of bytes used when a UTC long format value is stored in or retrieved from a sequence of bytes.
syntax: function long get.utc.byte.count ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: get.var
doc: This retrieves the value of the specified variable. The variable can be a single variable of any type or an array.
syntax: function [long] get.var (long processno, string variable_name, ref void destination)
returns: 0 — error; probably variable not found 1 — success

name: get.window.attrs
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This stores attributes of the specified window in the attrs array. The maximum number of attributes that can be retrieved is indicated by the predefined constant WINMAXSIZE. You can retrieve the attributes with the following predefined variables: win.parent( attrs ) — window ID of parent window win.x( attrs ) — x-position of window win.y( attrs ) — y-position of window win.width( attrs ) — width of window win.height( attrs ) — height of window win.border.width( attrs ) — border width of window (gwindow only) win.background( attrs ) — background color of window win.event.mask( attrs ) — mask indicating the events generated by the window
syntax: function long get.window.attrs (long wind_id, ref long attrs(WINMAXSIZE))
returns: TRUE — Success. FALSE — Error.

name: get_function
doc: This loads a specified function from a previously loaded DLL. It returns an identification number for the function.
syntax: function long get_function (long dll_id, string funct_name)
returns: > 0 — Function identifier. 0 — Error; Function not found or DLL not loaded.

name: getcwd
doc: c:/baan/bin ).
syntax: function string getcwd ()
returns: The current path as a string. Or an empty string if an error occurs.

name: getenv$
doc: This returns the value of a specified environment variable of the operating system. It returns an empty string if the variable is not available.
syntax: function string getenv$ (string env_var)
returns: This returns the value of a specified environment variable of the operating system.

name: grab.mwindow
doc: This specifies the process group to which a particular main window must send its events. After calling this function, all events that occur in the main window are sent to the process group. grab.mwindow() is mainly used immediately after creation of a new process group.
syntax: function void grab.mwindow (long mwindow, long process_group)
returns: void

name: green.component
doc: These return the values of the blue, green, and red components respectively of an rgb color.
syntax: function long blue.component (long color)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: group.exists
doc: This checks whether a specified group is defined on the system. Whether group names are case-sensitive or case-insensitive is a system-dependent feature.
syntax: function boolean group.exists (const string groupname)
returns: TRUE group exists FALSE group does not exist

name: group.invisible
doc: This hides the specified group completely, including all associated fields, labels, and subgroups. The group.nr argument specifies the group number, as defined in the form editor. The group cannot be made visible again. This function is relevant to dynamic forms only and can be used only in the before.program and in the after.form.read section of 4GL scripts.
syntax: function void group.invisible (long group.nr)
returns: void

name: halfadj
doc: This rounds a given value to a specified number of decimal places.
syntax: function double halfadj (double value, long diga)
returns: The rounded value. Or the original value ( value) if an error occurs. Because the return value is of type double, the number of digits after the decimal sign is always 6. For example, halfadj(1.345, 2) returns 1.350000. The function is identical to round( value, diga, 1)

name: hex2bytes
doc: Converts a string of hexadecimal characters to bytes.
syntax: function long hex2bytes (const string hex, ref string bytes)
returns: >= 0: the number of bytes stored in parameter 'bytes' -1: in case of an invalid hex string

name: hide.selection.column
doc: This hides the selection column in thin-client sessions completely.
syntax: function void hide.selection.column ()
returns: void

name: hmac.hash
doc: Calculates a keyed-hash message authentication code (HMAC) using a cryptographic hash function in combination with a secret cryptographic key. The cryptographic strength of the HMAC depends upon the cryptographic strength of the underlying hash function, the size of its hash output, and on the size and quality of the key. The hash is returned in 'raw hex' format; depending on the specified hash type, this is a string of max 128 bytes. The following cryptographic hash functions are supported:
syntax: function long hmac.hash (long type, const string key, long keysize, const string data, long size, ref string hash)
returns: >= 0 — the number of hex characters copied into 'hash'; this is at max 128 < 0 — in case of an error

name: hostname$
doc: This returns the hostname of the local machine. If no hostname is found, the function returns an empty string.
syntax: function string hostname$ ( [boolean getcanonicalname])
returns: This returns the hostname of the local machine.

name: http.connect
doc: Sends a CONNECT HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.connect (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.cookie.delete
doc: Deletes an http.cookie object. If the http.cookie object is part of an http.cookiejar object, it is removed from the cookiejar as well.
syntax: function void http.cookie.delete (long cookie)
returns: void

name: http.cookie.domain
doc: Returns the cookie domain of an http.cookie object. The cookie domain is a value like "www.infor.com" (in which case subdomains is false) or ".infor.com" (in which case subdomains is true).
syntax: function string http.cookie.domain (long cookie)
returns: the cookie domain

name: http.cookie.expires
doc: Returns when the cookie expires as a UTC date/time. A value of 0 indicates this is a session cookie.
syntax: function long http.cookie.expires (long cookie)
returns: > 0 — a UTC date/time indicating when the cookie expires 0 — the cookie is a session cookie

name: http.cookie.httponly
doc: Returns whether an http.cookie object only applies to a HTTP (and not to other protocols, like FTP). Although this attribute has no meaning for the HTTP Client, it is still retained, so that when the cookie is part of an http.cookiejar object, and the cookiejar is saved to a file, this attribute is stored in the file as well.
syntax: function boolean http.cookie.httponly (long cookie)
returns: true if the cookie appies to HTTP only, else false

name: http.cookie.name
doc: Returns the cookie name of an http.cookie object.
syntax: function string http.cookie.name (long cookie)
returns: the cookie name

name: http.cookie.new
doc: Constructs a new http.cookie object. Use the attributes as specified below to configure the cookie. Example: long cookie cookie = http.cookie.new( HTTP_COOKIE_NAME, "SID", HTTP_COOKIE_VALUE, "1234abcd", HTTP_COOKIE_DOMAIN, ".infor.com", HTTP_COOKIE_PATH, "/api", HTTP_COOKIE_SECURE, true, HTTP_COOKIE_HTTPONLY, true, HTTP_EXPIRES, 0) |* 0 = session cookie
syntax: function long http.cookie.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.cookie object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.cookie.next
doc: Returns an http.cookie object's next http.cookie object. This can be used to traverse http.cookie objects in an http.cookiejar object. Example: long cookiejar long cookie |* assume cookiejar refers to a filled http.cookiejar object |* get the first cookie from the cookiejar cookie = http.cookiejar.first(cookiejar) while cookie <> 0 |* handle cookie here ... |* get next cookie cookie = http.cookie.next(cookie) endwhile
syntax: function long http.cookie.next (long cookie)
returns: the next http.cookie object, or 0 if there is no next http.cookie object

name: http.cookie.parse
doc: Parses a cookie string and constructs a new http.cookie object based on it. The cookie string can be in Netscape format or in Set-Cookie format. A Netscape formatted cookie string consist of 7 parts, separated by tabs: See https://curl.se/docs/http-cookies.html for more info. Notes A Set-Cookie cookie string consists of a name=value pair with 0 or more attributes, separated by ';'. The following attributes are recognized (others are silently ignored): See https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc6265.txt for more info. Notes
syntax: function long http.cookie.parse (const string format, const string cookie_string)
returns: a new http.cookie object, or 0 in case the specified cookie string could not be parsed

name: http.cookie.path
doc: Returns the cookie path of an http.cookie object.
syntax: function string http.cookie.path (long cookie)
returns: the cookie path

name: http.cookie.secure
doc: Returns whether an http.cookie object only applies to secure connections (like https).
syntax: function boolean http.cookie.secure (long cookie)
returns: true if the cookie applies to secure connections only, else false

name: http.cookie.subdomains
doc: Returns whether an http.cookie object only applies to a single host or multiple hosts in the domain. If the domain does not start with a dot (e.g. www.example.com), the subdomains flag is false. If the domain starts with a dot (e.g. .example.com), the subdomains flag is true.
syntax: function boolean http.cookie.subdomains (long cookie)
returns: true if the cookie applies to subdomains, else false

name: http.cookie.to_string
doc: Returns a cookie string in Netscape format or Set-Cookie format. A Netscape formatted cookie string consist of 7 parts, separated by tabs: See https://curl.se/docs/http-cookies.html for more info. A Set-Cookie cookie string consists of a name=value pair with 0 or more attributes, separated by ';': See https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc6265.txt for more info.
syntax: function string http.cookie.to_string (long cookie, const string format)
returns: a cookie string in the requested format

name: http.cookie.value
doc: Returns the cookie value of an http.cookie object.
syntax: function string http.cookie.value (long cookie)
returns: the cookie value

name: http.cookiejar.add
doc: Adds an http.cookie object to an http.cookiejar object.
syntax: function void http.cookiejar.add (long cookiejar, long cookie)
returns: void

name: http.cookiejar.delete
doc: Deletes an http.cookiejar object. All contained http.cookie objects are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.cookiejar.delete (long cookiejar)
returns: void

name: http.cookiejar.first
doc: Returns the first http.cookie object of an http.cookiejar. This can be used to iterate all cookies in the cookiejar. Example: long cookiejar long cookie |* assume cookiejar refers to a filled http.cookiejar object |* get the first cookie from the cookiejar cookie = http.cookiejar.first(cookiejar) while cookie <> 0 |* handle cookie here ... |* get next cookie cookie = http.cookie.next(cookie) endwhile
syntax: function long http.cookiejar.first (long cookiejar)
returns: the first http.cookie object in the cookiejar, or 0 if the cookiejar is empty

name: http.cookiejar.load
doc: Fills an http.cookiejar object with the cookies stored in the specified file. If no http.cookiejar object is specified, one is created. If an existing http.cookiejar object is specified it is cleared before loading from the specified file. The file is expected to have the cookies stored in Netscape format, in which each cookie is a line consisting of the following 7 parts, separated by tabs: See https://curl.se/docs/http-cookies.html for more info. Notes
syntax: function long http.cookiejar.load (ref long cookiejar, const string file)
returns: 0 — success <> 0 — an I/O error, like ENOENT

name: http.cookiejar.new
doc: Creates a new empty http.cookiejar object. This can be used to keep track of cookies when doing multiple requests. When passed to a http.get(), http.post() etc. call as the value of the HTTP_COOKIEJAR attribute, any applicable cookies from the cookiejar are sent to the server, and when the response is received, the cookiejar is updated with any received cookies from the server.
syntax: function long http.cookiejar.new ()
returns: a new http.cookiejar object

name: http.cookiejar.save
doc: Saves the contents of an http.cookiejar object in a file. The contents of this file is overwritten. The cookies are stored in Netscape format, in which each cookie is a string consisting of the following 7 parts, separated by tabs: See https://curl.se/docs/http-cookies.html for more info.
syntax: function long http.cookiejar.save (long cookiejar, const string file)
returns: 0 — success <> 0 — an I/O error, like ENOSPC

name: http.delete
doc: Sends a DELETE HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.delete (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.get
doc: Sends a GET HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.get (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.head
doc: Sends a HEAD HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.head (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.header.name
doc: Returns the HTTP header name of an http.header object.
syntax: function string http.header.name (long header)
returns: the HTTP header name, eg. "Content-Type"

name: http.header.next
doc: Returns an http.header object's next http.header object. Example: long headerlist long header |* assume headerlist refers to a filled http.headerlist object |* get the first header from the headerlist header = http.headerlist.first(headerlist) while header <> 0 |* get name and values from header here ... |* get next header header = http.header.next(header) endwhile
syntax: function long http.header.next (long header)
returns: the next http.header object, or 0 if there is no next http.header object

name: http.header.value
doc: Returns the HTTP header value of an http.header object.
syntax: function string header.value (long header)
returns: the HTTP header value, e.g. "application/json" (which is a possible value of the "Content-Type" HTTP header)

name: http.headerlist.add
doc: Adds a name-value HTTP header pair to an http.headerlist object. Note that adding an HTTP header multiple times with the same name), overwrites the already existing one. The only exception is the Set-Cookie which can occur multiple times in the headerlist. HTTP header names are searched in a case-insensitive way. So e.g. "Content-Type" is equal to "content-type".
syntax: function void http.headerlist.add (long headerlist, const string name, const string value)
returns: void

name: http.headerlist.add_list
doc: Adds the contents of another http.headerlist to an http.headerlist object. When an HTTP header already exists, it is overwritten. The only exception is the Set-Cookie header, which can occur multiple times in a headerlist.
syntax: function void http.headerlist.add_list (long headerlist, long other_headerlist)
returns: void

name: http.headerlist.delete
doc: Deletes an http.headerlist object. All contained http.header objects are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.headerlist.delete (long headerlist)
returns: void

name: http.headerlist.first
doc: Returns the first http.header object of an http.headerlist. This can be used to iterate all HTTP headers in the list. Example: long headerlist long header |* assume headerlist refers to a filled http.headerlist object |* get the first header from the headerlist header = http.headerlist.first(headerlist) while header <> 0 |* get name and values from header here ... |* get next header header = http.header.next(header) endwhile
syntax: function long http.headerlist.first (long headerlist)
returns: the first http.header object in the list, or 0 if the list is empty

name: http.headerlist.get
doc: Gets the HTTP header with the specified name from an http.headerlist object. The name is searched in a case-insensitive way. The HTTP header is returned as an http.header object. Note: The Set-Cookie header can occur multiple times in an http.headerlist object. This function returns the first Set-Cookie header found. An http.headerlist object stores Set-Cookie headers in sequence. In this way it is possible to get the next Set-Cookie header(s) by calling http.header.next() on the first Set-Cookie header returned by this function. Example: long headerlist long header |* assume headerlist refers to a filled http.headerlist object |* get the "Content-Type" header |* searching is done in a case-insensitive manner, so the following names also work: |* "CONTENT-TYPE", "content-type", "Content-type" header = http.headerlist.get(headerlist, "Content-Type") if header <> 0 then |* header found endif
syntax: function long http.headerlist.get (long headerlist, const string name)
returns: the (first) http.header object with the specified name, or 0 if no header with the specified name was found

name: http.headerlist.get_all
doc: Returns a new http.headerlist object containing http.header objects with the given name. As this is a new list, you have to take care of deleting it when it is no longer needed. If no header was found with the given name, 0 is returned. Currently, this function is only useful for Set-Cookie HTTP response headers, as that is the only HTTP header that can occur multiple times. Example: long headerlist long set_cookie_headers long set_cookie_header |* assume headerlist refers to a filled http.headerlist object |* get all "Set-Cookie" headers; this returns a new http.headerlist |* with copies of the found Set-Cookie http.header objects; |* searching is done in a case-insensitive manner, so the following names also work: |* "SET-COOKIE", "set-cookie" set_cookie_headers = http.headerlist.get_all(headerlist, "Set-Cookie") set_cookie_header = http.headerlist.first(set_cookie_headers) while set_cookie_header <> 0 |* process the header |* get the next header set_cookie_header = http.header.next(set_cookie_header) endwhile |* delete the list of Set-Cookie headers http.headerlist.delete(set_cookie_headers)
syntax: function long http.headerlist.get_all (long headerlist, const string name)
returns: an http.headerlist object containing http.header objects with the specified name, or 0 if the specified header name was not found

name: http.headerlist.new
doc: Constructs a new http.headerlist object. It is possible to initialize the http.headerlist object with HTTP header name-value pairs. Example: long headerlist headerlist = http.headerlist.new( "Content-Type", "application/json", "X-Infor-LnCompany", 422)
syntax: function long http.headerlist.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.headerlist object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.mimepart.delete
doc: Deletes an http.mimepart object. If the http.mimepart object is part of an http.mimepartlist object is it removed from the mimepart list as well.
syntax: function void http.mimepart.delete (long mimepart)
returns: void

name: http.mimepart.new
doc: Constructs a new http.mimepart object. Use the attributes as specified below to configure the MIME part. Example: long mimepart mimepart = http.mimepart.new( HTTP_MIME_CONTENTTYPE, "application/json", HTTP_MIME_NAME, "part1", HTTP_MIME_STRING, "{ ""key"": ""value"" }", HTTP_MIME_ENCODER, "base64")
syntax: function long http.mimepart.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.mimepart object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.mimepartlist.add
doc: Adds an http.mimepart object to an http.mimepartlist object.
syntax: function void http.mimepartlist.add (long mimepartlist, long http.mimepart)
returns: void

name: http.mimepartlist.add_list
doc: Adds the contents of another http.mimepartlist to an http.mimepartlist object.
syntax: function void http.mimepartlist.add_list (long mimepartlist, long other_mimepartlist)
returns: void

name: http.mimepartlist.delete
doc: Deletes an http.mimepartlist object. All contained http.mimepart objects are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.mimepartlist.delete (long http.mimepartlist)
returns: void

name: http.mimepartlist.new
doc: Constructs a new http.mimepartlist object.
syntax: function long http.mimepartlist.new ()
returns: a new http.mimepartlist object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.oauth1params.delete
doc: Deletes an http.oauth1params object.
syntax: function void http.oauth1params.delete (long oauth1params)
returns: void

name: http.oauth1params.new
doc: Constructs a new http.oauth1params object. Use the attributes as specified below to specify the OAuth1 parameters. Example: long oauth1params oauth1params = http.oauth1params.new( HTTP_OAUTH1_SIGNATUREMETHOD, "HMAC-SHA1", HTTP_OAUTH1_CONSUMERKEY, "some_key", HTTP_OAUTH1_CONSUMERSECRET, "some_secret")
syntax: function long http.oauth1params.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.oauth1params object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.options
doc: Sends an OPTIONS HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.options (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.patch
doc: Sends a PATCH HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.patch (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.post
doc: Sends a POST HTTP request to a URL.

returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.put

returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.queryparamlist.add
doc: Adds a name-value query parameter pair to an http.queryparamlist object.
syntax: function void http.queryparamlist.add (long queryparamlist, const string name, const string value)
returns: void

name: http.queryparamlist.add_list
doc: Adds the contents of another http.queryparamlist to an http.queryparamlist object.
syntax: function void http.queryparamlist.add_list (long queryparamlist, long other_queryparamlist)
returns: void

name: http.queryparamlist.delete
doc: Deletes an http.queryparamlist object. Any contained name-value query parameter pairs are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.queryparamlist.delete (long queryparamlist)
returns: void

name: http.queryparamlist.new
doc: Constructs a new http.queryparamlist object. It is possible to initialize the http.queryparamlist object with name-value query parameter pairs. When the http.queryparamlist object is passed to eg. http.get(), the name and value pairs will be used to build a url-encoded querystring. The querystring is then appended to the url after the '?' sign. Example: long queryparamlist long response queryparamlist = http.queryparamlist.new( "name", "John Doe", "address", "34, Mainstreet", "city", "New York") response = http.get("http://example.com/get", HTTP_QUERYPARAMLIST, queryparamlist) http.queryparamlist.delete(queryparamlist) This results in the following url: http://example.com/get?name=John%20Doe&address=34,%20Mainstreet&city=New%20York
syntax: function long http.queryparamlist.new ( ...)
returns: a new http.queryparamlist object, or 0 in case of an error

name: http.queryparamlist.to_string
doc: Converts the key-value pairs in an http.queryparamlist object to an application/x-www-form-urlencoded string. The string can be used as the body of an HTTP request to post form data. By default the '&' is used to separate key-value pairs, but this can be overruled. Example: long queryparamlist string formdata(1) based queryparamlist = http.queryparamlist.new( "name", "John Doe", "address", "34, Mainstreet", "city", "New York") str.assign(formdata, http.queryparamlist.to_string(queryparamlist)) |* formdata now contains: "name=John%20Doe&address=34,%20Mainstreet&city=New%20York" http.queryparamlist.delete(queryparamlist)
syntax: function string http.queryparamlist.to_string (long queryparamlist [, string sep(1)])
returns: an application/x-www-form-urlencoded string; or an empty string if the http.queryparamlist object is empty

name: http.response.bodystream
doc: Returns the stream id of the response body. It is not necessary to rewind the stream, the position is already at the start of the data retrieved from the server. In case a stream id was passed using the HTTP_RESPONSE_BODY option, this returns that stream id.
syntax: function long http.response.bodystream (long response)
returns: a stream id

name: http.response.curlcode
doc: Returns the cURL code stored in the response object. A cURL code of 0 means that communication was successful. Any other code indicates that communication was not successful. Reasons may be e.g. that the host could not be resolved, or (in case of https) that there are issues with the certificate(s). Note that a cURL code of 0 only tells that communication was successful. This does however not tell whether the HTTP request succeeded. Use http.response.statuscode() to check whether the HTTP request could be handled by the webserver. Use function http.response.error_message() to retrieve an English description of the cURL error.
syntax: function long http.response.curlcode (long response)
returns: a cURL code, 0 means OK, any other code indicates an error

name: http.response.delete
doc: Deletes an http.response object. If the response object contains a body stream that was automatically opened, the stream will be closed as well.
syntax: function void http.response.delete (long response)
returns: void

name: http.response.error_message
doc: Call this to retrieve an error message in case there was an error while sending the request. In case the cURL code is zero (0), this returns "No error"
syntax: function string http.response.error_message (long response)
returns: an English error message, which can be used for debugging and/or logging

name: http.response.headerlist
doc: Returns the list of HTTP headers received from the server.
syntax: function long http.response.headerlist (long response)
returns: an http.headerlist object

name: http.response.request_method
doc: Returns the HTTP method of the request for which the response was created. The HTTP method and the URL are stored to identify to what request the response object belongs.
syntax: function string http.response.request_method (long response)
returns: the HTTP request method, like "GET", "POST" etc.

name: http.response.request_url
doc: Returns the URL of the request for which the response was created. The HTTP method and the URL are stored to identify to what request the response object belongs.
syntax: function string http.response.request_url (long response)
returns: the request URL

name: http.response.statuscode
doc: Returns the HTTP response statuscode, like 200, 404 or 500, etc.
syntax: function long http.response.statuscode (long response)
returns: an HTTP statuscode

name: http.response.statustext
doc: Returns the HTTP response status text, like "OK" (for 200), "Not Found" (for 404), "Internal Server Error" (for 500), etc.
syntax: function string http.response.statustext (long response)
returns: an HTTP status text

name: http.routeparamlist.add
doc: Adds a name-value route parameter pair to an http.routeparamlist object.
syntax: function void http.routeparamlist.add (long routeparamlist, const string name, const string value)
returns: void

name: http.routeparamlist.add_list
doc: Adds the contents of another http.routeparamlist to an http.routeparamlist object. If route parameters already exist, they are replaced.
syntax: function void http.routeparamlist.add_list (long routeparamlist, long other_routeparamlist)
returns: void

name: http.routeparamlist.delete
doc: Deletes an http.routeparamlist object. Any contained name-value route parameters pairs are deleted as well.
syntax: function void http.routeparamlist.delete (long routeparamlist)
returns: void

name: http.routeparamlist.new
doc: Constructs a new http.routeparamlist object. It is possible to initialize the http.routeparamlist object with name-value route parameter pairs. When the http.routeparamlist object is passed to eg. http.get(), the name and value pairs will be used to fill in route parameters in the url. Example: long routeparamlist long response routeparamlist = http.routeparamlist.new( "app", "eln", "farm", "euwe1prda", "tenant", "ACME_PRD") response = http.get( "https://aws.com/apps/{app}/farms/{farm}/tenant/{tenant}", HTTP_ROUTEPARAMLIST, routeparamlist) http.routeparamlist.delete(routeparamlist) This results in the following url: https://aws.com/apps/eln/farms/euwe1prda/tenant/ACME_PRD
syntax: function void http.routeparamlist.new ( ...)
returns: void

name: http.send
doc: Sends an HTTP request to a URL.

returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: http.trace
doc: Sends a TRACE HTTP request to a URL.
syntax: function long http.trace (const string url, ...)
returns: an http.response object; check the response object for information about whether the request succeeded

name: import
doc: Import retrieves the value of the specified variable of the parent process. This parent process is not always identified by the variable parent in case of dynamic index switching. When using dynamic index switching, the parent process is sometimes killed and restarted. This causes a different parent process, whereas the variable parent is not updated. For all other circumstances, import is equivalent to get.var( parent, "variable", value).
syntax: function [long] import (string variable_name, ref void value)
returns: 0 — error; probably variable not found in the parent process 1 — success

name: import.4gl.var
doc: Imports a 'predefined' 4GL variable. Like number.of.marks which is actually a macro.
syntax: function void import.4gl.var (string variable_name, ref void value)
returns: void

name: ims.clearerr
doc: Resets the error and end-of-byte-array indicator.
syntax: function long ims.clearerr (long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.close
doc: Closes the byte array. This is done automaticallly when you leave your process. For a variable byte array (VBA), the claimed memory will be freed. For a fixed byte array (FBA), the used memory buffer has to be freed manually (or is freed automatically when you leave your process).
syntax: function long ims.close (long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.eof
doc: Detects if the end of the byte array is reached.
syntax: function long ims.eof (long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Not at the end of the byte array. > 0 — The end of the byte array is detected.

name: ims.error
doc: Detects if an error has occurred while reading from or writing to the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.error (long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — No errors. > 0 — An error occurred.

name: ims.getc$
doc: Returns the next character from the byte array.
syntax: function string ims.getc$ (long bytearray)
returns: If an empty string is returned, either the end of the string has been reached or an error has occurred.

name: ims.getproperties
doc: Returns the properties of the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.getproperties (long bytearray, ref string buffer [, ref long size])
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.gets
doc: Reads characters from the byte array into a buffer ( line).
syntax: function long ims.gets (ref string line, long size, long bytearray [, long skip.mode] [, long there.was.more])
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.openfba
doc: Opens a Fixed Byte Array (FBA). The following code fragment shows an example of how to create an FBA: string buffer(1) based long size long stream.id size = 1024 alloc.mem(buffer, size) stream.id = ims.openFBA(buffer, size, "r+")
syntax: function long ims.openfba (string buffer, long size, string type)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably buffer is not a valid stream, the type is invalid or the byte array is full. > 0 — Success. A byte array identifier was returned..

name: ims.openvba
doc: Opens a Variable Byte Array (VBA).
syntax: function long ims.openvba (string type [, long initialSize] [, long increment])
returns: -11 — Error, more than 512 streams are in use. -1 — Error, most probably bytearrray is not a valid stream or the byte array is full. > 0 — Success. A byte array identifier was returned.

name: ims.putc$
doc: Writes a character to the current position in the byte array.
syntax: function string ims.putc$ (string char, long bytearray)
returns: If no error occurs, the written character is returned. Otherwise, an empty string is returned.

name: ims.puts
doc: Writes a line (and a new-line character) to the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.puts (string line, long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.r.long
doc: Reads a 32-bit value from the byte array. The 4 bytes read from the byte array are interpreted as the 32-bit two’s complement representation of a signed integer value.
syntax: function long ims.r.long (long bytearray)
returns: Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream, or end-of-byte-array reached. Notice that this error value -1 cannot be distinguished from normal value -1. This is problematic, unless it is known that value -1 is not expected as a normal value to be read from the byte array. -1 >= -2^31 and < 2^31 — The numerical value of the 4 bytes read from the supplied byte array. This is a value in the signed 32-bit range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]).

name: ims.r.short
doc: Reads a 16-bit value from the byte array. The 2 bytes read from the byte array are interpreted as the 16-bit binary representation of an unsigned integer value.
syntax: function long ims.r.short (long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream, or end-of-byte-array reached. >= 0 — The numerical value of the 2 bytes read from the supplied byte array. This is a value in the unsigned 16-bit range [0 … 2^16 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 65,535]).

name: ims.r.utc
doc: Reads a specified amount of bytes from the byte array. The bytes read from the byte array are interpreted as the two’s complement representation of a signed integer value.
syntax: function long ims.r.utc (long bytearray [, long byte.count])
returns: Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream, or end-of-byte-array reached. Notice that this error value -1 cannot be distinguished from normal value -1. This is problematic, unless it is known that value -1 is not expected as a normal value to be read from the byte array. -1 The numerical value of the bytes read from the supplied byte array. Typically, this is a (non-negative) UTC long format value stored earlier by the function ims.w.utc(), or prepared by any other means. This function does not perform any value check. >= -(256^ byte.count)/2 and < (256^ byte.count)/2

name: ims.read
doc: Reads a number of bytes from the byte array into a buffer.
syntax: function long ims.read (ref string buffer, long nrBytes, long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — End-of-byte-array. > 0 — Number of bytes actually read.

name: ims.rewind
doc: Sets the position in byte array to the beginning. Same as ims.seek(0, 0, bytearray).
syntax: function long ims.rewind (long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.seek
doc: Changes the current position within the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.seek (long offset, long opt, long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. >= 0 — New offset position from beginning of the byte array.

name: ims.setvbaproperties
doc: Sets the properties of the Variable Byte Array (VBA).
syntax: function long ims.setvbaproperties (long bytearray, long increment)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearrray is not a variable byte array . 0 — Success.

name: ims.skip
doc: Skips forward a number of bytes in the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.skip (long nrbytes, long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.spool.line
doc: Spools a line and writes it to the byte array. The characters in the line are copied to the byte array until the last non-white character in the line is encountered. After that, the contents of the line is cleared.
syntax: function long ims.spool.line (ref string line, long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.tell
doc: Returns the current offset within the byte array relative to the begin of the byte array.
syntax: function long ims.tell (long byetarray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. >= 0 — Offset, in number of bytes, within the byte array.

name: ims.w.long
doc: Writes a 32-bit integer value into the byte array. The function ims.w.long() writes the 32 least significant bits of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first 4 bytes of the supplied byte array. The inverse function ims.r.long() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the signed 32-bit value range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]) by repeatedly adding or subtracting 2^32 until the value is in the signed 32-bit value range. More specifically, the inverse function ims.r.long() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the signed 32-bit value range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]).
syntax: function long ims.w.long (long value, long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.w.short
doc: Writes a 16-bit integer value into the byte array. The function ims.w.short() writes the 16 least significant bits of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first 2 bytes of the supplied byte array. The inverse function ims.r.short() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the unsigned 16-bit value range [0 … 2^16 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 65,535]) by repeatedly adding or subtracting 2^16 until the value is in the unsigned 16-bit value range. More specifically, the inverse function ims.r.short() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the unsigned 16-bit value range [0 … 2^16 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 65,535]).
syntax: function long ims.w.short (long value, long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.w.utc
doc: Writes an integer value into the byte array. The function ims.w.utc() writes the byte.count least significant bytes of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first byte.count bytes of the supplied byte array. The inverse function ims.r.utc() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the signed byte.count-byte value range [-(256^ byte.count)/2 … (256^ byte.count)/2 - 1] by repeatedly adding or subtracting 256^ byte.count until the value is in the signed byte.count-byte value range. More specifically, the inverse function ims.r.utc() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the signed byte.count-byte value range [-(256^ byte.count)/2 … (256^ byte.count)/2 - 1].
syntax: function long ims.w.utc (long value, long bytearray [, long byte.count])
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — Success.

name: ims.write

syntax: function long ims.write (string buffer, long nrBytes, long bytearray)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably bytearray is not a valid stream. 0 — End-of-byte-array. > 0 — Number of bytes actually written.

returns: 1 — Bshell runs in FIPS-140-2 mode. NOTE: The function may return other values for other secure modes in the future. Make sure you test for values "1" (and not just "true") when you want to test for FIPS-140-2 mode. 0 — Bshell does not run in a secure mode.

name: inherit.object

name: input.again

returns: The local date or local time value depending on the format string. Or -1 if an error occurs (such as when there is no valid local date or local time value possible for the given string). Related topics the local date as the number of days since 01-01-0001 or the local time as the number of seconds since 00:00 hour depending on the format string. -1 — Error. The exact result is negative or greater than the maximum value 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) - 1 of the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range.

"before.program" , the field, including label etc, is not visible anymore but the space on the form is still reserved. So when the field is made visible again later, the empty reserved space is occupied again with the field. However, when the field is made invisible in the before program, it may not be made visible later in the code, since no space is available.

returns: void

name: inputfield.visible

returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

syntax: function string insertln$ (string string_expr)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: int
doc: The function int() performs explicit double to long type conversion. If the supplied double value is positive, it is incremented by 0.0000001 as the first step of the conversion. If the supplied value is negative, it is decremented by 0.0000001 as the first step of the conversion. This is done to avoid rounding problems. The next step of the explicit conversion uses the same algorithm as implicit double to long type conversion: discarding the fractional part of the double value, leaving only its integer part. If the exact resulting integer value is outside the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range of the long data type, then the result is undefined.
syntax: function long int (double x)
returns: The long value resulting from the described explicit double to long type conversion applied to the supplied input value.

name: is.administrator
doc: This checks whether or not the user that is running the bshell has administrator rights on the server that the bshell is running. On UNIX systems, the function returns TRUE if the user has root access to the system. On Windows NT systems, the function returns TRUE if the user belongs to the administrator group.
syntax: function boolean is.administrator ()
returns: TRUE user has administrator rights FALSE user does not have administrator rights

name: is.composite.child
doc: This function checks whether the current session is running as a composite child session or not. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode and as a child within a composite session. This function can be called from a 4GL-Session or from a GBF session.
syntax: function boolean is.composite.child ()
returns: true — this session is running as a composite child session false — otherwise

name: is.field.invisible

name: is.field.multi.currency

syntax: function boolean is.field.multi.currency (string field_name(18))
returns: TRUE — Field is a multi currency field. FALSE — Field is not a multi currency field.

name: is.graph.present

returns: true — the session is part of an active graph false — otherwise

name: is.image.changed

syntax: function boolean is.image.changed (string fieldname)
returns: true — When an image is changed for this image field. false — When no image is changed for this image field.

name: is.image.dropped

syntax: function boolean is.image.dropped (string fieldname)
returns: true — When an image is changed for this image field. false — When no image is changed for this image field.

name: is.internal.session.graphs.active

returns: true — If the Internal Session Graphs is active false — Otherwise

name: is.landlord.bse

returns: TRUE — The BSE is a landlord BSE. FALSE — The BSE is not multi tenant enabled or is not a landlord BSE.

name: is.mmt.controller
doc: This function checks whether the current session is running as a multi-main table controller session or not. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode or as a controller within a multi-main table session.

returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: is.mmt.satellite

syntax: function boolean is.mmt.satellite ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: is.multi.tenant.enabled
doc: Deprecated. This function is deprecated as the name is confusing and it is actually the same as function is.landlord.bse(). Returns TRUE if the current BSE is multi-tenant enabled; FALSE otherwise. Note: if the current BSE runs in a tenant, the function returns FALSE.
syntax: function boolean is.multi.tenant.enabled ()
returns: TRUE — The BSE is multi tenant enabled. FALSE — The BSE is not multi tenant enabled.

name: is.tenant.bse
doc: This function returns TRUE if the current BSE is a tenant BSE; FALSE otherwise.
syntax: function boolean is.tenant.bse ()
returns: TRUE — The BSE is a tenant BSE. FALSE — The BSE is not multi tenant enabled or is not a tenant BSE.

name: is.tree.detail.child
doc: This function tells whether the current session is running as part of a Tree-Detail session. This function can be useful when a session can be run in standalone mode and as a child within a Tree-Detail session. This function can be called from a 4GL-Session or from a GBF session.
syntax: function boolean is.tree.detail.child ()
returns: true — The session is running as a child of a Tree-Detail session false — Otherwise

name: is.view.field
doc: This function can be used to check whether a field is currently a view field. This is useful when, for example, the view can be personalized and a total line only makes sense with a specific field in the view. before.program after.form.read sections.

returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: is_kms_encrypted

syntax: function boolean is_kms_encrypted (string encrypted_password)
returns: 0 — False. The string is not KMS encrypted. 1 — The string looks like it is encrypted with KMS. The function only looks at the lead-in of the string, if that is "$1AWSKMS$" it will return TRUE, else FALSE.

name: isdigit
doc: This function tests whether the supplied string is the textual representation of an integer value.
syntax: function boolean isdigit (string str_expr)
returns: TRUE string contains the textual representation of an integer value FALSE string does not contain the textual representation of an integer value

name: iso.to.date
doc: This converts an ISO 8601 date string to a local date. The following formats are supported:
syntax: function long iso.to.date (const string iso.date)
returns: > 0 — The local date value. 0 — An empty string was specified. < 0 — Error.

name: iso.to.utc
doc: This converts a string, representing a time in ISO 8601 format into a UTC long value. The following formats are supported:
syntax: function domain ttutc iso.to.utc (const string iso.string)
returns: > 0 — The UTC long format value. 0 — An empty string was specified. < 0 — Error.

name: isspace
doc: This tests whether the result of string_expr contains only spaces or is empty.
syntax: function boolean isspace (string str_expr)
returns: TRUE string is empty or contains only spaces FALSE string is not empty and contains characters other than spaces

name: java.destroy.queue
doc: Removes a queue, given the queue id. This will also remove all buckets on that queue!!
syntax: function long java.destroy.queue (long Queue.id)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.execute.static.application.method
doc: Executes a versioned, dynamically loaded, Java method. These Java mehods can also return a (string) value to the 3 GL.

returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.execute.static.method.sync
doc: Executes a Java static method, with no return type, within the JavaVM. java.execute.static.method.sync() returns to the caller AFTER completion of the Java method. java.execute.static.method.async() returns to the caller BEFORE completion of the Java method. See also java.execute.static.application.method for an alternative Java interface that allows a result to be returned from the Java method.
syntax: function long java.execute.static.method.sync (string class.name, string method.name [, void ...])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.get.bucket

syntax: function long java.get.bucket (long Queue.id, ref string body, long length [, ref string header])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.install.listener
doc: Installs a listener at the Infor Enterprise Server side. Whenever a message arrives on the queue specified by queue.id, the 3GL process will be notified by an EVT_CHANNEL_EVENT event. For installation of a listener at the Java side, see the Java IQueueListener interface definition.
syntax: function long java.install.listener (long Queue.id [, long become.owner])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.load.application
doc: Load the most recent version of a Java application and return a handle to be used in subsequent operations. A Java virtual machine (JVM) is started when required (or an existing one is used), see Java VM integration - Infor Enterprise Server 3GL for details.
syntax: function long java.load.application (string Application.Name)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.lookup.queue
doc: Checks whether a queue is still valid and, if so, if the queue contains a message. The message is not removed from the queue.
syntax: function long java.lookup.queue (long Queue.id [, ref string header])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.new.queue
doc: Creates a new queue for buckets. Upon return, the new queue.id is returned, or an error code is presented. NOTE: queues are removed automatically if the process that created it (or the process that called java.install.listener(…) on that queue) is finished !! See also the 3GL function java.install.listener.
syntax: function long java.new.queue ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.put.bucket
doc: Places a message onto a queue. The message contains a header (of type string) and a body (which can contain any character).
syntax: function long java.put.bucket (long Queue.id, string body, long length [, string header])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.uninstall.listener
doc: Uninstalls a listener at the Infor Enterprise Server side. All buckets on this queue will remain available. The listener can only be uninstalled by the process that installed the listener.
syntax: function long java.uninstall.listener (long Queue.id)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: java.unload.application
doc: Unloads an application loaded by java.load.application. This will free some resources depending on the garbage collector of the JVM and invalidates the handle. The JVM is not stopped upon this call. The JVM is only stopped when the bshell stops.
syntax: function long java.unload.application (long handle)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: job.add.field

returns: void

name: Json.add
doc: Adds a JSON value at the end of a JSON array.
syntax: function [long] Json.add (long json_array, long json_value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON value which has been added to the JSON array.

name: Json.addBoolean
doc: Convenience function for directly adding a 3GL boolean value to a JSON array. The 3GL boolean value is first converted to a JSON boolean value which is then added to the array. Json.add(json, Json.newBoolean(value))
syntax: function [long] Json.addBoolean (long json_array, boolean value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON boolean value which has been added to the JSON array.

name: Json.addDouble
doc: Convenience function for directly adding a 3GL double value to a JSON array. The 3GL double value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then added to the array. Json.addNumber(json, value)
syntax: function [long] Json.addDouble (long json_array, double value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been added to the JSON array.

name: Json.addLong
doc: Convenience function for directly adding a 3GL long value to a JSON array. The 3GL long value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then added to the array. Json.add(json, Json.newLong(value))
syntax: function [long] Json.addLong (long json_array, long value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been added to the JSON array.

name: Json.addNull
doc: Convenience function for adding a JSON null value to a JSON array. Json.add(json, Json.newNull())
syntax: function [long] Json.addNull (long json_array)
returns: Optional, the new JSON null value which has been added to the JSON array.

name: Json.addNumber
doc: Convenience function for directly adding a 3GL long or double value to a JSON array. The 3GL long or double value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then added to the array. Json.add(json, Json.newNumber(value))
syntax: function [long] Json.addNumber (long json_array, long|double value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been added to the JSON array.

name: Json.addString
doc: Convenience function for directly adding a 3GL string value to a JSON array. The 3GL string value is first converted to a JSON string value which is then added to the array. Json.add(json, Json.newString(value))
syntax: function [long] Json.addString (long json_array, const string value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON string value which has been added to the JSON array.

name: Json.at
doc: Returns the JSON value that is stored at the specified index in a JSON array.
syntax: function long Json.at (long json_array, long idx)
returns: The JSON value that is stored in the JSON array at the specified index.

name: Json.boolean
doc: Returns the 3GL value of a JSON boolean value.

returns: true or false

name: Json.booleanAt
