syntax: function boolean Json.booleanAt (long json_array, long idx)
returns: The 3GL boolean value stored at the specified index, true or false.

name: Json.copy
doc: Returns a (deep) copy of a JSON value. In case the JSON value is of type JSON_TYPE_OBJECT or JSON_TYPE_ARRAY, all contained members are copied as well.
syntax: function long Json.copy (long json_value)
returns: A (deep) copy of the passed JSON value.

name: Json.copyToProcess
doc: Returns a (deep) copy of a JSON value. The copy is created in the address space of the specified process. If this is another process than the current process, then the JSON is readonly for the current process. In case the JSON value is of type JSON_TYPE_OBJECT or JSON_TYPE_ARRAY, all contained members are copied as well.
syntax: function long Json.copyToProcess (long json_value, long process_id)
returns: A (deep) copy of the passed JSON value.

name: Json.count
doc: Returns the number of JSON values stored in a JSON array.
syntax: function long Json.count (long json_array)
returns: The number of JSON values in the JSON array.

name: Json.del
doc: Deletes the specified key from a JSON object. The associated JSON value is deleted as well.
syntax: function void Json.del (long json_object, const string key)
returns: void

name: Json.delete
doc: Deletes a JSON value. In case the JSON value is of type JSON_TYPE_OBJECT or JSON_TYPE_ARRAY all contained members are deleted as well.
syntax: function void Json.delete (long json_value)
returns: void

name: Json.detach
doc: Detaches a JSON value from its parent JSON object or JSON array. After calling this function, the JSON value is no longer a member of its parent. The member of the parent JSON object or array is assigned the JSON null value.
syntax: function [long] Json.detach (long json_value)
returns: Optional, the detached JSON value.

name: Json.double
doc: Returns a JSON number value as a 3GL double value. Json.number(json)
syntax: function double Json.double (long json_value)
returns: The value contained in the JSON number value as a double.

name: Json.doubleAt
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL double value of the JSON number value that is stored at the specified index in a JSON array. Json.numberAt(json, idx)
syntax: function double Json.doubleAt (long json_array, long idx)
returns: The JSON number value stored at the specified index, as a 3GL double value.

name: Json.get
doc: Returns the JSON value associated with the specified key of a JSON object.
syntax: function long Json.get (long json_object, const string key)
returns: The JSON value associated with the specified key.

name: Json.getBoolean
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL boolean value of the JSON boolean value associated with the specified key of a JSON object. Json.boolean(Json.get(json, key))
syntax: function long Json.getBoolean (long json_object, const string key)
returns: The 3GL boolean value associated with the specified key, true or false.

name: Json.getDouble
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL double value of the JSON number value associated with the specified key of a JSON object. Json.getNumber(json, key)
syntax: function double Json.getDouble (long json_object, const string key)
returns: The JSON number value associated with the specified key, as a 3GL double value.

name: Json.getLong
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL long value of the JSON number value associated with the specified key of a JSON object. Note that if the actual value stored in the JSON number is a double value, the value is truncated. E.g. 1.234 becomes 1. int(Json.getNumber(json, key))
syntax: function long Json.getLong (long json_object, const string key)
returns: The JSON number value associated with the specified key, as a 3GL long value.

name: Json.getNumber
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL long or double value of the JSON number value associated with the specified key of a JSON object. Json.number(Json.get(json, key))
syntax: function double Json.getNumber (long json_object, const string key)
returns: The JSON number value associated with the specified key, as a 3GL double value.

name: Json.getString
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL string value of the JSON string value associated with the specified key of a JSON object. Json.string(Json.get(json, key))
syntax: function string Json.getString (long json_object, const string key)
returns: The 3GL string value associated with the specified key.

name: Json.has
doc: Tests whether a JSON object contains the specified key.
syntax: function boolean Json.has (long json_object, const string key)
returns: true if the specified key exists, else false

name: Json.isJson
doc: Tests whether parameter 'json_value' is a JSON value.
syntax: function boolean Json.isJson (long json_value)
returns: true if parameter 'json_value' is a JSON value, else false.

name: Json.isNull
doc: Tests whether a JSON value is a JSON null value.
syntax: function boolean Json.isNull (long json_value)
returns: true if the JSON value is of type JSON_TYPE_NULL, else false.

name: Json.iter
doc: Returns an iterator which can be used to traverse the members of a JSON object or JSON array. On return the iterator points to the first member.

returns: An iterator pointing to the first member of a JSON object or JSON array, or 0 in case the JSON object or JSON array has no members.

name: Json.iterKey
doc: Returns the key name to which the specified iterator is pointing.
syntax: function string Json.iterKey (long json_object, long iter)
returns: The key name to which the specified iterator is pointing.

name: Json.iterNext
doc: Moves the iterator to the next member of a JSON object or JSON array.
syntax: function long Json.iterNext (long json_value, long iter)
returns: An iterator pointing to the next member of a JSON object or JSON array, or 0 in case the JSON object or JSON array has no more members.

name: Json.iterValue
doc: Returns the JSON value to which the specified iterator is pointing.
syntax: function long Json.iterValue (long json_value, long iter)
returns: The JSON value to which the specified iterator is pointing.

name: Json.long
doc: Returns a JSON number value as a 3GL long value. Note that if the actual value stored in the JSON number is a double value, the value is truncated. E.g. 1.234 becomes 1. int(Json.number(json))
syntax: function long Json.long (long json_value)
returns: The value contained in the JSON number value as a long.

name: Json.longAt
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL long value of the JSON number value that is stored at the specified index in a JSON array. Note that if the actual value stored in the JSON number is a double value, the value is truncated. E.g. 1.234 becomes 1. int(Json.numberAt(json, idx))
syntax: function long Json.longAt (long json_array, long idx)
returns: The JSON number value stored at the specified index, as a 3GL long value.

name: Json.newArray

name: Json.newBoolean

name: Json.newDouble

name: Json.newLong

name: Json.newNull

name: Json.newNumber

returns: A new JSON number value, containing the passed 3GL long or double value.

name: Json.newObject
doc: Creates a new empty JSON object.
syntax: function long Json.newObject ()
returns: A new empty JSON value of type JSON_TYPE_OBJECT.

name: Json.newString
doc: Creates a new JSON string value, containing the passed string value.
syntax: function long Json.newString (const string value)
returns: A new JSON string value, containing the passed string value.

name: Json.number
doc: Returns a JSON number value as a 3GL double.
syntax: function double Json.number (long json_value)
returns: The value contained in the JSON number value as a double.

name: Json.numberAt
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL long or double value of the JSON number value that is stored at the specified index in a JSON array. Json.number(Json.at(json, idx))
syntax: function double Json.numberAt (long json_array, long idx)

name: Json.path
doc: Returns the JSON value in a JSON object or array, which is located at the specified path. The parameters passed to this function determine the path that is chosen to locate the JSON value. Example: { "name": "John Doe", "phone numbers": [ "06-12345678", "0342-428888" ], "department": { "id": "HR", "name": "Human Resources", "office days": ["Monday", "Wednesday", "Friday"] } } |* To get the 2nd phone number: phone2 = Json.path(obj, "phone numbers", 2) |* To get the department name: depname = Json.path(obj, "department", "name") |* To get the value "Friday": workday3 = Json.path(obj, "department", "office days", 3)

returns: Optional, the new JSON value which has been put into the JSON array.

name: Json.putBoolean
doc: Convenience function for directly putting a 3GL boolean value at the specified index in a JSON array. The 3GL boolean value is first converted to a JSON boolean value which is then put into the array. Json.put(json, idx, Json.newBoolean(value))
syntax: function [long] Json.putBoolean (long json_array, long idx, boolean value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON boolean value which has been put into the JSON array.

name: Json.putDouble
doc: Convenience function for directly putting a 3GL double value at the specified index in a JSON array. The 3GL double value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then put into the array. Json.putNumber(json, idx, value)
syntax: function long Json.putDouble ([long] json_array, long idx, double value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been put into the JSON array.

name: Json.putLong
doc: Convenience function for directly putting a 3GL long value at the specified index in a JSON array. The 3GL long value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then put into the array. Json.putNumber(json, idx, value)
syntax: function long Json.putLong ([long] json_array, long idx, long value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been put into the JSON array.

name: Json.putNull
doc: Convenience function for putting a JSON null value at the specified index in a JSON array. Json.put(json, idx, Json.newNull())
syntax: function long Json.putNull ([long] json_array, long idx)
returns: Optional, the new JSON null value which has been put into the JSON array.

name: Json.putNumber
doc: Convenience function for directly putting a 3GL long or double value at the specified index in a JSON array. The 3GL long or double value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then put into the array. Json.put(json, idx, Json.newNumber(value))
syntax: function long Json.putNumber ([long] json_array, long idx, ... value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been put into the JSON array.

name: Json.putString
doc: Convenience function for directly putting a 3GL string value at the specified index in a JSON array. The 3GL string value is first converted to a JSON string value which is then put into the array. Json.put(json, idx, Json.newString(value))
syntax: function long Json.putString ([long] json_array, long idx, string value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON string value which has been put into the JSON array.

name: Json.read
doc: Reads JSON text from a stream, parses it and creates a JSON value from it. The stream can be an already opened file, or an in-memory stream. By default, the JSON text is interpreted as UTF-8 text.
syntax: function long Json.read (long stream, ref string error_str [, long options])
returns: A JSON value, or 0 in case of an error.

name: Json.readFile
doc: Reads JSON text from a file, parses it and creates a JSON value from it. By default, the JSON text is interpreted as UTF-8 text.
syntax: function long Json.readFile (const string path, ref string error_str [, long options])
returns: A JSON value, or 0 in case of an error.

name: Json.readString
doc: Reads JSON text from a string, parses it and creates a JSON value from it. By default, the JSON text is interpreted as TSS text.
syntax: function long Json.readString (const string json_str, ref string error_str [, long options])
returns: A JSON value, or 0 in case of an error.

name: Json.set
doc: Associates a JSON value with a key in a JSON object. If the key does not yet exist, it is created first. If the key already exists, its current JSON value is deleted and replaced by the new value.
syntax: function long Json.set (long json_object, const string key, long json_value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON value which has been associated with the key.

name: Json.setBoolean
doc: Convenience function for directly associating a 3GL boolean value with a key in a JSON object. The 3GL boolean value is first converted to a JSON boolean value which is then associated with the specified key. Json.set(json, key, Json.newBoolean(value))
syntax: function long Json.setBoolean (long json_object, const string key, boolean value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON boolean value which has been associated with the key.

name: Json.setDouble
doc: Convenience function for directly associating a 3GL double value with a key in a JSON object. The 3GL double value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then associated with the specified key. Json.setNumber(json, key, value)
syntax: function [long] Json.setDouble (long json_object, const string key, double value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been associated with the key.

name: Json.setLong
doc: Convenience function for directly associating a 3GL long value with a key in a JSON object. The 3GL long value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then associated with the specified key. Json.setNumber(json, key, value)
syntax: function [long] Json.setLong (long json_object, const string key, long value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been associated with the key.

name: Json.setNull
doc: Convenience function for associating a JSON null value with a key in a JSON object. Json.set(json, key, Json.newNull())
syntax: function long Json.setNull (long json_object, const string key)
returns: Optional, the new JSON null value which has been associated with the key.

name: Json.setNumber
doc: Convenience function for directly associating a 3GL long or double value with a key in a JSON object. The 3GL long or double value is first converted to a JSON number value which is then associated with the specified key. Json.set(json, key, Json.newNumber(value))
syntax: function [long] Json.setNumber (long json_object, const string key, long|double value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON number value which has been associated with the key.

name: Json.setString
doc: Convenience function for directly associating a 3GL string value with a key in a JSON object. The 3GL string value is first converted to a JSON string value which is then associated with the specified key. Json.set(json, key, Json.newString(value))
syntax: function long Json.setString (long json_object, const string key, const string value)
returns: Optional, the new JSON string value which has been associated with the key.

name: Json.string
doc: Returns the 3GL string value of a JSON string value.
syntax: function string Json.string (long json_value)
returns: The string contained in the JSON string value.

name: Json.stringAt
doc: Convenience function for directly returning the 3GL string value of the JSON string value that is stored at the specified index in a JSON array. Json.string(Json.at(json, idx))
syntax: function string Json.stringAt (long json_array, long idx)
returns: The 3GL string value stored at the specified index.

name: Json.type
doc: Returns the type of a JSON value.
syntax: function long Json.type (long json_value)
returns: The type of the JSON value. One of { JSON_TYPE_OBJECT, JSON_TYPE_ARRAY, JSON_TYPE_BOOLEAN, JSON_TYPE_NUMBER, JSON_TYPE_STRING, JSON_TYPE_NULL, JSON_TYPE_UNKNOWN }.

name: Json.write
doc: Writes a JSON value to a stream as JSON text. This can be an already opened file, or an in-memory stream. By default, the JSON text is converted to UTF-8 and the output is written in compact mode (ie. no whitespace is added between JSON tokens).
syntax: function long Json.write (long json_value, long stream [, long options])
returns: >= 0: the number of bytes written to the stream when successful < 0: in case of a failure [e.g. when the string to write to is too small] variable 'e' contains an error code, [e.g. ENOSPC]

name: Json.writeFile
doc: Writes a JSON value to a file as JSON text. By default, the JSON text is converted to UTF-8 and extra new-lines and indents are added to make the output human readable.
syntax: function long Json.writeFile (long json_value, const string path [, long options])
returns: >= 0: the number of bytes written to the string when successful < 0: in case of a failure [e.g. when the string to write to is too small] variable 'e' contains an error code [e.g. ENOSPC]

name: Json.writeString
doc: Writes a JSON value object to a string as JSON text. By default, no UTF-8 conversion is done and no additional formatting is done.
syntax: function long Json.writeString (long json_value, ref string str [, long options])
returns: >= 0: the number of bytes written to the string when successful < 0: in case of a failure [e.g. when the string to write to is too small] variable 'e' contains an error code, [e.g. ENOSPC]

name: keyfields.to.object
doc: Store the current value of the key fields to the passed key field object.
syntax: function void keyfields.to.object (long object)
returns: void

name: keyin$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This reads the first character from the keyboard buffer. If there is no character in the buffer, the function waits until one is entered. If you include the optional argument, the function performs a non-blocking read. If there is no character in the buffer, the function returns immediately with an empty string. This form of the function is used for interrupting a batch process when the user presses a key. The function converts the following function keys to ASCII characters: Key — Ascii LEFT ARROW — BS — 8 — ^H RIGHT ARROW — FF — 12 — ^L UP ARROW — VT — 11 — ^K DOWN ARROW — LF — 10 — ^J INSERT — EM — 25 — ^Y
syntax: function string keyin$ ( [long flag])
returns: The character read from the event queue. If the returned string contains multiple bytes, the character is a multi-byte character. If the character is a function that cannot be converted, the function returns an empty string.

name: kill
doc: This deletes the specified process from the bshell process queue. If the process is in a running state, it is interrupted.
syntax: function void kill (long processno)
returns: void

name: kill.pgrp
doc: This ends all processes within the specified process group. All windows and graphical parts of the processes are removed.
syntax: function void kill.pgrp (long process_id)
returns: void

name: kill.timer
doc: This ends a specified timer.
syntax: function void kill.timer (long timer_id)
returns: void

name: l.expr
doc: Executes (or evaluates) an expression previously compiled by expr.compile(). The result is always converted to a long.
syntax: function long l.expr (long expr_id [, void value] [, boolean suppressError])
returns: The result of the expression converted to an integer value. Notice that signed 64-bit values are used for integer arithmetic in runtime expression evaluation. In older porting sets (with bshell TIV level less than 2000), signed 32-bit values are used for integer arithmetic in runtime expression evaluation. If the resulting integer value is greater than the maximum value 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) - 1 of the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range, then that maximum value is returned. If the resulting integer value is less than the minimum value -2^( BitCountOfLong-1) of the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range, then that minimum value is returned.

name: last.window
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This places the specified window below all other windows on the screen. The window is also placed at the last position in the internal window stack. The alterations become visible on screen only when you call refresh() or wrebuild().
syntax: function void last.window (long wind_id)
returns: void

name: len
doc: This function returns the length in characters (character count) of the supplied string argument. len() and len.in.bytes().
syntax: function long len (string value)
returns: This function returns the length in characters (character count) of the supplied string argument. Notice that, regarding the character count, there is a difference between a single-byte string value and a multi-byte string value.

name: len.in.bytes
doc: This function returns the length in bytes (byte count) of the supplied string argument. len.in.bytes() and len().
syntax: function long len.in.bytes (string value)
returns: This function returns the length in bytes (byte count) of the supplied string argument. Notice that, regarding the byte count, there is no difference between a single-byte string value and a multi-byte string value.

name: lf$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to send one or more line feeds to the screen or printer. The cursor is moved down num_expr lines. If you do not specify a number of lines, the cursor is moved down one line.
syntax: function string lf$ ( [long num_expr])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: load.byte
doc: The function load.byte() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The byte read from the string is interpreted as the 8-bit binary representation of an unsigned integer value. The load.byte() function is machine independent and can be used (for example) in network communications.
syntax: function long load.byte (string record$)
returns: The numerical value of the first byte of the supplied string. This is a value in the unsigned 8-bit range [0 … 2^8 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 255]).

name: load.double
doc: The function load.double() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes, without trying to interpret that sequence of bytes as the encoding of a sequence of characters. Instead, the bytes are interpreted as the encoding of numerical values. The function load.double returns the numerical value of the first eight bytes of the supplied string, interpreted as the eight-byte encoding of a floating point value. The load.double() function is not machine independent and must be used with care in (for example) network communications.
syntax: function double load.double (string record$ [, long swap])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: load.float
doc: The function load.float() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes, without trying to interpret that sequence of bytes as the encoding of a sequence of characters. Instead, the bytes are interpreted as the encoding of numerical values. The function load.float returns the numerical value of the first four bytes of the supplied string, interpreted as the four-byte encoding of a floating point value. The load.float() function is not machine independent and must be used with care in (for example) network communications.
syntax: function double load.float (string record$ [, long swap])
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: load.long
doc: The function load.long() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The 4 bytes read from the string are interpreted as the 32-bit two’s complement representation of a signed integer value. The load.long() function is machine independent and can be used (for example) in network communications.
syntax: function long load.long (string record$ [, long endian])
returns: The numerical value of the first 4 bytes of the supplied string. This is a value in the signed 32-bit range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]).

name: load.short
doc: The function load.short() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The 2 bytes read from the string are interpreted as the 16-bit two’s complement representation of a signed integer value. The load.short() function is machine independent and can be used (for example) in network communications.
syntax: function long load.short (string record$ [, long endian])
returns: The numerical value of the first 2 bytes of the supplied string. This is a value in the signed 16-bit range [-2^15 … 2^15 - 1] (i.e. [-32,768 … 32,767]).

name: load.utc
doc: The function load.utc() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The bytes read from the string are interpreted as the two’s complement representation of a signed integer value. The load.utc() function is machine independent and can be used (for example) in network communications.
syntax: function long load.utc (string record$ [, long endian] [, long byte.count])
returns: The numerical value of the bytes read from the supplied string. This is a value in the signed byte.count-byte range [-(256^ byte.count)/2 … (256^ byte.count)/2 - 1]. Typically, this is a (non-negative) UTC long format value stored earlier by the function store.utc(), or prepared by any other means. This function does not perform any value check.

name: load_dll
doc: This loads a specified DLL. You can use it in combination with get_function() and exec_function() to call and execute a function in a DLL. These three functions provide a fast algorithm for accessing a function that is to be executed more than once. You load the DLL and function only once and can then execute the function any number of times. load_dll() returns an identification number that the other functions use to identify a particular DLL. You can also use load_dll() to replace one or more functions within a DLL by overloading a different DLL containing functions with the same names and arguments. But note that once a function has been loaded from a DLL, that DLL cannot subsequently be overloaded. For a full discussion on function overloading, see Function overloading.
syntax: function long load_dll (string dll_name [, long overload])
returns: > 0 — DLL identifier. 0 — Error; DLL not found or No license to run object

name: local.to.utc
doc: This converts a local date and time to UTC long format. Input values for local date and time must be in the signed 32-bit value range.
syntax: function long local.to.utc (long local_days, long local_time, ref long utc [, string local_dst])
returns: 0 — Success. The supplied reference argument utc now contains the UTC value of the supplied local date and time. -1 — Error. The supplied reference argument utc is unchanged. The cause of the error may be one of the following. The exact result is negative. The exact result is greater than the maximum value 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) - 1 of the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range. The optional argument local_dst is not supplied and the ( local_days, local_time) combination is in the skipped range at the begin of a DST period. See the Daylight Saving Time handling section and the examples below.

name: local.with.timezone.info.to.utc
doc: This converts a local date and time to UTC long format. For the conversion, it will NOT use the timezone of the user, but the difference in seconds to UTC as supplied in the variable utcdiff. Input values for local date and time must be in the signed 32-bit value range.
syntax: function long local.with.timezone.info.to.utc (long local_days, long local_time, long utcdiff, ref domain ttutc utc)
returns: 0 — Success. The supplied reference argument utc now contains the UTC value of the supplied local date and time. -1 — Error. The exact result is negative or greater than the maximum value 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) - 1 of the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range. The supplied reference argument utc is unchanged.

name: log
doc: This computes the natural logarithm of x. The value of x must be greater than zero.
syntax: function double log (double x)
returns: The log of x.

name: log10
doc: This computes the base 10 logarithm of x. The value of x must be greater than zero.
syntax: function double log10 (double x)
returns: The base 10 log of x.

name: lower.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This moves the specified object to the bottom of the object stack on the workspace.
syntax: function void lower.object (long object_id)
returns: void

name: lpow
doc: This computes the value of x raised to the power of y. The y argument must be positive.
syntax: function long lpow (long x, long y)
returns: The value of x^y, (i.e. x to the power of y). If y is zero, the return value is always 1. When the exact resulting value is outside the signed BitCountOfLong-bit value range, then the result is undefined.

name: ltob
doc: Cast a long to a boolean.
syntax: function boolean ltob (long long_value)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: ltoe
doc: This returns the named constant corresponding to a specified numeric code. The numeric code represents one of the values in an enumerated domain.
syntax: function domain ltoe (long long_value)
returns: This returns the named constant corresponding to a specified numeric code.

name: lval
doc: This function performs explicit string to long type conversion. If the resulting value is within the limits of the signed BitCountOfLong-bit range, that value is returned. Otherwise, the concerned bound is returned.
syntax: function long lval (string string$)
returns: Condition on exact conversion result — Description — Value returned by lval >= -2^( BitCountOfLong-1) and < 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) — success — exact conversion result < -2^( BitCountOfLong-1) — lower bound is applied — -2^( BitCountOfLong-1) >= 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) — upper bound is applied — 2^( BitCountOfLong-1) - 1

name: main
doc: See syntax: function main()
syntax: function main()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: make.current
doc: This reads the current main table record and displays it on screen. Calling this function is similar to calling execute(find.data), except that if the specified record is not present, make.current() does not read the next record.
syntax: function void make.current ()
returns: void

name: make.path.absolute
doc: Makes path absolute given in path_name. It gives the full path back also in path_name.
syntax: function long make.path.absolute (ref string path_name)
returns: 0 — Success. other value — Errror.

name: map.add.info
doc: Add an info object to a route point. An info object will be shown as a tooltip when the user hovers the mouse pointer over a route point icon.
syntax: function long map.add.info (long rpid, string title)
returns: <> 0 — A new info object id. 0 — When this function fails.

name: map.add.infoline
doc: Add a new line to an info object.
syntax: function void map.add.infoline (long infoid, string label, string value)
returns: void

name: map.add.legendline
doc: Add a line to to the legend explaining the meaning of an icontype.
syntax: function void map.add.legendline (long mid, string label, string icontype)
returns: void

name: map.add.point
doc: Add a new point to the map at the given position. The order in which points are added to the map determines the route order.
syntax: function long map.add.point (long mid, double lat, double lon, string icontype)
returns: <> 0 — A new point object id. 0 — When this function fails.

name: map.create
doc: Create a new map object.
syntax: function long map.create ()
returns: <> 0 — A new map object id. 0 — When this function fails.

name: map.delete
doc: Delete a map object which was created with map.create().
syntax: function void map.delete (long mid)
returns: void

name: map.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This makes the specified object visible, without changing the order of the objects on the workspace.
syntax: function void map.object (long object_id)
returns: void

name: map.show
doc: Show or update the map. When no map is currently visible a new map session window will be started. When this map is already visible, its content will be updated. The map session window will be brought into view.
syntax: function void map.show (long mid, string title)
returns: void

name: map.window
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This makes the specified window visible, without changing the order of the windows.
syntax: function void map.window (long wind_id)
returns: void

name: mark.handler
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This enables a user to mark one or more records on an ASCII form. On return, the mark.table argument indicates which records are marked. Each element in the mark.table array corresponds to a record on the form. If an array element is set to 1, the corresponding record is marked. If it set to 0, the corresponding array element is not marked. The predefined variables marked and mark.status are not affected by this function.
syntax: function long mark.handler (ref long mark.table())
returns: 0 no records marked 1 one or more records marked

name: mark.occ
doc: This marks the specified occurrence with a reverse bar, makes the marked record the current record in the database, and sets the predefined variable actual.occ to the marked occurrence. For sessions with TIV lower than TIV 1075 the following predefined variables are relevant to this function: marked — Use this to check whether an occurrence is marked or not. This can also be tested in the on.exit subsection of a zoom process. This is available in the subsections before.choice and after.choice of choice.mark.occur. It indicates the type of marking that the 4GL engine is executing. It can have the following values: DUPL.OCCUR during marking for copying TEXT.MANAGER during marking for edit text 0 in all other cases and when not marking mark.status For sessions with TIV TIV 1075 or higher see the Form and form field operations synopsis for an overview of related functions and variables.
syntax: function void mark.occ (long occurence)
returns: void

name: max
doc: This compares the values of the two arguments and returns whichever is the greatest. The arguments can be of type long or double or can contain any numeric expression.
syntax: function double max (double x, double y)
returns: The greatest of the two values.

name: mb.cast$
doc: This function converts a specified string to a multi-byte string. The content of the string remains the same.
syntax: function string mb.cast$ (string string_expres)
returns: The multi-byte string.

name: mb.cast.to.str$
doc: This function converts a specified string to a single-byte string. The content of the string remains the same.
syntax: function string mb.cast.to.str$ (string string_express)
returns: The single-byte string.

name: mb.char
doc: This function tests whether a specified code point represents a single-byte character, a multi-byte character, or something else. It is mainly used in conjunction with the next.event() function, which returns a character as a long value.
syntax: function long mb.char (long code_point)
returns: Return value — Code point range — Description 2 — [0x9b000000 … 0x9bffffff] — The supplied value is the code point of a multi-byte TSS character. 1 — [1 … 0xff] — The supplied value is the code point of a non-zero single-byte TSS character. 0 — 0 — The supplied value is zero. [0x100 … 0x9affffff] — The supplied value is not the code point of any TSS character, but may indicate some non-character key (for example, a function key). [0x9c000000 … 0xffffffff] — The supplied value is not expected and is assessed as ‘not the code point of any TSS character’. In earlier versions of the bshell (before bshell TIV level 2340), the supplied value was assessed as the code point of a multi-byte TSS character (return value 2).

name: mb.char.info
doc: This function identifies the character set to which a TSS-encoded character belongs. It returns the character set ID for the first character in the specified string. In TSS, due to the phenomenon of unification, it is not in all cases clear to which character set a character belongs. This function tries all available character sets in a certain order and returns the ID of the first encountered character set containing a character that reasonably might have been mapped to the first character of the supplied string.
syntax: function long mb.char.info (string tss_string$)
returns: The ID of the character set for the first character in the specified string. Or -1 if ch$ is an empty string or if the TSS character could not be found in one of the TSS character sets. For the same character, different calls of this function can give different results. The search order is not the same for every call of mb.char.info. The character set resulting from a successful call of mb.char.info occurs early in the search order of the next call of mb.char.info. Also the character set of the current locale occurs early in the search order of each call.

name: mb.coerce.to.sb
doc: This function converts a string from the TSS character set to the external, native character set, assuring that each resulting character is a single byte. By default, the setting of the current user locale (single-byte or multi-byte environment) or the installation locale (Unicode environment) determines the character set to which the string is converted. Code features in the string are skipped. This function may be used when a string containing multi-byte characters must be assigned to a single-byte string. Note that the conversion may result in ambiguous high ascii characters (see TSS Encoding).
syntax: function long mb.coerce.to.sb (ref string string$ [, long setid])
returns: >= 0 — The number of bytes in the result string. -1 — The conversion failed because some character could not be converted, or some converted character is not a single byte.

name: mb.display
doc: This function returns that part of a specified string that fits in a specified display space. The substring is equal to the source string if the source string fits in the display space. If one or more characters do not fit in the display space, a ghost character (default is >) is appended to the substring.
syntax: function long mb.display (string string_expr, ref string substr$, long space [, long flags])
returns: An index to omitted characters if the string is truncated. Otherwise, the length of the string.

name: mb.export$
doc: This function converts a string from the TSS character set to the external, native character set. By default, the setting of the current locale determines the character set to which the string is converted. Code features in the string are skipped.
syntax: function long mb.export$ (ref string target$, string source$ [, long setid])
returns: Note: This can be an indication of an overflow condition! If the supplied buffer is too small, the number of output bytes that fits in the supplied buffer is returned, with no clear indication of the overflow condition. This behaviour is retained for compatibility reasons. Make sure your output buffer is of sufficient size to hold the resulting string. >= 0 -1 — An incomplete character was found at the end of the string, or an illegal code sequence was detected. -3 — Character could not be converted.

name: mb.export.raw
doc: This function converts a string from the TSS character set to the external, native character set. By default, the setting of the current locale determines the character set to which the string is converted. This function is almost identical to mb.export$(), but in contrast to that function, no special conversion is done for code features in source$.
syntax: function long mb.export.raw (ref string target$, string source$ [, long setid])
returns: >= 0 — The number of converted bytes. -1 — The target string was too small to contain the converted string. -2 — An incomplete character was found at the end of the string. -3 — Character could not be converted.

name: mb.hasbidi
doc: Deprecated. This function is supported for backward compatibility reasons only. As of object TIV level 2200 (specified with the -T option of the compiler) using this function will trigger a compilation error.
syntax: function boolean mb.hasbidi (string string_expres)
returns: FALSE

name: mb.import$
doc: This function converts a string from the external, native character set to the TSS character set. By default, the setting of the current locale determines the native character set from which the string is converted. Code features are restored.
syntax: function long mb.import$ (ref string target$, string source$ [, long setid])
returns: >= 0 — The number of converted bytes. -1 — The target string was too small to contain the converted string. -2 — An incomplete character was found at the end of the string. -3 — Character could not be converted.

name: mb.import.raw
doc: This function converts a string from the external, native character set to the TSS character set. By default, the setting of the current locale determines the native character set from which the string is converted. Unlike mb.import$(), no special conversion is done for Code Features.
syntax: function long mb.import.raw (ref string target$, string source$ [, long setid])
returns: >= 0 — The number of converted bytes. -1 — The target string was too small to contain the converted string. -2 — An incomplete character was found at the end of the string. -3 — Character could not be converted.

name: mb.isbidi
doc: This function checks whether the current environment is a bidirectional one.
syntax: function boolean mb.isbidi ()
returns: TRUE current environment is bidirectional FALSE current environment is not bidirectional

name: mb.isbidi.language
doc: This function checks whether the specified language is a bidirectional one. To use the function, you must link to the ttdllbidi library. The function checks the flag ‘ %TF@ttaad110.bidi’ in the table ‘%TB@ttaad110’.
syntax: function boolean mb.isbidi.language (string lang)
returns: TRUE current language is bidirectional FALSE current language is not bidirectional

name: mb.locale.enumerate
doc: This function returns information about one specific locale or about all locales.
syntax: function long mb.locale.enumerate (const string locale.name$)
returns: An XML tree containing the requested information. Like any other XML tree, the returned tree must be freed from memory by using xmlDelete. When the supplied argument locale.name$ refers to a not existing locale, e.g. "abcdefg", then the returned xml tree looks like this: <enumeration type="locales" name="abcdefg" /> When the supplied argument refers to an existing locale, e.g. "ISO88591_WIN32", then the returned xml tree looks like this: <enumeration type="locales" name="ISO88591_WIN32"> <locale name="ISO88591_WIN32" nlsname="NULL" tssname="CP1252" tss_characterset_id="7" internal_factor="1" external_factor="1" multibyte="false" language_group="Latin1" /> </enumeration> When the supplied argument locale.name$ is an empty string "", then the returned xml tree contains a <locale> node for each existing locale, and looks like this: <enumeration type="locales"> <locale name="GB2312_WIN32" nlsname="chs" tssname="CP936" tss_characterset_id="17" internal_factor="2" external_factor="2" multibyte="true" language_group="Simplified Chinese" /> <locale name="ISO88591" nlsname="NULL" tssname="ISO88591" tss_characterset_id="0" internal_factor="1" external_factor="1" multibyte="false" language_group="Latin1" /> ... etcetera ... <locale name="ISO_BIN5" nlsname="NULL" tssname="ISO88595" tss_characterset_id="23" internal_factor="1" external_factor="1" multibyte="false" language_group="Cyrillic" /> </enumeration> The 'name' attribute corresponds to the locale name as returned by mb.localename$(). The five attribute names 'name', 'nlsname', 'tssname', 'internal_factor', and 'external_factor' correspond to the five values 'TSS_GET_LOCALE_NAME', 'TSS_GET_NLS_NAME', 'TSS_GET_TSS_NAME', 'TSS_GET_IFACTOR', and 'TSS_GET_EFACTOR' of the flag supplied to the function mb.locale.info(). The attributes 'tss_characterset_id' and 'tssname' correspond to the first two arguments of mb.set.info(). The attribute 'tss_characterset_id' corresponds to the value returned by mb.char.info() and to the optional third argument of mb.import$(), mb.import.raw(), mb.export$(), and mb.export.raw(). The attribute 'multibyte' indicates if the locale has a multi-byte native encoding. All locales that share a common character set have the same 'language_group' attribute.

name: mb.locale.info
doc: This function returns information about the current locale.
syntax: function string mb.locale.info (long info_flag [, const string locale_name])
returns: A string containing the requested information. Where applicable, lval() can be used to convert the string to a long.

name: mb.localename$
doc: This function returns the name of the current locale as defined in the file '$bse/lib/user/u< user >'. The file ‘$BSE/lib/tss_locale x.x ’ (where x.x is the bshell version) contains all locales that the system supports.
syntax: function string mb.localename$ ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: mb.long.to.str$
doc: This function returns a single-character string corresponding to the supplied TSS code point.
syntax: function string mb.long.to.str$ (long code_point)
returns: A string containing exactly one character, specifically the character determined by the specified code point. Code point range — Description of the return value [0 … 0xff] — In the context of the function mb.long.to.str$, all code point values in the considered range are regarded as valid, except code point 0x9b (the lead-byte value for four-byte TSS sequences). For valid code point values the resulting string is a single-byte string; the supplied code point is encoded as a single byte; in most cases the byte limit of the result is 1; however, the byte limit of the result is 0 for code point 0 (the code point of the NULL character, usually interpreted as the end of the string value and as such not part of the string value). For code point 0x9b the result is left unspecified and may change in the future. [0x100 … 0x9affffff] — In the context of the function mb.long.to.str$, all code point values in the considered range are regarded as invalid. For these code point values, the behavior of this function is left unspecified and may change in the future. [0x9b000000 … 0x9bffffff] — For valid code point values in the considered range the resulting string is a multi-byte string; the supplied code point is encoded as a four-byte sequence; the byte limit of the result is 4. For other code point values, the behavior of this function is left unspecified and may change in the future. In the context of the function mb.long.to.str$, a code point value in the considered range is regarded as valid when the last three bytes of the resulting four-byte sequence are non-zero; notice that the first byte is 0x9b. [0x9c000000 … 0xffffffff] — In the context of the function mb.long.to.str$, all code point values in the considered range are regarded as invalid. For these code point values, the behavior of this function is left unspecified and may change in the future. Notice that for valid code point values the behavior of mb.long.to.str$ is very similar to that of chr$. For invalid code point values the behavior of mb.long.to.str$ is left unspecified and, above that, may be different from that of chr$.

name: mb.nsets
doc: This function returns the number of TSS character sets currently defined. This is useful for retrieving character set information using mb.set.info().
syntax: function long mb.nsets ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: mb.rev$
doc: Deprecated. This function is supported for backward compatibility reasons only. As of object TIV level 2200 (specified with the -T option of the compiler) using this function will trigger a compilation error.
syntax: function string mb.rev$ (string string_expr [, long flags])
returns: The supplied string_expr.

name: mb.scrpos
doc: This function converts a string position to a screen position. Code features are ignored.
syntax: function long mb.scrpos (string string_expr, long pos)
returns: The screen position corresponding to the specified string position. Or -1 if pos lies beyond the end of the string.

name: mb.set.info
doc: This function returns information about a specified character set.
syntax: function long mb.set.info (long setid, ref string name, string desc, ref long n_items)
returns: 0 success -1 the set ID is not linked to a known character set

name: mb.strpos
doc: This function converts a screen position to a string position. Code features are ignored.
syntax: function long mb.strpos (string string_expr, long pos)
returns: The string position corresponding to the specified screen position. Or -1 if pos lies beyond the end of the string.

name: mb.type
doc: This function tests whether the supplied value is a multi-byte string (or string array). It only tests the type of the supplied value, not its content.
syntax: function long mb.type (void value)
returns: 0 — the supplied value is neither of type multi-byte string nor of type multi-byte string array. 1 — the supplied value is of type multi-byte string or of type multi-byte string array.

name: mb.width
doc: This function returns the display width of a specified string; that is, the number of positions the string will occupy on the screen. A single-byte character has a display width of 0 or 1 screen positions. A multi-byte character has a display width of 0 or 1 or 2 screen positions.
syntax: function long mb.width (string string_expres)
returns: The display width of the specified string.

name: mess
doc: This retrieves a message from the data dictionary and displays it on screen. Using this function makes your program script language independent.
syntax: function void mess (string messcode, long separate_window [, void arg ...])
returns: void

name: message
doc: This displays the specified message string on screen in a separate window, and waits until the user closes it. This is applicable in case the message mode of the concerning user is set to "Interactive". In case of a "Non-interrupting" message mode, Infor Enterprise Server displays the message strings in a separate "Messages" window without interruption.
syntax: function void message (string mess_str [, void arg ...])
returns: void

name: method.is.allowed
doc: This is a special hook for handling centralized authorizations. Use it to perform checks that determine whether certain Data Access Methods are permitted for an object. The method argument specifies the method to check.
syntax: function boolean method.is.allowed (long method)
returns: TRUE if the method is permitted FALSE if the method is not permitted

name: min
doc: This compares the values of the two arguments and returns whichever is the smallest. The arguments can be of type long or double or can contain any numeric expression.
syntax: function double min (double x, double x)
returns: The lesser of the two values.

name: mkdir
doc: This creates the specified directory. You must have write permission in the parent directory to do this. Access permissions for the new directory are set to read, write, and execute for all users.
syntax: function long mkdir (string path_name$ [, long access_level])
returns: >= 0 — Success. (If the return value is 0 then you can be sure that the directory existed already.) < 0 — Error. The error code is stored in the e variable.

name: ml_get_baselang
doc: Returns the base language of the environment.
syntax: function string ml_get_baselang ()
returns: the base language of the environment, or "" in case Multi Language support is inactive

name: ml_get_datalang
doc: Returns the current data language of the user.
syntax: function string ml_get_datalang ()
returns: the current data language of the user, or "" in case Multi Language support is inactive

name: ml_get_datalang_of_softlang
doc: Returns the data language of the specified software language.
syntax: function string ml_get_datalang_of_softlang (const string softlang)
returns: the data language of the specified software language, or "" if no data language defined for the specified software language

name: ml_is_active
doc: Tests whether Multi Language support is active on runtime for the current environment.
syntax: function boolean ml_is_active ()
returns: TRUE — Multi Language support is active. FALSE — Multi Language support is inactive.

name: ml_one_lang
doc: This function retrieves the value in a specific data language from a string variable.
syntax: function string ml_one_lang (const string mlv [, const string language])
returns: The value in the specified data language'. If the optional argument 'language' is not specified: the value in the 'current data language' This function can be used in SQL as well, to select values in just one language from the database.

name: ml_set_datalang
doc: Sets a new data language for the user.
syntax: function long ml_set_datalang (const string datalang)
returns: 0 — OK <> 0 — Error

name: monitor_add_field
doc: Adds or replaces a field to an existing monitor event/interval class. A field is like a metric, but all events of a class have the same value for this field. A field differs from a tag in that it doesn’t identify the event, it just provides supplementary information. Furthermore, a field is not restricted to string for its type.
syntax: function long monitor_add_field (long event_class_id, const string field_name, void field_value)
returns: On success — Returns 0. On failure — Returns an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_class monitor_error_invalid_field_name monitor_error_invalid_field_type

name: monitor_add_metric
doc: Adds or replaces a metric to an existing monitor event/interval class.
syntax: function long monitor_add_metric (long event_class_id, const string metric_name, long metric_type)
returns: On success — Returns 0. On failure — Returns an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_class monitor_error_invalid_field_name monitor_error_invalid_field_type

name: monitor_add_tag
doc: Adds or replaces a tag to an existing monitor event/interval class.
syntax: function long monitor_add_tag (long event_class_id, const string tag_name, const string tag_value)
returns: On success — Returns 0. On failure — Returns an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_class monitor_error_invalid_tag_name monitor_error_invalid_tag_value

name: monitor_define_event_class
doc: Creates a monitor event class. The class will contain the tags as defined in the BSE. In addition, the monitoring system may afterwards add some tags to each event, such as account, region or host.
syntax: function long monitor_define_event_class (const string event_class_name)
returns: On success — Returns a number > 0, which identifies the monitor event class which has been created. On failure — No monitor event class is created, and the function returns a number < 0, possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_invalid_class_name

name: monitor_define_interval_class
doc: Creates a monitor interval class. A monitor interval class is a special monitor event class, which has 1 additional metric (‘duration’), the value for this metric is automatically determined, being the time (in seconds, with millisecond granularity) between the start of a timer and the actual occurrence of the event.
syntax: function long monitor_define_interval_class (const string interval_class_name)
returns: On success — Returns a number > 0, which identifies the monitor interval class which has been created. On failure — No monitor interval class is created, and the function returns a number < 0, possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_invalid_class_name

name: monitor_event
doc: An event will be reported to the monitoring system. The event will be off the class identified and contains all tags and fields as defined for this class. In addition, the metrics which are given in this call will be added to the reported event.
syntax: function long monitor_event (long event_class_id, void ...)
returns: On success — The event will be reported, and the function returns 0. On failure — No event will be reported and the function returns an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_class monitor_error_unknown_field monitor_error_missing_field_value monitor_error_field_value_of_wrong_type monitor_error_invalid_field_value

name: monitor_remove_event_class
doc: Removes an event class. When this function succeeds, subsequent use of this event class id will result in a monitor_error_unknown_class error.
syntax: function long monitor_remove_event_class (long event_class_id)
returns: On success — Returns 0. On failure — Returns an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_class

name: monitor_remove_interval
doc: Removes an interval. When this function succeeds, subsequent use of this interval id will result in a monitor_error_unknown_interval error.
syntax: function long monitor_remove_interval (long interval_id)
returns: On success — Returns 0. On failure — Returns an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_interval

name: monitor_remove_interval_class
doc: Removes an interval class. In addition to the interval class itself, all associated intervals are removed as well. When this function succeeds, subsequent use of this interval class id will result in a monitor_error_unknown_class error.
syntax: function long monitor_remove_interval_class (long interval_class_id)
returns: On success — Returns 0. On failure — Returns an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_class

name: monitor_start_interval
doc: Start a timer for an interval of the indicated class.
syntax: function long monitor_start_interval (long interval_class_id)
returns: On success — The interval will be remembered, and the function returns the interval id (value > 0). On failure — No timer will be started, nor will an interval be remembered. The function will return an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_class

name: monitor_stop_interval
doc: An interval event will be reported to the monitoring system. The event will be off the interval class the interval identified belongs to, and contains all tags and fields as defined for this interval class. In addition, the metrics which are given in this call will be added to the reported event.
syntax: function long monitor_stop_interval (long interval_id [, void ...])
returns: On success — The interval event will be reported, the interval will be forgotten, and the function returns 0. On failure — No event will be reported, nor will the interval be forgotten. The function returns an error code (value < 0), possible values are: monitor_not_enabled monitor_error_unknown_interval monitor_error_unknown_class monitor_error_unknown_field monitor_error_missing_field_value monitor_error_field_value_of_wrong_type monitor_error_invalid_field_value

name: move.window
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This moves the current window to a specified position (relative to the top left corner of the parent window). There is no need to refresh the window.
syntax: function void move.window (long col, long row)
returns: void

name: mtime
doc: This measures the time elapsed since the first mtime() call. The function is common to all processes within the same bshell. That is, when it is called by a process, the result is the number of milliseconds since the function was first called by a process in the same bshell.
syntax: function long mtime ()
returns: The first call returns 0. Subsequent calls return the number of milliseconds since the first call. A negative value is returned if an error occurs.

name: ncrs.is.session.empty
doc: This function can be used in a print or a processing session in an init.form section. The function can be used to decide whether the functional default command should be triggered. Possible the default command is another one, than the command that actually trigges the wanted functionality. The function tells whether the session has no fields left, because the selection group has been made invisible.
syntax: function boolean ncrs.is.session.empty ()
returns: TRUE No fields are left, session won't be shown FALSE Session will be shown

name: new.window
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This creates a new window. The new window automatically becomes the current window.
syntax: function long new.window (long height, long width, long row, long col)
returns: The window ID for the new window.

name: no.scroll
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This disables scrolling for the specified window.
syntax: function void no.scroll (long wind_id)
returns: void

name: not.curr
doc: This switches the current and previous values of the specified variable. This is considered a value change by the checking mechanism. So if you subsequently call changed(), that function will return TRUE.
syntax: function void not.curr (string variable)
returns: void

name: not.fixed
doc: You can fill a string with or without specifying a start position. If you specify a start position, unused positions in the string are filled with spaces. You can prevent the string from being filled out with spaces by calling not.fixed() before filling the string. Note that, when you assign a new value to the string variable, positions after the new value are not changed.
syntax: function void not.fixed (string string_var)
returns: void

name: num.to.date
doc: This converts a specified number of days since 01-01-0001 to the corresponding year, month, and day of the month.
syntax: function long num.to.date (long dayno, ref long yearno, ref long monthno, ref long month_dayno)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error.

name: num.to.date$
doc: This converts a specified number of days since 01-01-0001 to the corresponding date, formatted as a date string. The sequence of day, month, and year in the string depends on the user data settings defined in the data dictionary (default is "YYMMDD"). The separator character used is also defined in the data dictionary (default is '/').
syntax: function string num.to.date$ (long dayno, long mode)
returns: The formatted date string. Or an empty string if an error occurs.

name: num.to.week
doc: This converts a specified number of days since 01-01-0001 to the corresponding day of the week, day of the year, and week number of the year.
syntax: function long num.to.week (long dayno, ref long week_dayno, ref long year_dayno, ref long weekno [, ref long yearno])
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error.

name: object.to.keyfields
doc: Restore the value of the key fields from the passed key field object.
syntax: function void object.to.keyfields (long object)
returns: void

name: occ.independent.view.field
doc: This defines the specified field as occurrence independent. This means that its value is not stored in one of the records that is shown in the grid. An example is an order total field that is shown in the grid. Another example is a field that is used to filter out records. Occurrence independent fields are treated in a special way. When normal fields get input, the update.status and choice variables will be set (if they do not already have a value) and the record will be locked (delayed lock). This is not the case for occurrence independent fields, which makes them perfectly suitable for e.g. filtering functionality.
syntax: function void occ.independent.view.field (string field.name)
returns: void

name: off.change.check
doc: This switches off the checking mechanism for the specified variable. Changes to the variable are no longer monitored by the checking mechanism.
syntax: function void off.change.check (string variable)
returns: void

name: on.change.check
doc: This starts the checking mechanism by setting a checkpoint for the specified variable. The current value of the variable becomes the checkpoint value.
syntax: function void on.change.check (string variable)
returns: void

name: on.drop
doc: Call back function which is passed in function enable.drop(). This function will be called when a drop event from the associated session arrives. In this function the business logic related to the drop operation must be implemented. In case database table updates are done in this function, the function must also commit the transaction.
syntax: function void on.drop (long from.pid, long collection, boolean copy)
returns: void

name: on.main.table
doc: This copies the contents current record of the main table to the record buffer of that table, saves the record, and executes the specified function. After that the saved record buffer is restored. This enables you to perform actions on the record contents without affecting the values in the table.
syntax: function void on.main.table (string function_name [, string ...])
returns: void

name: on.old.occ
doc: This executes the specified function for the current occurrence, using the old values of the record. The record must have been previously modified.
syntax: function void on.old.occ (const string function_name, const string ...)
returns: void

name: on.recall
doc: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL, is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any changes made to the Business Object must be recalled, the DBCM layer will execute this hook. This hook must then publish a Workflow BOD to ION with a request to recall a previous request for approval. Note: This hook should only be implemented for root tables.
syntax: function long on.recall ()
returns: In case of success. 0 In case of a failure. DALHOOKERROR

name: on.reject
doc: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any submitted changes made to the Business Object have been rejected in ION, the DBCM layer will execute this hook. Note: This hook should only be implemented for root tables.
syntax: function long on.reject ()
returns: In case of success. 0 In case of a failure. DALHOOKERROR

name: on.set.approved
doc: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any submitted changes made to the Business Object have been approved in ION, the DBCM layer will execute this hook. This hook will be called after the Business Object has been checked-in. Note: This hook should only be implemented for root tables.
syntax: function long on.set.approved ()
returns: In case of success. 0 In case of a failure. DALHOOKERROR

name: on.set.draft
doc: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any submitted changes made to the Business Object have been approved in ION, the DBCM layer will execute this hook. This hook will be called after the Business Object has been checked-out. Note: This hook should only be implemented for root tables.
syntax: function long on.set.draft ()
returns: In case of success. 0 In case of a failure. DALHOOKERROR

name: on.set.recalled
doc: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case a previous request to recall a started Workflow in ION is confirmed, the DBCM layer will execute this hook. Note: This hook should only be implemented for root tables.
syntax: function long on.set.recalled ()
returns: In case of success. 0 In case of a failure. DALHOOKERROR

name: on.submit
doc: This hook is executed in case Workflow Document Authorization is active for the Business Object of which the table of this DAL, is the root table, as defined in the OCM Workflow Model. In case any changes made to the Business Object are submitted, the DBCM layer will execute this hook. This hook must then publish a Workflow BOD to ION with a request for approval. Note: This hook should only be implemented for root tables.
syntax: function long on.submit ()
returns: In case of success. 0 In case of a failure. DALHOOKERROR

name: open.message
doc: Use this to create a new mailbox or to connect to an existing mailbox. You must call this function before you can read from or write to the mailbox.
syntax: function long open.message (long project, string name$, long action [, long fast])
returns: This returns a unique key for the opened mailbox. It returns -1 if an error occurs (the predefined variable e contains the error number).

name: open.url.local
doc: This function opens a URL in an (embedded) browser. This function is only supported in WebUI and LN UI.
syntax: function boolean open.url.local (string url, long mode [, string dialog.title] [, string dialog.message] [, string browser.title] [, string redir.param] [, ref long params.node])
returns: true — Browser application started successfully. false — iBrowser application failed to start.

name: ostype
doc: This function returns a long value that indicates the operating system environment. The possible values are: OS_WINDOWS_NT — All Windows variants. OS_UNIX — All UNIX variants
syntax: function long ostype ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: par.abort.client.server
doc: This function can be used in the client as well in the server. When there are (application) problems in the client or server, an abort message will be sent to the client and all servers. After this function call, all servers are stopped and all communication will be ended.
syntax: function void par.abort.client.server (string error.message)
returns: void

name: par.client.close.servers
doc: This function will close all servers in a group. Normally this call should only be done when all servers are ready, so after a call to par.client.wait.ready(). Closing the servers means that the application servers will terminate.
syntax: function boolean par.client.close.servers (long group.id)
returns: true — When successful false — When an error occurred

name: par.client.get.message
doc: This function will check if a message has been sent by one of the servers in the indicated server group. A server process can sent a message back to the client with the function: par.server.send.message(). This function will not wait for any messages from a server process.
syntax: function long par.client.get.message (long group.id, ref string comm.string)
returns: 0 — When no message is received (so no message was sent by any server) > 0 — Server number from which this message is received.

name: par.client.get.status
doc: Returns the current status of the specified server.
syntax: function long par.client.get.status (long group.id, long server.number, ref long messages)
returns: This function returns the current state of this server, which can be one of the following STATE_SRV_CLOSED — Initial state after par.init.client.to.server() was called STATE_SRV_LISTEN — par.client.start.servers() called, waiting for connect from server STATE_SRV_KNOWN — Server called: par.init.server.to.client() STATE_SRV_IDLE — Server ready to accept a new message and waiting in par.server.get.message() STATE_SRV_PROCESSING — Server busy processing a message. STATE_SRV_QUESTION — Server waiting in function par.server.question() STATE_SRV_CLOSING — par.client.close.servers() called, waiting for server to close STATE_SRV_ERROR — Server in error state -1 — Invalid group id or group already closed

name: par.client.running
doc: This function will return whether the current session is running in parallel processing client mode. It will be true when function par.init.client.to.server() was called successfully. This function can be useful in DLL’s.
syntax: function boolean par.client.running ()
returns: true — Session is running in parallel processing client mode false — Session is not running a parallel processing client mode

name: par.client.send.message
doc: Send a message to the indicated group or application server. When a server.number is passed, the message is sent to that particular server. Otherwise the message is sent to the first server in the group which is ready. This function will wait until the message has been sent to a server. This does however not mean that the message is already processed by this server when this function returns. When not in CONTINUE_ON_SERVER_ERRORS mode, this function will return false when one or more servers are in error state. When in CONTINUE_ON_SERVER_ERRORS mode the following rules are applied:
syntax: function boolean par.client.send.message (long group.id [, string comm.string] [, long server.number])
returns: true — When message was sent successfully false — When sending the message failed

name: par.client.start.servers
doc: This function is used to actually start the application servers (Bshells) for the indicated group.
syntax: function boolean par.client.start.servers (long group.id [, long options])
returns: true — When all application servers started successfully false — When one or more application servers could not be started

name: par.client.wait.ready
doc: This function will wait until servers are ready with processing messages. When no group.id and no server.number are specified, this function will wait for all servers in all groups to become ready. When only a group.id is specified, this function will wait for all servers in the specified group to become ready. When both a group.id and a server.number is specified, this function will wait for one specific server to become ready. When not in CONTINUE_ON_SERVER_ERRORS mode (this can be specified in par.client.start.servers()), this function will return false when one or more servers are in error state. When in CONTINUE_ON_SERVER_ERRORS mode the following rules are applied:
syntax: function boolean par.client.wait.ready ( [long group.id] [, long server.number])
returns: true — When successful false — When an error occurred

name: par.get.no.of.server
doc: This function will return the number of servers configured for this client session. See the section Parallel Application Processing Configuration.
syntax: function long par.get.no.of.server ()
returns: > 0 — number of servers configured for this client session <= 0 — session not configured for parallel processing operation

name: par.init.client.to.server
doc: This function is used to initialize the client to server communication for one group. Starting the application servers (Bshells) will be done when the function par.client.start.servers() is called.
syntax: function long par.init.client.to.server (long nr.of.servers, string server.session [, string support.session])
returns: > 0 — The id of the server group < 0 — When parallel processing is not configured for the current session and nr.of.servers is <= 0

name: par.init.server.to.client
doc: This function is used to initialize the communication to the client. This function must be called rather in the beginning of a program which can be started as server. This because of the fact that the client function has a time out time (default 2 minutes) on starting each server (receiving the 'known' command).
syntax: function boolean par.init.server.to.client (ref long group.number, ref long server.number [, ref long tot.nr.servers])
returns: true — When this session is running in parallel processing server mode. false — When this session is not running in parallel processing server mode.

name: par.server.get.message
doc: This function will inform the client that this server is ready and wait for a new message from the client.
syntax: function long par.server.get.message (ref string comm.string)
returns: 1 — a message is available in comm.string 0 — an error occurred -1 — the client called the function par.client.close.servers() to indicate that all servers should end processing and exit.

name: par.server.id
doc: This function will return the identification of a server within its group. This function can be useful in includes or DLL’s to determine if the session is running in the context of parallel processing.
syntax: function long par.server.id ()
returns: > 0 — The server number when the session is running in a parallel processing context 0 — Session is not running a parallel processing context

name: par.server.question
doc: This function can be used by a server session to send a question message to the "support" session in the client. The "support" session in the client must use function par.support.get.question() to receive questions from server processes and function par.support.send.answer() to sent an answer message to the server. The function par.server.question() waits until an answer message is received from the "support" session.
syntax: function boolean par.server.question (string question, ref string answer)
returns: true — when an answer is returned by the support session false — when an error occurred

name: par.server.retry.hit
doc: This function must be called in a server after a real db.retry.hit() call. When this function is called x times and x = MAX.RETRY-1, this function will do an abort of the client server communication with the abort message "Too many retry hits in server". See section: Parallel Application Processing Database Retries for a further explanation.
syntax: function void par.server.retry.hit ()
returns: void

name: par.server.retry.point
doc: This function is used for setting a not real retry point after a db.retry.point (). It must be used together with function par.server.retry.hit(). See section: Parallel Application Processing Database Retries for a further explanation.
syntax: function void par.server.retry.point ()
returns: void

name: par.server.running
doc: This function will return whether the current session is running in parallel processing server mode. It will be true when function par.init.server.to.client() was called successfully. This function can be useful in DLL’s.
syntax: function boolean par.server.running ()
returns: true — Session is running in parallel processing server mode false — Session is not running a parallel processing server mode

name: par.server.send.message
doc: Send a message to the client. This function will return as soon as the message has been sent. This function is not intended to sent a high volume of messages from the server to the client. This function is also not intended to ask the client for additional information during processing a client message.
syntax: function boolean par.server.send.message (string comm.string)
returns: true — when message was sent successfully false — when sending the message failed

name: par.support.get.question
