doc: This function will wait for a question message from any server. When this function returns -1, the support session must end processing and exit.
syntax: function long par.support.get.question (ref string question)
returns: > 0 — The server number which has sent the question string -1 — The client called the function par.client.close.servers() to indicate that all servers (and support sessions) should end processing and exit.

name: par.support.init
doc: This function is used to initialize the communication for a support session. This function must be called at the start of a session which can be used as a parallel processing support session. A session which acts as a parallel processing support session is used to handle questions from parallel processing servers. A parallel processing support session cannot at the same time be a parallel processing client session or a parallel processing server session. Usually a support session runs without a user interface. Therefore such a session must call function tc.ignore.process() during startup.
syntax: function boolean par.support.init (ref long group.number, ref long tot.nr.servers)
returns: true — When this session is running in parallel processing support session mode. false — When this session is not running in parallel processing support session mode.

name: par.support.running
doc: This function will return whether the current session is running in parallel processing support session mode. It will be true when function par.support.init() was called successfully. This function can be useful in DLL’s.
syntax: function boolean par.support.running ()
returns: true — Session is running in parallel processing support session mode false — Session is not running a parallel processing support session mode

name: par.support.send.answer
doc: Send an answer message to a server session. This function will return as soon as the message has been sent. This function should only be used after a successful call of function: par.support.get.question()
syntax: function boolean par.support.send.answer (string answer, long server.number)
returns: true — when message was sent successfully false — when sending the message failed

name: parse_and_exec_function
doc: This function is similar to exec_dll_function(). It loads a specified DLL and parses and executes a specified function within that DLL. If the DLL is already loaded, the identification number of the loaded DLL is used to search for the specified function. Otherwise, a load_dll(dll_name, 0) call is executed automatically. Use this function only when the function and its arguments are known only at runtime. The function is intended for handing function calls received as strings from other processes.
syntax: function long parse_and_exec_function (string dll_name, string function_call [, ref void return_value] [, ref string return_call])
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error; DLL not found. -2 — Error; Function not found. -3 — Error; Syntax error in function call.

name: path.change.extension
doc: Changes the extension of the specified path string. By default the path string is interpreted according to the Operating System of the Infor Enterprise Server server. OS_WINDOWS_NT .
syntax: function string path.change.extension (const string path, const string extension [, long os.type])
returns: The modified path information. If path is an empty string (""), the extension (with a leading period) is returned. If extension is an empty string, the returned string contains the specified path with its extension removed. If path has no extension, and extension is not empty, the returned path string contains extension appended to the end of path.

name: path.combine
doc: Combines one ore more strings into a path. OS_WINDOWS_NT .
syntax: function string path.combine (const string path, ..., long os.type)
returns: The combined paths. path.combine path.combine("c:\", "*.txt")

name: path.dir.separator
doc: Provides a platform-specific character used to separate directory levels in a path string that reflects a hierarchical file system organization. If Infor Enterprise Server is running on UNIX, the returned directory separator is the forward slash ("/"); if Infor Enterprise Server is running on Windows, the returned directory separator is the backslash ("\"). By supplying the OS type this function will return the directory separator for the given OS type.
syntax: function string path.dir.separator ( [long os.type])
returns: The value is a slash ("/") for UNIX, and a backslash ("\") for the Windows operating systems.

name: path.directory
doc: Returns the directory information for the specified path string. OS_WINDOWS_NT .
syntax: function string path.directory (const string path [, long os.type])
returns: Directory information for path, or an empty string if path denotes a root directory or is empty, or if path does not contain directory information. path.dir.separator() path.directory() will result in "C:\Directory".

name: path.exists
doc: This function returns true if the given path exists, and false otherwise. If the current BSE is a tenant BSE, path is always interpreted as a relative path.
syntax: function boolean path.exists (const string path [, long access_level])
returns: True if the file or directory exists, false otherwise

name: path.extension
doc: Returns the extension of the specified path string. OS_WINDOWS_NT .
syntax: function string path.extension (const string path [, long os.type])
returns: The extension of the specified path (including the period "."), or an empty string. If path is an empty string, or if path does not have extension information, this function returns an empty string. path.dir.separator() character, the returned string contains the period and the characters after it; otherwise, an empty string is returned.

name: path.filename
doc: Returns the filename and extension of the specified path string. OS_WINDOWS_NT .
syntax: function string path.filename (const string path [, long os.type])
returns: The characters after the last directory character in path. If the last character of path is a directory or volume separator character, this method returns an empty string. If path is an empty string, this function returns an empty string as well. path.dir.separator() .

name: path.filename.without.extension
doc: Returns the filename of the specified path string without the extension. OS_WINDOWS_NT .
syntax: function string path.filename.without.extension (const string path [, long os.type])
returns: path.filename() , minus the last period (.) and all characters following it. This method does not verify that the path or file name exists.

name: path.has.extension
doc: Determines whether a path string includes a file name extension. OS_WINDOWS_NT .
syntax: function boolean path.has.extension (const string path [, long os.type])
returns: true if the characters that follow the last directory separator (\ or /) in the path include a period (.) followed by one or more characters; otherwise, false. path.dir.separator() character is encountered, this method returns true.

name: path.is.absolute
doc: This checks if path_name is an absolute path.
syntax: function boolean path.is.absolute (string path_name)
returns: false — path_name is not absolute. true — path_name is absolute.

name: path.separator
doc: Returns a platform-specific separator character (":" or ";") used to separate path strings in environment variables. path.dir.separator() . If Infor Enterprise Server is running on UNIX, the returned separator is the colon (:); if Infor Enterprise Server is running on Windows, the returned separator is the semi-colon (;). By supplying the OS type this function will return the separator for the given OS type.
syntax: function string path.separator ( [long os.type])
returns: On Windows-based platforms, the value returned is the semicolon (;). On Unix platforms the value returned is the colon (:).

name: pathname
doc: This searches for and returns the location of a specified file. The function uses the file $BSE/lib/fd ver.pack_combination to find the file. ver refers to a particular release of the software; pack_combination refers to a particular package combination. It is not necessary to use this function within functions such as db.bind(). These also use the file $BSE/lib/fd ver.pack_combination to search for a path name.
syntax: function long pathname (string file_basename, string file_type, ref string file_path [, long log.options])
returns: 0 — Success. ENOENT — File not found.

name: pc$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to set certain printer codes. The following printer codes are available: 1 — paper bin 1 2 — paper bin 2 3 — paper bin 3 4 — paper bin 4 5 — landscape 6 — portrait 7 — usr1 8 — usr2 ... — ... 22 — usr16 You define codes 9 to 22 in the printer information file for the particular printer (for example, $BSE/lib/printinf/m/m290).
syntax: function string pc$ (long num_expr)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: pcm.activate.session
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This starts a specified 4GL session. It generates a new window for the session and ensures that it is handled correctly. You can use this function in combination with pcm.send.bms.event(), which sends changed values back to the application as events.
syntax: function long pcm.activate.session (ref string session, string title)
returns: The function returns the process ID of the activated session.

name: pcm.change
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this function to change the attributes of a specified chart.
syntax: function void pcm.change (long plan_id, ..., long flag, long value)
returns: void

name: pcm.change.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this function to change the attributes of an object that was created by pcm.create.object().
syntax: function void pcm.change.object (long plan_id, long object_id [, long flag] [, long value,])
returns: void

name: pcm.create
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This starts the Plan Chart Manager and creates a new chart with the specified attributes. It returns the variable plan_id, which is a unique identifier for the chart. You use plan_id in the other functions in order to identify the chart you want to work with.
syntax: function long pcm.create ( [long flag] [, long value,...])
returns: The function returns a unique ID for the new chart.

name: pcm.create.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This creates an object of the specified type – for example, a menu item, an activity, a relation, or a marker. The function returns the object_id, which in turn is used in the functions pcm.change.object() and pcm.destroy.object() to identify the particular object to be changed or deleted. The object_id is also used in submenus and with subactivities in order to indicate the parent of the menu or activity.
syntax: function long pcm.create.object (long plan_id, long object_type [, long flag] [, long value] [, long flag, value])
returns: The function returns a unique ID for the new object.

name: pcm.destroy
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This ends the specified plan chart and removes all associated settings and objects.
syntax: function void pcm.destroy (long plan_id)
returns: void

name: pcm.destroy.object
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This deletes the specified object.
syntax: function void pcm.destroy.object (long plan_id, long object_id)
returns: void

name: pcm.get.data
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. When the client application receives an event from the Plan Chart Manager, use this function to read the event.
syntax: function void pcm.get.data (long evt_type, ref string arglist,...)
returns: void

name: pcm.lock
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this function to lock and unlock the Plan Chart Manager (for example, when data is changed in a session).
syntax: function void pcm.lock (long plan_id, long lock)
returns: void

name: pcm.refresh
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This (re)draws the specified chart and updates the display with all new and changed objects.
syntax: function void pcm.refresh (long plan_id)
returns: void

name: pcm.send.bms.event
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this in a process started by pcm.activate.session() in order to send an event back to the application that started the session.
syntax: function void pcm.send.bms.event (long command, ref string arglist)
returns: void

name: pf$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to change the printer font settings. The following settings are available: 1 — large 2 — small 3 — middle 4 — dblwide 5 — nlq 6 — italic 7 — superscript 8 — subscript 9 — .font1 10 — font2 ... — ... 24 — font16 You define settings 9 to 24 in the printer information file of the particular printer (for example, $BSE/lib/printinf/m/m290).
syntax: function string pf$ (long num_expr)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: pipe.clearerr
doc: This resets the error and end-of-file indicators on the specified pipe.
syntax: function long pipe.clearerr (long pipe_id)
returns: 0: success -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.close
doc: This clears any buffers associated with the specified pipe and closes the file. Buffers allocated by the standard input/output system are also cleared. Note that pipe.close() is performed automatically when the process exits.
syntax: function long pipe.close (long pipe_id)
returns: -1: error -2: child process is not allowed to read/write anymore >= 0: exit value of child process (0 is OK)

name: pipe.eof
doc: This checks the end-of-file indicator on the specified pipe. Note that the end-of-file indicator lasts until the pipe is closed, unless you explicitly clear it by calling pipe.clearerr().
syntax: function long pipe.eof (long pipe_id)
returns: <> 0: end-of-file indicator read on specified pipe 0: end-of-file indicator not read

name: pipe.error
doc: This checks the error indicator on the specified pipe to determine whether an error has occurred when reading or writing to the pipe. Note that the error indicator lasts until the pipe is closed, unless you explicitly clear it by calling pipe.clearerr().
syntax: function long pipe.error (long pipe_id)
returns: <> 0: error has occurred when reading or writing to the pipe 0: no error has occurred

name: pipe.flush
doc: This writes any buffered data associated with a pipe to the related file. The stream remains open.
syntax: function long pipe.flush (long pipe_id)
returns: 0: success -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.gets
doc: This reads a maximum of one line from the specified pipe.
syntax: function long pipe.gets (ref string line, long nr_of_bytes, long pipe_id)
returns: 0: success -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.open
doc: This creates a UNIX process with the specified name and links an input and/or output stream to it. It returns a pointer to the pipe; this is used to identify the pipe in subsequent operations.
syntax: function long pipe.open (string pathnm, string openmode)
returns: >= 1: success; a pointer to the pipe is returned < 1: error; that is, the negative value of the system error (for example, for a permission error, the system returns 13 and the function returns -13, or if the internal table is full, the function returns -EAGAIN).

name: pipe.puts
doc: This writes data to the specified pipe. It automatically appends a newline character to the data.
syntax: function long pipe.puts (string line, long pipe_id)
returns: 0: success -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.read
doc: This reads a specified number of bytes from the specified pipe.
syntax: function long pipe.read (ref string buffer, long nr_of_bytes, long pipe_id)
returns: > 0: the number of bytes read 0: end-of-file -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: pipe.write
doc: This appends a specified number of bytes to the specified pipe.
syntax: function long pipe.write (string buffer, long nr_of_bytes, long pipe_id)
returns: > 0: the number of bytes written 0: end-of-file -1: error; most probably no connected stream on pipe_id

name: plcm.activity.action.performed
doc: Callback-function for when the activity is double-click upon.
syntax: function boolean plcm.activity.action.performed (const string activity.id)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.activity.deleted
doc: Callback-function for when the activity is about to be deleted in the UI.
syntax: function boolean plcm.activity.deleted (const string activity.id)
returns: True, when the delete is allowed. False, when the delete is not allowed.

name: plcm.activity.moved
doc: Callback-function for when the activity end-date and/or start-date have been changed in the UI.
syntax: function boolean plcm.activity.moved (string activity.id, long start.date, long end.date)
returns: True, when the move is allowed. False, when the move is not allowed.

name: plcm.add.activity
doc: Adds a child activity to an activity. This will cause the parent activity to be displayed as a summary bar.
syntax: function long plcm.add.activity (string parent.activity.id, string activity.id, string activity.name [, long start.date] [, long end.date] [, long completion.percentage])
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.activity.marker
doc: Adds a marker to an activity. The marker will be visualized by an icon.
syntax: function long plcm.add.activity.marker (string activity.id, long icon.id, long date_time, string tooltip, string legend.id)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.activity.property
doc: Adds a property to an activity. The property will be visualized as a column in the table part of the Gantt view.
syntax: function long plcm.add.activity.property (string property.id, string property.label)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.command
doc: Adds a custom command. This command will appear in the specific menu of the plan chart.
syntax: function long plcm.add.command (string command.id, string command.text [, enum ecatg] [, boolean command.checked])
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.constraint
doc: Adds a constraint between two activities.
syntax: function long plcm.add.constraint (string activity.id.from, string activity.id.to, long constraint.type)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.reservation
doc: Assigns an activity to a resource.
syntax: function long plcm.add.reservation (string activity.id, string resource.id)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.resource
doc: Adds a child resource to a resource.
syntax: function long plcm.add.resource (string parent.resource.id, string resource.id, string resource.name [, long quantity])
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.resource.property
doc: Adds a property to a resource. The property will be visualized as a column in the table part of the Schedule view.
syntax: function long plcm.add.resource.property (string property.id, string property.label)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.root.activity
doc: Call this function only once. The root activity will serve as highest level parent for all other activities. Therefore it will be displayed as summary bar in the Gantt view.
syntax: function long plcm.add.root.activity (string root.activity.id, string root.activity.name)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.add.root.resource
doc: Call this function only once. The root resource will serve as highest level parent for all other resources
syntax: function long plcm.add.root.resource (string root.resource.id, string root.resource.name)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.clear
doc: Clears the plan chart in order to build up a new schedule.
syntax: function long plcm.clear ()
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.command.performed
doc: Callback-function for when a "custom' command has been performed in the UI.
syntax: function long plcm.command.performed (string command.id, const long activities.context.count, const string activities.context(), const long resources.context.count, string resources.context())
returns: None.

name: plcm.constraint.deleted
doc: Callback-function for when the constraint is about to be deleted in the UI.
syntax: function boolean plcm.constraint.deleted (const string activity.id.from, const string activity.id.to, const long constraint.type)
returns: True, when the delete is allowed. False, when the delete is not allowed.

name: plcm.create.legend.entry
doc: Defines a legend entry. This function must be called before the plcm.start() is called. The legend will be visualized in the underneath the plan chart.
syntax: function long plcm.create.legend.entry (string legend.id, long color, string description)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.delete.activity
doc: Deletes an activity.
syntax: function long plcm.delete.activity (string activity.id)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.delete.constraint
doc: Deletes a constraint between two activities.
syntax: function long plcm.delete.constraint (string activity.id.from, string activity.id.to, long constraint.type)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.delete.reservation
doc: Deletes a reservation.
syntax: function long plcm.delete.reservation (string activity.id, string resource.id)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.delete.resource
doc: Deletes a resource.
syntax: function long plcm.delete.resource (string resource.id)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.get.default.availability
doc: Callback-function for the initial setting value of the show availability.
syntax: function boolean plcm.get.default.availability ()
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.get.resource.unavailability
doc: Callback-function when the scope of the view of unavailabilities of the resource is changed in the UI.
syntax: function void plcm.get.resource.unavailability (const string resource.id(), const long i.start.date, const long i.end.date)
returns: void

name: plcm.init
doc: This function must be the first to be called, it initializes the global data structures of the plan chart.
syntax: function long plcm.init (string title, string initial.types [, long options])
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.move.activity
doc: Sets a new start/end date for an activity
syntax: function long plcm.move.activity (string activity.id, long start.date, long end.date)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.reservation.changed
doc: Callback-function for when a reservation is about to change in the UI.
syntax: function boolean plcm.reservation.changed (const string activity.id., const string old.resource.id, const string new.resource.id)
returns: True, when the delete is allowed. False, when the delete is not allowed.

name: plcm.reservation.deleted
doc: Callback-function for when the reservation is about to be deleted in the UI.
syntax: function boolean plcm.reservation.deleted (const string activity.id, const string resource.id)
returns: True, when the delete is allowed. False, when the delete is not allowed.

name: plcm.resource.deleted
doc: Callback-function for when the resource is about to be deleted in the UI.
syntax: function boolean plcm.resource.deleted (const string resource.id)
returns: True, when the delete is allowed. False, when the delete is not allowed.

name: plcm.set.activity.completion.percentage
doc: Change the completion.percentage of an activity.
syntax: function long plcm.set.activity.completion.percentage (string activity.id, long completion.percentage)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.set.activity.end.date
doc: Change the end.date of an activity.
syntax: function long plcm.set.activity.end.date (string activity.id, long end.date)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.set.activity.name
doc: Change the name of an activity.
syntax: function long plcm.set.activity.name (string activity.id, string name)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.set.activity.property
doc: Sets an activity property. The property will be visualized in the table part of the Gantt view.
syntax: function long plcm.set.activity.property (string activity.id, string property.id, string property.value)
returns: 0 — Success

name: plcm.set.activity.property.date

name: pos
doc: This returns the start position of a specified substring ( part) in a specified string ( source). source and part can be either strings or string expressions. pos() starts searching for the substring at the first position in the source string. It returns the start position relative to the beginning of the source string. To start searching at the last position instead, use rpos(). As of TIV 1700, pos() can start the search at the specified offset. In this way it is possible to not only find the first occurrence of a substring, but also the next one(s). The returned start position is also in this case relative to the beginning of the source string. See the example below for how to use this optional parameter. The string effectively searched in is a substring from source, starting at offset. As of TIV 2200, an alternative to this function exists ( str_pos()), which finds the same parts in the source string as pos() does, but always returns a start position in the source which can be used as offset in the source string. For more information see str_pos().
syntax: function long pos (string source, string part [, long offset])
returns: The start position of the substring in the string. Or 0 if the substring is not found.

name: pow

syntax: function double pow (double x, double y)
returns: The value of x to the power of y. If y is zero, the return value is always 1.0

name: prcm.bms.is.notification

name: prcm.notify

It is also possible to pass some data to the observer processes in the form of an XML document. Observer processes then have read-only access to this XML document.

name: print.const

If you do not include the fill_string argument, the field is filled with asterisk characters (*). If the argument is a string of length one, the field is filled with the specified character. If the argument is a string of length greater than one, the specified string is displayed in the field, without repetition. The maximum length for the string is 127 characters.

name: publish.check
doc: This function checks whether a destination (bus component) is available for publishing events. Note that publish.open() and publish.message() will not always report errors, but will send messages to an error handler or log file instead. To avoid publishing many message to the error handler or log file, this check function can be used before using publish.open().

name: publish.error.message
doc: This function reports an error instead of publishing a message. It can be used if a message could not be created or sent successfully. Note that the error message is not sent to the bus component as specified in publish.open(). Instead, the Adapter configuration specifies an error handler for the bus component and the error message is sent to that error handler. If the error handler cannot be found or is unavailable, the Adapter will take care that the error is logged.
syntax: function long publish.error.message (long publication.id, long error.xml, ref long result.xml)
returns: 0 — success. <> 0 — an error value (this only occurs if the functionality is unavailable in the current Adapter version)

name: publish.message

returns: 0 — Error. <> 0 — Publication id to be used subsequently in publish.message(), publish.error.message() and publish.close()

name: qss.search
doc: This searches a specified array for a particular value, which is referred to as the search key. By default, it reads the array sequentially until it finds the specified value (that is, it performs a linear search). To perform a binary search instead, you must first sort the data, for example with qss.sort() and then call qss.search() with the flag argument set to QSS.SRC.IS.SORTED. If the same search key occurs more than once, then you should also specify the QSS.SRC.DUPL.ALLOWED option, or else it is not predictable which one of the duplicate records is found.
syntax: function long qss.search (long flag, void search, const void array, const long def(,) [, long dept])
returns: > 0 — index in the array where the search key was found -1 — error; search argument not found -11 — search argument must be of same type as array; def is not of type long array or array not of type array -12 — search argument not correct; string not expected -13 — dept must be positive -14 — def argument not correctly declared -15 — search argument does not fit in declared array -16 — QSS.TYPE not correct -17 — array argument not correct -18 — no definition found in def -21 — flag LOOKUP.FOR.STRUCT is used; search argument must be a string -22 — search argument not correct; probably a size problem - size of search must match size of an element in array if LOOKUP.FOR.STRUCT is set or (if LOOKUP.FOR.STRUCT is not set) must be at least the sum of lengths of the key fields (set by qss.length()) -23 — search argument not correct; probably a type problem

name: qss.sort
doc: This function performs a fast sort of a specified array. Note that the order in the result array of two elements that compare identical is unpredictable.
syntax: function long qss.sort (ref void array, const long def(,) [, long dept])
returns: 0 — success -1 — error, array and/or def is empty -11 — def is not of type long array or array not of type array -12 — array of strings must have > 1 dimension -13 — dept must be positive -14 — def argument not correctly declared -15 — def size exceeds array size -16 — QSS.TYPE not correct -17 — array argument not correct -18 — no definition found in def

name: query.extend.fld.from
doc: With the query.extend.fld… interface the metadata is stored in the 4gl engine. The query.extend.fld… information is used to build the standard query for retrieving requested data, inclusive the application fields. The result is used for the display of the field. The value of easy filter on the application field and the query.extend.fld… information is used to extend the WHERE clause of the standard query. The standard query is used to display the session. Use this to construct a query extension for the FROM clause of a database query. This expression will be added to the standard query for retrieving the column as form field. ( see query.extend.fld.select() or query.extend.fld.where()) You can use this function in the section before.program.
syntax: function long query.extend.fld.from (string select_column, string extension_string)
returns: 0 — On success. <> 0 — error

syntax: function long query.extend.fld.parm (string select_column, string parameter)
returns: 0 — On success. <> 0 — Error -1 — Qrycol not supported (application version must be at least 10.4 or tiv portingset is not 2030 or higher.) -2 — Unknown parameter value -3 — Query.extend.fld for columnName not present

name: query.extend.fld.select
doc: With the query.extend.fld… interface the metadata is stored in the 4gl engine. The query.extend.fld… information is used to build the standard query for retrieving requested data, inclusive the application fields. The result is used for the display of the field. The value of easy filter on the application field and the query.extend.fld… information is used to extend the WHERE clause of the standard query. The standard query is used to display the session. SQL expression for the SELECT clause of a column. This expression will be added to the standard query for displaying the column as form field. ( see query.extend.fld.from() or query.extend.fld.where()) You can use this function in the section before.program.
syntax: function long query.extend.fld.select (string select_column, string select_expression)
returns: 0 — On success. <> 0 — error

name: query.extend.fld.where
doc: With the query.extend.fld… interface the metadata is stored in the 4gl engine. The query.extend.fld… information is used to build the standard query for retrieving requested data, inclusive the application fields. The result is used for the display of the field. The value of easy filter on the application field and the query.extend.fld… information is used to extend the WHERE clause of the standard query. The standard query is used to display the session. SQL expression for the WHERE clause of the select column. This expression will be added to the standard query for selecting the rows. The query query.extend.fld... functionality is based on the main table of the session. All the used references must be defined. Existing relations in the session can be used as template, but must be added. The reason to declare all used references is the existing of them. With personalize form and possibility to change (overwrite) the present reference the reference can be removed from the standard query. Defining a reference more then once is taken in account. ( see example query.extend.fld.select() or query.extend.fld.from()) You can use this function in the section before.program.
syntax: function long query.extend.fld.where (string select_column, string where_condition)
returns: 0 — On success. <> 0 — error

name: random
doc: This function uses a system-independent random number generator. On all systems, the generator will generate the same random numbers, provided that the same seed is supplied. Calls to this function return successive random numbers in the range 0 to 32767. The function uses a multiplicative congruential random number generator, with period 2^32. The default seed is 1. To use a different seed, call srand() before starting the generator.
syntax: function long random ()
returns: A random number.
