name: rdi.format.digits
doc: This returns information about a specified format.
syntax: function long rdi.format.digits (string format(), ref long digits.before, ref long digits.after [, ref string display.format()])
returns: 0 success -1 error

name: rdi.index
doc: This returns information about a specified index.
syntax: function long rdi.index (string table_name(9), long index_no, ref long parts(32, 3), ref boolean duplicate, ref boolean active)
returns: The number of filled parts.

name: rdi.is.application.column
doc: This function checks whether the given column is an application column, or one that is automatically added by tools. Indices, combined fields, rcd_utc, and _compnr (among others) are not considered to be application columns by this function. Either only the first, or all parameters must be specified. The optional parameters can be used to prevent this function from calling rdi.table() and rdi.column() again when that was already done by the application. DB.CDF flag parameter returned by rdi.column() or rdi.table.column()
syntax: function boolean rdi.is.application.column (const string column.name [, long column.type] [, long column.offset] [, long table.real.length])
returns: True if the column is a regular application column, false if the column is one that is automatically added by tools.

name: rdi.reference
doc: If a database column references a column in another table, use this function to retrieve information about the referenced column.
syntax: function long rdi.reference (string column_name(18), ref string ref_column(18), ref long ref_mode, ref string ref_mess() [, ref boolean check_by_db] [, ref long ref_update_mode] [, ref long ref_delete_mode])
returns: 0 success -1 error

name: rdi.report.sensitivity
doc: Returns sensitivity of current report if no reportname was specified, otherwise the given reportname is used.
syntax: function long rdi.report.sensitivity (const string reportname)
returns: A value of 0 means that the report is not sensitive. A value of 1 - 99 is the sensitivity level. A value of < 0 or > 99 indicates an error.

name: rdi.session.sensitivity
doc: Returns sensitivity of current session. The function rdi.session.sensitivity also checks all table fields on a form (if any). The returned sensitivity is the highest sensitivity applicable to a session of table field on a form.
syntax: function long rdi.session.sensitivity ()
returns: A value of 0 means that the session is not sensitive. A value of 1 - 99 is the sensitivity level. A value of < 0 or > 99 indicates an error.

name: rdi.table
doc: This returns information about a specified table.
syntax: function long rdi.table (string table_name(9), ref long no_keys, ref long no_columns, ref long int_length, ref long real_length [, ref long no_cdf] [, ref boolean mlf_table_all_languages])
returns: 0 success -1 error

name: rdi.table.column
doc: This returns information about a specified column which is identified by the table name and the column number. Note that the first columns in the table are reserved for the following columns: Refcntd, Refcntu, _compnr, _dlock, and _index<number> (one column for each index).
syntax: function long rdi.table.column (string table_name(9), long column_number, ref string column_name, ref string domain_name(14), ref long offset, ref long size, ref long dept, ref long type, ref long flag, ref string default_value [, long flag_filter])
returns: 0 success -1 error

name: rdi.table.referenced
doc: This returns information about columns referring to this table.
syntax: function long rdi.table.referenced (string table_name(9), long referring_index, ref string referring_column_name(18), ref long ref_mode)
returns: 0 success -1 index too high -2 error

name: rdi.tablefield.sensitivity
doc: Returns sensitivity of the provided table field.
syntax: function long rdi.tablefield.sensitivity (const string tablefield)
returns: A value of 0 means that the report is not sensitive. A value of 1 - 99 is the sensitivity level. A value of < 0 or > 99 indicates an error.

name: reactivate
doc: This activates the specified sleeping process.
syntax: function void reactivate (long processno)
returns: void

name: rebuild.query
doc: Use this function to rebuild a query. If the query.extend functions are used the default query should be rebuild. This is done automatically after the before.program and the before.open.object.set sections. If these functions are used in other sections (to adjust them dynamically), the 4GLE has to be informed when the query has to be rebuild.
syntax: function void rebuild.query ()
returns: void

name: receive.bucket$
doc: This waits for a bucket message to be sent to the calling process by another process. It then returns that message. The processno argument returns the process ID of the sending process.
syntax: function string receive.bucket$ (long processno)
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: recv.message
doc: This reads a message from the specified mailbox. The process must previously have connected to the mailbox by calling open.message().
syntax: function long recv.message (long key, long sender.key, long time, ref string message$ [, long fast])
returns: This returns the sender key. It returns -1 if an error occurs (the predefined variable e contains the error number).

name: refresh
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This copies the internal screen to the terminal screen. The internal screen is modified by any function which sends data to the screen (for example, print(), box(), map.window()). The terminal screen is updated only after you call refresh(). If you specify a window ID, the specified window is refreshed. But the window sequence is not changed. If you do not specify a window ID, the current window is refreshed and placed above all other windows on the screen.
syntax: function void refresh ( [long wind_id])
returns: void

name: refresh.all.occs
doc: This re-reads all records that are currently on the screen and refreshes them (after all processes are idle). Note that this is not done in the following cases: This function works in both overview and details sessions. This function does not work in display sections.
syntax: function void refresh.all.occs ()
returns: void

name: refresh.curr.occ
doc: This reads the current record and refreshes it on screen. All references on the form are read again. For example, in the case of a zoom from a field to a session where the record can be modified, calling refresh.curr.occ() refreshes the occurrence on the parent form also. Note that the function locks the record before reading it; this is necessary for delayed locks.
syntax: function void refresh.curr.occ ()
returns: void

name: refresh.graph
doc: This function forces the display of all graph fields based on the most recent data (the current record buffer, the calculations made based on the current record buffer) of the session. This function can be called by a form command or a field button and is typically called from the session that contains the graph field(s).
syntax: function void refresh.graph ()
returns: void

name: refresh.list.detail.list
doc: This function refreshes the list of a list-detail session. On an user update action the list is automatically updated. But if an update of a record is done outside the save action, on a form command action or in another session (satellite), the list is not automatically updated. In these situations this function can be used to refresh the list.
syntax: function void refresh.list.detail.list ()
returns: void

name: refresh.parent
doc: This refreshes the parent session of the current session. The occurrence parameter determines which ocurrence of the child session must be refreshed in the parent session. If -1 is passed to this function, the parent session will refresh all its occurrences.
syntax: function long refresh.parent (long occurrence)
returns: 0 The parent is refreshed -1 No parent process -2 Invalid occurrence specified

name: refresh.total.line
doc: This triggers the 4GL-Engine to execute the program section: on.display.total.line. This section is not called directly but after all other sections have been executed. This function can be useful when the total line must be updated immediately after a user action or a change of a field value. When this function is not used, the program section on.display.total.line is only called after reading a new set of records from the database.
syntax: function void refresh.total.line ()
returns: void

name: refresh.tree.detail.tree
doc: This function refreshes the tree of a tree-detail session. On an user update action on the detail session the tree is automatically updated. But if an update of a record is done outside the save action, on a form command action or in another session (satellite), the tree is not automatically updated. In that situation this function can be used to refresh the tree.
syntax: function void refresh.tree.detail.tree ()
returns: void

name: register.webpart.handler
doc: Registers a handler for the specified message type. When a message of this type is received from a webpart the specified function is called.
syntax: function void register.webpart.handler (const string type, const string handler)
returns: void

name: remove.field.from.view
doc: The view fields for a dynamic session are determined by the view-property of a field in the DFE or, in case of dynamic index switching, by the view column in the Available Indices by Session session. You can use this function to conditionally remove a field from the view-area. e.g. Based on the current index (the predefined variable session.current.index).
syntax: function void remove.field.from.view (const string fname)
returns: void

name: remove.form.commands
doc: This removes the specified form command(s). Form commands are identified either by a function name or a session code. There is no way to restore or create a new form command.
syntax: function void remove.form.commands (string command,...)
returns: void

name: remove.local.directory
doc: This deletes a specified directory on the client system.
syntax: function long remove.local.directory (string dirent)
returns: 0 — Success. <> 0 — Error. Probably directory not empty or no permission.

name: remove.local.file
doc: Deprecated. This deletes a specified file on the client system.
syntax: function long remove.local.file (string filename)
returns: >= 0 — Success. < 0 — Error; The negative value of the operating system error.

name: remove.mark
doc: This function clears the selection.
syntax: function void remove.mark ()
returns: void

name: remove.quick.flow
doc: This function can be used in the after.form.read section to remove the quick.flow support for one or more form commands. In this way the application script can decide to not support quick.flow based on a paremaeter.
syntax: function void remove.quick.flow (const string frmcmd, const string ...)
returns: void

name: remove.session.index
doc: This removes the specified session index. Session index is identified by a session index number as defined by the session. Removing session index 1 and removing the current active session index is not allowed. Active session index can be found with the variable curr.key
syntax: function long remove.session.index (long session.index)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Invalid session Index. Session index should be > 1 -2 — Invalid session Index. Not allowed to disable the current index

name: remove.textfields
doc: The text manager completely ignores the named text field(s) for this session.
syntax: function void remove.textfields (const string field.name.string [, const string ...])
returns: void

name: reset.numformat.symbols
doc: Reset the decimal sign and thousand separator to the user defined values. The user defined settings will be used from this moment on for all formatted numbers.
syntax: function void reset.numformat.symbols ()
returns: void

name: resize.window
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This resizes the current window. You must specify the new width and height in pixels. There is no need to refresh the window.
syntax: function void resize.window (long width, long height)
returns: void

name: restore.rcd.main
doc: This updates the main table with the contents of the buffer of the specified occurrence. It also makes the specified occurrence the current occurrence.
syntax: function void restore.rcd.main (long occurrence)
returns: void

name: rgb
doc: Use this to compose a color by specifying its red, green, and blue intensities. The intensities must be in the range 0 to 255.
syntax: function long rgb (long red, long green, long blue)
returns: A long which can be used as a color in graphical contexts such as windows, user interface controls, and so on.

name: rmdir
doc: This deletes the specified directory (local or remote). The path argument must include the full path to the directory, including the host name, where appropriate. For example: "host!c:\usr".
syntax: function long rmdir (const string spath [, boolean recursive])
returns: >= 0 — Success. < 0 — Error. The error code is stored in the e variable.

name: rnd.d
doc: This function uses a system-independent random number generator. On all systems, the generator will generate the same random numbers, provided that the same seed is supplied. Calls to rnd.d() return successive random numbers in the range 0.0 to 1.0. Use rnd.init() to specify a seed value before starting the random number generator. If you do not do this, the first result of rnd.d() is undefined.
syntax: function double rnd.d ()
returns: A random number in the range 0.0 to 1.0.

name: rnd.i
doc: This function uses a system-independent random number generator. On all systems, the generator will generate the same random numbers, provided that the same seed is supplied. Calls to rnd.i() return successive random numbers in the range 0 to 32767. You can specify a range argument if you want to limit the range further. The function then returns numbers in the range 0 to range- 1. Use rnd.init() to specify a seed value before starting the random number generator. If you do not do this, the first result of rnd.i() is undefined.
syntax: function long rnd.i ( [long range])
returns: A random number in the default or specified range.

name: rnd.init
doc: rnd.d() and rnd.i() use a system-independent random number generator to generate random numbers. On all systems, the generator will generate the same random numbers, provided that the same seed is supplied. rnd.init() resets the random number generator to the starting point specified by the seed argument (the seed can be any long value). If rnd.init() is not called before starting the generator, then the first results of rnd.d() and rnd.i() are undefined.
syntax: function void rnd.init (long seed)
returns: void

name: round
doc: This rounds a given value to a specified number of decimal places.
syntax: function double round (double value, long diga, long mode)
returns: The rounded value. Or the original value ( value) if an error occurs. Because the return value is of type double, the number of digits after the decimal sign is always 6. For example, round(1.345, 2, 1) returns 1.350000.

name: rpos
doc: This returns the start position of a specified substring ( part) in a specified string ( source). source and part can be either strings or string expressions. rpos() starts searching for the substring at the last position in the source string, searching backward. It returns the start position relative to the beginning of the source string. To start searching at the first position instead, use pos(). As of TIV 1700, rpos() can start the search at the specified offset. In this way it is possible to not only find the first occurrence of a substring, but also the next one(s). The returned start position is also in this case relative to the beginning of the source string. See the example below for how to use this optional parameter. The string effectively searched in is a substring from source, ending at offset. As of TIV 2200, an alternative to this function exists ( str_rpos()), which finds the same parts in the source string as rpos() does, but always returns a start position in the source which can be used as offset in the source string. For more information see str_rpos().
syntax: function long rpos (string source, string part [, long offset])
returns: The start position of the substring in the string. Or 0 if the substring is not found.

name: rprt_close
doc: This is a short version of brp.close(). It closes the report writer for the current report. You can use the function in a 4GL script in the subsection on.choice of the section choice.print.data. In this section, the predefined variable spool.report is available. This variable stores the name of the current report.
syntax: function void rprt_close ( [long mess_flag])
returns: void

name: rprt_open
doc: This is a short version of brp.open(). It has the same effect as: brp.open( spool.report, spool.device, 1 ) That is, it prints the current report to the default device. The predefined variables spool.report and spool.device store the names of the current report and default device respectively.
syntax: function long rprt_open ()
returns: > 0 an ID for the activated report 0 report could not be activated -1 spooler could not be opened

name: rprt_send
doc: This is a short version of brp.ready(). It has the same effect as: brp.ready( spool.report ) That is, it signals the report writer that a record is ready to be imported into the current report. The predefined variable spool.report stores the name of the current report.
syntax: function void rprt_send ()
returns: void

name: rsc.boolean
doc: These convert a specified program variable to the corresponding resource value format (boolean, double, enum, and so on).
syntax: function void rsc.boolean (string variable)
returns: void

name: rsc.font.spec
doc: This returns a string that defines a font with the specified characteristics.
syntax: function string rsc.font.spec (long font_weight, long font_slant, long font_height, long font_points, long font_spacing, long font_width, long font_charwidth)
returns: A string that defines a font with the specified characteristics.

name: rsc.get
doc: See syntax: function void rsc.get (ref string values(), string package_code(2), string resource_set(16), string resource_id(24),...)
syntax: function void rsc.get (ref string values(), string package_code(2), string resource_set(16), string resource_id(24),...)
returns: void

name: rsc.put
doc: This updates one or more resource values in a specified resource set. You can use the following functions to convert program variables to a resource value format: rsc.boolean(), rsc.double(), rsc.enum(), rsc.long(), rsc.string(), rsc.boolean(), rsc.double(), rsc.enum(), rsc.long(), rsc.string(), rsc.boolean(), rsc.double(), rsc.enum(), rsc.long(), rsc.string(), rsc.boolean(), rsc.double(), rsc.enum(), rsc.long(), rsc.string(), and rsc.boolean(), rsc.double(), rsc.enum(), rsc.long(), rsc.string().
syntax: function void rsc.put (string package_code(2), string resource_set(16), string resource_id(16), value(40) [, string resource_id(16), value(40) . . .])
returns: void

name: rsc.setboolean
doc: These store a resource value of a particular type in a specified program variable.
syntax: function void rsc.setboolean (string variable, string value(40))
returns: void

name: run.baan.prog
doc: The function run.baan.prog() runs a program from $BSE/bin.
syntax: function long run.baan.prog (const string progname, const string arguments, long mode [, string stdin] [, string stdout] [, string stderr])
returns: 0: program executed successfully. When mode RP_NOWAIT was used, it means the program was started successfully. < 0: program could not be started. > 0: program did not execute successfully. Note that the return value cannot be retrieved when the mode argument is set to RP_NOWAIT.

name: run.prog
doc: The function run.prog() runs an operating system command. It is a system-dependent function. It must not be used in applications that are distributed across different platforms.
syntax: function long run.prog (const string progname, const string arguments, long mode [, string stdin] [, string stdout] [, string stderr])
returns: 0: program executed successfully < 0: program could not be started > 0: program did not execute successfully Note that the return value cannot be retrieved when the mode argument is set to RP_NOWAIT.

name: s.expr$
doc: Executes (or evaluates) an expression previously compiled by expr.compile(). The result is always converted to a string.
syntax: function string s.expr$ (long expr_id [, void value] [, boolean suppressError])
returns: The result of the expression converted to a string. You can execute compiled expressions multiple times without recompiling. The current values of the variables are used each time. Related topics

name: satellite.invisible
doc: This hides the specified satellite. This function can only be used in section: after.form.read. This function is relevant in multi-main table controller sessions only.
syntax: function void satellite.invisible (const string session.code)
returns: void

name: save.image.field
doc: This function is used to save an image, which is dropped onto the image control, into the repository or delete the image from the repository if deleted by the user. When an image with the bound guid already exists, it will be overwritten. This function should be called from the after.update.db.commit: section in a UI script and is only allowed when the image field is bound using bind.image()
syntax: function boolean save.image.field (string fieldname)
returns: true — When successful false — When an error occurred

name: save.image.file
doc: This function will save an image file into the image repository (put it at proper place in directory and update the image table). This function can be used by an image import application.
syntax: function boolean save.image.file (string guid, long sequence, string pathname [, string tablename])
returns: true — When successful false — When an error occurred

name: scroll
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This enables scrolling for the specified window. By default, windows do not scroll.
syntax: function void scroll (long wind_id)
returns: void

name: sel.add.parent.tables
doc: In the Dynamic Form Editor you can already indicate the main table of the parent session for which a session can handle the selection. You should specify that table at the "selection range group" in which the user can specify the range if the selection of the parent session is not used. Because you can only specify one table per group, you need to use this function if you want to add one or more extra tables to a group.
syntax: function boolean sel.add.parent.tables (long group_id, string parent_table)
returns: true Tables are added for the group with the specified number. false The supplied arguments are not of the right type, or the group with the specified number doesn't exist.

name: sel.num.selected
doc: This function returns the number of records that is selected in the session.
syntax: function long sel.num.selected ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: sel.parent.num.selected
doc: This function returns the number of records that is selected in the parent of the current session. If the number of records cannot be determined, -1 is returned. Note that this function returns the number of records that is selected in the parent session at the moment the function is called. If the selection changes because the parent is not blocked (the child is started modeless), the number is not valid anymore.
syntax: function long sel.parent.num.selected ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: sel.use.parent.selection
doc: This function can be used in a print or a processing session to determine whether to user wants to print/process based on a selection range, or based on the selection that is made in the parent. If the user wants to use the selection of the parent, you should use the function do.parent.selection() to get the selection. The user can indicate his choice with an optionset. Read below how to create that option set. Because the information is not available, you can not use this function in the before.program section.
syntax: function boolean sel.use.parent.selection (string parent_table)
returns: true User wants to use the selection of the given table. (This also means that the parent session has the given table as maintable.) false User wants to specify a custom range.

name: send.bucket
doc: This sends a bucket message to a specified process. If the specified process is sleeping, it is automatically started. It can retrieve the message by calling receive.bucket$().
syntax: function long send.bucket (long processno, string bucket)
returns: > 0: the process ID of the called process -1: error

name: send.message
doc: This stores a message in the specified mailbox. The process must previously have connected to the mailbox by calling open.message().
syntax: function long send.message (long dest.key, long sender.key, string message$, long fast)
returns: This returns 0 when successful. Otherwise it returns an error number.

name: send.wait
doc: This sends a bucket message to a specified process and waits for a reply. The receiving process must send a reply by using send.bucket() or send.wait(). Note that the waiting process cannot receive any message string contained in the reply.
syntax: function long send.wait (ref long processno, string bucket)
returns: > 0: the process ID of the process that sends the reply -1: error

name: seq.clearerr
doc: This resets the error and end-of-file indicators for the specified file. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the file was opened.
syntax: function long seq.clearerr (long fp)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Errror. Probably fp not connected

name: seq.close
doc: This flushes the buffers associated with the specified file and closes the file. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the file was opened. Buffers allocated by the standard i/o system are also flushed and closed. These actions are performed automatically when the process exits.
syntax: function long seq.close (long fp)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error. Probably fp not connected. (the last system error is available in the e variable - for example, for file system full, e will be ENOSPC (that is, 28) - for a list of error codes, see Infor ES errors and messages)

name: seq.close.local
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Instead you should use functions: server2client() or client2server(). This empties the buffers associated with the specified file and closes the file. If the remove.after.use flag was set when the file was opened, the file is removed after it is closed.
syntax: function void seq.close.local (long lfn)
returns: void

name: seq.eof
doc: This checks the end-of-file indicator of a specified file. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the file was opened. An end-of-file indication lasts until it is cleared by seq.clearerr() or until the file is closed.
syntax: function long seq.eof (long fp)
returns: 0 — End-of-file indicator not set. > 0 — End-of-file indicator set -1 — Error; probably fp not connected

name: seq.error
doc: This checks the error indicator of a specified file. The error indicator is set when an error occurs while reading from or writing to the file. It lasts until it is cleared by seq.clearerr() or until the file is closed. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the file was opened.
syntax: function long seq.error (long fp)
returns: 0 — Error indicator not set. > 0 — Error indicator set -1 — Error; probably fp not connected

name: seq.flush
doc: This causes all buffered data for a specified file to be written to that file. The file remains open. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the file was opened.
syntax: function long seq.flush (long fp)
returns: 0 — Success. > 0 — Error indicator set -1 — Error; probably fp not connected. (The last system error is available in the e variable – for example, for file system full, e will be ENOSPC (that is, 28) – for a list of error codes, see Infor ES errors and messages)

name: seq.fstat.local
doc: Deprecated. This retrieves information about a specified file on a client system.
syntax: function long seq.fstat.local (string filename, ref long nr.bytes)
returns: >= 0 — Success. -2: File not found -3: Path not found -5: Permission denied -32: Sharing violation See windows error codes (on MSDN, for example) for details on a specific error. < 0

name: seq.getc$
doc: This returns the next character from a specified file. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the file was opened. An empty string (a string of length 0) indicates either that the end-of-file has been reached or that an error has occurred.
syntax: function string seq.getc$ (long fp)
returns: This returns the next character from a specified file.

name: seq.gets
doc: This reads one or more characters from a specified file.
syntax: function long seq.gets (ref string line, long nrbytes, long fp [, long mode] [, ref long there.was.more])
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error; probably fp not connected or end of file reached.

name: seq.islocked
doc: This checks whether a specified file or segment of a file has been locked by seq.lock().
syntax: function long seq.islocked (long mode, long offset, long size, long fp)
returns: 0 — File or file segment not locked. <> 0 — File or file segment locked

name: seq.lock
doc: This sets read and write locks on a specified file or segment of a file.
syntax: function long seq.lock (long mode, long offset, long size, long fp)
returns: >= 0 — Success. -1 — Error; probably fp not connected. < -1 — Operating system error code.

name: seq.open
doc: This opens a specified file. It uses the file $BSE/lib/fd ver.pack_combination to find the file. ver refers to a particular release of the software; pack_combination refers to a particular package combination (see pathname()).
syntax: function long seq.open (string file, string openmode [, ref string pathnm])
returns: >= 1 — Success; File pointer returned for use in subsequent operations. < 1 — Error; that is, the negative value of the system error (for example, for a permission error, the system returns 13 and the function returns -13, or if the internal table is full, the function returns -EAGAIN).

name: seq.open.dialog.local
doc: Deprecated. This shows the Windows file-open dialog, to allow the user to select one or more local files.
syntax: function long seq.open.dialog.local (boolean mselect, string defaultname, string directory, string filter, ref string filename)
returns: > 0 — Number of files selected by the user. 0 — File open dialog canceled by the user. -1 — Error occurred

name: seq.open.dialog.next
doc: Deprecated. Retrieve the next full pathname of the file selected by the user in a previous seq.open.dialog.local() function. This function should only be used when a previous call to seq.open.dialog.local() returned a value greater than 1.
syntax: function long seq.open.dialog.next (ref string filename)
returns: true — Successfully retrieved next filename false — No more filenames to be retrieved

name: seq.open.local
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Instead you should use functions: server2client() or client2server(). This opens a specified file on the client system. It returns a file pointer, which you can use to identify the file in subsequent operations.
syntax: function long seq.open.local (string filename, string mode(2) [, long remove.after.use])
returns: >= 0 — Success. File pointer is returned. < 0 — Error. File could not be opened.

name: seq.putc$
doc: This writes a specified character to a specified file. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the particular file was opened.
syntax: function string seq.putc$ (string char, long fp)
returns: The character written to the file. Or an empty string (a string of length 0) if the end-of-file was reached or an error occurred. The last system error is available in the e variable – for example, for file system full, e will be ENOSPC (that is, 28) – for a list of error codes, see Infor ES errors and messages.

name: seq.puts
doc: This writes the specified characters to a specified file, and appends a new line character. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the particular file was opened.
syntax: function long seq.puts (const string line, long fp)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error; probably fp not connected (the last system error is available in the e variable – for example, for file system full, e will be ENOSPC (that is, 28) – for a list of error codes, see Infor ES errors and messages)

name: seq.r.long
doc: Reads a 32-bit value from the file. The 4 bytes read from the file are interpreted as the 32-bit two’s complement representation of a signed integer value.
syntax: function long seq.r.long (long fp)
returns: Error, most probably fp is not a valid file pointer or end-of-file was reached. The last system error is available in predefined variable e. Notice that this error value -1 cannot be distinguished from normal value -1. This is problematic, unless it is known that value -1 is not expected as a normal value to be read from the file. -1 >= -2^31 and < 2^31 — The numerical value of the 4 bytes read from the supplied file. This is a value in the signed 32-bit range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]).

name: seq.r.short
doc: Reads a 16-bit value from the file. The 2 bytes read from the file are interpreted as the 16-bit binary representation of an unsigned integer value.
syntax: function long seq.r.short (long fp)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably fp is not a valid file pointer. The last system error is available in predefined variable e. >= 0 — The numerical value of the 2 bytes read from the supplied file. This is a value in the unsigned 16-bit range [0 … 2^16 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 65,535]).

name: seq.r.utc
doc: Reads a specified amount of bytes from the file. The bytes read from the file are interpreted as the two’s complement representation of a signed integer value.
syntax: function long seq.r.utc (long fp [, long byte.count])
returns: Error, most probably fp is not a valid file pointer. The last system error is available in predefined variable e. Notice that this error value -1 cannot be distinguished from normal value -1. This is problematic, unless it is known that value -1 is not expected as a normal value to be read from the file. -1 The numerical value of the bytes read from the supplied file. Typically, this is a (non-negative) UTC long format value stored earlier by the function seq.w.utc(), or prepared by any other means. This function does not perform any value check. >= -(256^ byte.count)/2 and < (256^ byte.count)/2

name: seq.read
doc: This reads a specified number of bytes from a specified file into buffer. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the particular file was opened.
syntax: function long seq.read (ref string buffer, long nrbytes, long fp)
returns: > 0 — Number of bytes read. 0 — Either end of file encountered or the number of bytes to read was 0. -1 — Error; probably fp not connected.

name: seq.read.local
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Instead you should use function: client2server(). This reads a specified number of bytes from a specified file into buf.
syntax: function long seq.read.local (ref string buf, ref long size, long lfn)
returns: >= 0 — Success. < 0 — Error. Probably lfn not connected.

name: seq.rewind
doc: This sets the current file position to the beginning of the file. It is equivalent to: seq.seek() except that the return value is always -1 on error.
syntax: function long seq.rewind (long fp)
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error; probably fp not connected.

name: seq.saveas.dialog.local
doc: Deprecated. This shows the Windows file save-as dialog, to allow the user to select a new or existing local file to be saved.
syntax: function long seq.saveas.dialog.local (string defaultname, string directory, string filter, ref string filename)
returns: 1 — One file selected by the user. 0 — File save-as dialog canceled by the user. -1 — Error occurred

name: seq.seek
doc: This changes the current file position.
syntax: function long seq.seek (long offset, long opt, long fp)
returns: >= 0 — Success. Returns new position in bytes from the beginning of the file. < 0 — Error; probably fp not connected. Current file position is not changed.

name: seq.skip
doc: This skips nrbytes bytes, relative to the current file position, in a file represented by fp. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the particular file was opened. It is equivalent to: seq.seek().
syntax: function long seq.skip (long nrbytes, long fp)
returns: >= 0 — Success. Returns new position in bytes from the beginning of the file. < 0 — Error; probably fp not connected. Current file position is not changed.

name: seq.tell
doc: This returns the current file position, relative to the beginning of the file. The file position is measured in bytes. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the particular file was opened. Take care when using this function on files that have been opened in append mode (that is, with the openmode argument set to a or a+). Before calling seq.tell(), always call seq.flush() after you have written to the file with seq.write().
syntax: function long seq.tell (long fp)
returns: >= 0 — Success. < 0 — Error; probably fp not connected.

name: seq.ungetc$
doc: This puts back a specified character, retrieved by seq.getc$(). The character will be returned by the next seq.getc$() call on that file. This function works only if something has been read from the file and if the file is buffered. fp is the file pointer returned by seq.open() when the particular file was opened.
syntax: function string seq.ungetc$ (string char, long fp)
returns: The character written to the file. Or an empty string if end-of-file is reached or an error occurred.

name: seq.unlink
doc: This deletes the file indicated by the path_name argument.
syntax: function long seq.unlink (string path_name(512))
returns: >= 0 — Success. < 0 — Error; The negative value of the operating system error.

name: seq.unlock
doc: This removes a lock set by seq.lock().
syntax: function long seq.unlock (long mode, long offset, long size, long fp)
returns: >= 0 — Success. -1 — Error; probably fp not connected. < -1 — Error; Negative error value.

name: seq.w.long
doc: Writes a 32-bit integer value into the file. The function seq.w.long() writes the 32 least significant bits of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first 4 bytes of the supplied file. The inverse function seq.r.long() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the signed 32-bit value range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]) by repeatedly adding or subtracting 2^32 until the value is in the signed 32-bit value range. More specifically, the inverse function seq.r.long() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the signed 32-bit value range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]).
syntax: function long seq.w.long (long value, long fp)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably fp is not a valid file pointer. The last system error is available in predefined variable e. 0 — Success.

name: seq.w.short
doc: Writes a 16-bit integer value into the file. The function seq.w.short() writes the 16 least significant bits of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first 2 bytes of the supplied file. The inverse function seq.r.short() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the unsigned 16-bit value range [0 … 2^16 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 65,535]) by repeatedly adding or subtracting 2^16 until the value is in the unsigned 16-bit value range. More specifically, the inverse function seq.r.short() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the unsigned 16-bit value range [0 … 2^16 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 65,535]).
syntax: function long seq.w.short (long value, long fp)
returns: -1 — Error, most probably fp is not a valid file pointer. The last system error is available in predefined variable e. 0 — Success.

name: seq.w.utc
doc: Writes an integer value into the file. The function seq.w.utc() writes the byte.count least significant bytes of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first byte.count bytes of the supplied file. The inverse function seq.r.utc() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the signed byte.count-byte value range [-(256^ byte.count)/2 … (256^ byte.count)/2 - 1] by repeatedly adding or subtracting 256^ byte.count until the value is in the signed byte.count-byte value range. More specifically, the inverse function seq.r.utc() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the signed byte.count-byte value range [-(256^ byte.count)/2 … (256^ byte.count)/2 - 1].
syntax: function long seq.w.utc (long value, long fp [, long byte.count])
returns: -1 — Error, most probably fp is not a valid file pointer. The last system error is available in predefined variable e. 0 — Success.

name: seq.write
doc: This function appends the specified number of bytes from the specified buffer to the specified file, beginning at the current file position.
syntax: function long seq.write (const string buffer, long nrbytes, long fp)
returns: > 0 — Number of bytes actually written. 0 — End-of-file. < -1 — Error; Probably fp not connected. (the last system error is available in the e variable – for example, for file system full, e will be ENOSPC (that is, 28) – for a list of error codes, see Infor ES errors and messages)

name: seq.write.local
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Instead you should use function: server2client(). This writes data from the specified buffer to the specified file, beginning at the current file position.
syntax: function long seq.write.local (long buf, long size, long lfn)
returns: >= 0 — Success. < 0 — Error. Probably lfn not connected.

name: server2client
doc: Deprecated. This copies a specified file from the server to the client.
syntax: function long server2client (string source, string dest, boolean text.mode [, boolean progress.window] [, boolean read.only])
returns: 0 — File copy success. 1 — Error. File copy canceled by the user. < 0 — Error. Source file not copied to the destination file.

name: set.alarm
doc: This starts a timer that sends a single EVTTIMEREVENT event to the calling process after the number of milliseconds specified in the msec argument. The timer automatically ends after sending the event. The timer also ends automatically when the process ends or when the program explicitly kills it with kill.timer().
syntax: function long set.alarm (long msec)
returns: A unique identifier for the timer.

name: set.ask.enum.values
doc: This restricts the values valid for the ask.enum() function. Only the values specified are shown as buttons.
syntax: function void set.ask.enum.values (enum_constant,... enum_constant)
returns: void

name: set.bg.color
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This sets the background color of a specified ASCII window. The color argument can have the following values: CW.BLACK — CW.BLUE — CW.GREEN — CW.CYAN CW.RED — CW.MAGENTA — CW.YELLOW — CW.WHITE
syntax: function void set.bg.color (long wind_id, long color)
returns: void

name: set.checked.command
doc: Use this to check or uncheck a command in the menubar or the toolbar. This can be used to indicate to the user that the command is activated. Example: Passing TRUE as the 2nd argument to this function will place a check mark in front of the command in the menubar. If the command is also shown as a toolbar icon then the icon will appear pressed.
syntax: function void set.checked.command (string command, boolean checked)
returns: void

name: set.currencies
doc: Use this function to create and fill the multicurrency table. The function inserts a single entry in the table. Currency rotation is based on the order of currencies in this table. Make sure that all the indices of the table (seqno) form a consecutive range, starting at 1
syntax: function void set.currencies (long seqno, string currency(3) [, string currency.desc mb])
returns: void

name: set.dynamic.synchronized.dialog
doc: This function can be used to set the synchronize session when the session to start depends on data of the record, or when the synchronized session uses a child table. Note that the session must have a regular synchronized dialog set for this function to work. Using this function also implies that adding records is done via the grid or via form commands that start the appropriate session directly.
syntax: function void set.dynamic.synchronized.dialog (const string sessioncode [, const string parent.field] [, const string child.field, ...])
returns: void

name: set.enum.array.for.field
doc: In case the field is a listbox, this fills the list with a specified set of enumerate values. In case the field is an optionset, only the options that are specified will be enabled; all other options will be disabled. This function should be used in the before.display.object section and/or in the when.field.changes section of each field on which the change depends.
syntax: function void set.enum.array.for.field (const string field.name, const long size, const long values)
returns: void

name: set.enum.values
doc: This restricts the values valid for the ask.enum() function. Only the values specified are shown as buttons.
syntax: function void set.enum.values (enum_constant enum_constant,...)
returns: void

name: set.enum.values.for.field
doc: In case the field is a listbox, this fills the list with a specified set of enumerate values. In case the field is an optionset, only the options that are specified will be enabled; all other options will be disabled. This function should used in the before.display.object section and/or in the when.field.changes section of each field on which the change depends.
syntax: function void set.enum.values.for.field (const string field.name [, long ALL_ENUMS_EXCEPT] [, enum enum_value, ...])
returns: void

name: set.fg.color
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This sets the foreground color of a specified ASCII window. The color argument can have the following values: CW.BLACK — CW.BLUE — CW.GREEN — CW.CYAN CW.RED — CW.MAGENTA — CW.YELLOW — CW.WHITE
syntax: function void set.fg.color (long wind_id, long color)
returns: void

name: set.fields.default
doc: It is possible to define default values for form fields with the form editor. For all fields of the current form, this function sets the corresponding script variables to the default form values. The function is often used before batch or print programs, where the user must specify some parameters for the batch run.
syntax: function void set.fields.default ()
returns: void

name: set.file.for.textfield
doc: This fills the textbox of a text field with the contents of a specified file present on the server.
syntax: function void set.file.for.textfield (const string field.name.string, string filename)
returns: void

name: set.fmax
doc: This sets a specified string variable to its maximum value. For standard variables, use set.max() instead. For setting the minimum value, use set.fmin() and set.min().
syntax: function void set.fmax (ref void variable [, string domain])
returns: void

name: set.fmin
doc: This sets a specified string variable to its minimum value. For standard variables, use set.min() instead. For setting the maximum value, use set.fmax() and set.max().
syntax: function void set.fmin (ref void variable [, string domain])
returns: void

name: set.focus
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This moves the keyboard input focus to the specified object. When an object has input focus, all keyboard input within the object's main window is received by that object, regardless of the position of the cursor. When an object has input focus, it is surrounded by a rectangular highlight.
syntax: function void set.focus (long object_id)
returns: void

name: set.initial.enum.array.for.field
doc: This function applies to enumerated fields that are displayed as listbox or option set. It limits the number of options to the specified set of enum constants. Any options not specified will be hidden.
syntax: function void set.initial.enum.array.for.field (const string field.name, long size, const long values)
returns: void

name: set.initial.enum.values.for.field
doc: This function applies to enumerated fields that are displayed as listbox or optionset. It limits the number of options to the specified set of enum constants. Any options not specified will be hidden.
syntax: function void set.initial.enum.values.for.field (const string field.name, long ALL_ENUMS_EXCEPT, enum enum_value, ...)
returns: void

name: set.initial.enum.values.for.workflow.status.field
doc: set.initial.enum.values.for.field() with the field.name argument set to “ttocm999.stts”
syntax: function void set.initial.enum.values.for.workflow.status.field (long ALL_ENUMS_EXCEPT, enum workflow_status, ...)
returns: void

name: set.input.error
doc: This causes the 4GL engine to display the specified error message and to force input again in the same input field. If you specify an empty string, no error message is displayed.
syntax: function void set.input.error (string mess.or.code [, void arg ...])
returns: void

name: set.insert.in.detail.session
doc: In sessions where the standard insert does not allow the user to insert all the fields, this function can be used to give the user an alternative session to insert the record. This function activates the standard command insert.in.detail. This standard command has (as other standard commands) an is.allowed before.choice and after.choice hook.
syntax: function void set.insert.in.detail.session (string sess_code [, string parent.var child.var])
returns: void

name: set.limits.off
doc: This removes the limits set with the store.occ.max(), store.occ.min() and/or store.occ.max(), store.occ.min() functions. The entire table can then be accessed again.
syntax: function void set.limits.off ()
returns: void

name: set.list.values.for.field
doc: This fills a listbox field or a combobox field with a specified set of values. The field must be a string type field, and the appearance must be set to Dropdown Listbox or Dropdown Combobox in the DFE.
syntax: function void set.list.values.for.field (const string field.name.string, long no.list.values, const string list.values(,))
returns: void

name: set.max
doc: This sets a specified standard variable to its maximum value. For string variables, use set.fmax() instead. For setting the minimum value, use set.min() and set.fmin().
syntax: function void set.max (ref void variable [, string domain])
returns: void

name: set.mem
doc: The stores the value of source in the destination argument. By default, the value of source is repeated in destination until the latter is completely filled. Use the optional count argument to repeat the value of source a specific number of times only. Elements in the destination argument which are not overwritten remain unchanged.
syntax: function long set.mem (ref void destination, void source [, long count])
returns: 0 success -1 error

name: set.min
doc: This sets a specified standard variable to its minimum value. For string variables, use set.fmin() instead. For setting the maximum value, use set.max() and set.fmax().
syntax: function void set.min (ref void variable [, string domain])
returns: void

name: set.multiline.text.in.html.mode
doc: This switches the editing of a text_field to html mode in a Rich Text Editor. Text edited in this way is saved in html format.
syntax: function long set.multiline.text.in.html.mode (string text_field)
returns: 0 Success -1 Not in LnUI -2 LnUI version too old, minimum version is 12.0.5 -3 Object TIV too low, it should be >= 2150

name: set.node.class
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this function to assign a different class to a particular node. The node class determines the color in which a node is displayed.
syntax: function void set.node.class (string tree_name, string node_id, long node_class [, long process_id])
returns: void

name: set.node.class.color
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. The node class assigned to a node determines the color in which the node is displayed. You use this function to define the color for a specified node class. You use set.node.class() to assign a class to a particular node.
syntax: function void set.node.class.color (string tree_name, long node_class, long class_color [, long process_id])
returns: void

name: set.numformat.symbols
doc: Set the decimal sign and thousand separator. These settings will be used from this moment on for all formatted numbers.
syntax: function void set.numformat.symbols (string decimal(1), string grouping(1))
returns: void

name: set.object.defaults
doc: Use this hook to fill a new record with defaults. Before this hook will be called a db.set.to.default() has been executed; therefore it is not necessary to assign values that are already present in the table definition. This is hook is executed by OpenWorld through a BOI in case of a DAL_NEW or in case of a DAL2 DAL, when an insert is started. Note: This hook only contains assignments.
syntax: function long set.object.defaults ()
returns: The hook returns 0 if the hook has been executed successfully.

name: set.pgrp
doc: This places a specified process in a specified process group. If the process group ID is the same as the process ID, a new process group is created with the specified ID. The specified process becomes the leader of the new group. The parent of the process does not change when you call this function.
syntax: function long set.pgrp (long process_id, long group_id)
returns: The function returns the ID of the process group.

name: set.refresh.rate
doc: With this function the refresh rate of the session will be overruled temporary. The refresh interval is part of the User Data Template. This interval is used for sessions where the Auto Refresh in standard commands is set. This function overrules the setting of the session, also if the refresh interval is not defined on the User Data Template for the current user.
syntax: function long set.refresh.rate (long rateInSeconds [, long thresholdInSeconds])
returns: Error Code: 0: Successful completion -1: Refresh rate must be greater than or equal to -1. -2: Threshold must be greater than or equal to zero. -3: No action on XML Response Node "Session Refresh" -4: Refresh interval not supported

name: set.sensitive
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This sets the sensitivity of a specified object.
syntax: function void set.sensitive (long object_id, long status)
returns: void

name: set.spool.main.report
doc: This stores a specified report name in the predefined variable spool.main.report.
syntax: function void set.spool.main.report (string rep_name)
returns: void

name: set.starting.satellite
doc: This function specifies which satellite should be active when the multi-main table session is started.
syntax: function void set.starting.satellite (const string satelliteSessionCode)
returns: void

name: set.strip.mode
doc: set.strip.mode() sets or resets the 'strip-on-assignment' flag for all string fields of the table specified by table_id. The mode argument indicates whether the flag is to be set on or off. 1 indicates set flag on, 0 indicates set flag off. Setting this flag on a symbol a means that assignments to other variables from this value will behave as an assignment from
syntax: function long set.strip.mode (long table.id, long mode)
returns: 0: success < 0: error

name: set.symbol.strip.mode
doc: set.symbol.strip.mode() sets or resets the 'strip-on-assignment' flag for all string fields of the table specified by table_id. The mode argument indicates whether the flag is to be set on or off. 1 indicates set flag on, 0 indicates set flag off. Setting this flag on a symbol a means that assignments to other variables from this value will behave as an assignment from
syntax: function long set.symbol.strip.mode (ref string str, long mode)
returns: 0: success < 0: error

name: set.synchronized.dialog
doc: This defines for the current session the dialog to synchronize with. Both sessions act on the same maintable. When the user double-clicks on an occurrence in the parent session, the synchronized dialog is updated with information from the selected record. The synchronized dialog also automatically opens when the user initiates any of the following actions: insert record, edit record or duplicate record. When a record is saved in the synchronized dialog, the 4GL engine updates the occurrence in the parent window. When the synchronized dialog is opened or updated, the synchronized.reason variable (read-only) is set. This indicates the command that caused the synchronization. The possible values are: ADD.SET, DUPL.OCCUR, MODIFY.SET, and DISPLAY.SET. This variable is available in all sections in the synchronized dialog session.
syntax: function void set.synchronized.dialog (string sess_code [, boolean editable.grid] [, boolean use.dialog.for.insert])
returns: void

name: set.time.zone
doc: This sets the local time zone at run time.
syntax: function long set.time.zone (string time_zone(50))
returns: 0 — Success. -1 — Error.

name: set.timer
doc: This starts a timer that sends an EVTTIMEREVENT event to the calling process every msec milliseconds. The timer continues to send events until the process ends or until the program explicitly terminates the timer using kill.timer().
syntax: function long set.timer (long msec)
returns: A unique identifier for the timer.

name: set.transaction.readonly
doc: This defines a transaction as read only. The transaction can only read records (without locks) from the database; it cannot update the database. When included, this function must be the first command of a transaction. So, you must include it either at the start of the program or immediately following a commit.transaction() or abort.transaction() call. Because it is not possible to update the database in a read-only transaction, you can use only the following database calls in the transaction: db.first() db.lt() db.last() db.le() db.next() db.set.to.default() db.prev() db.change.order() db.gt() db.indexinfo() db.ge() db.nr.indices() db.eq() db.nr.rows() db.cur() db.row.length() db.bind() db.record.to.columns() db.unbind() db.columns.to.record() db.error()
syntax: function long set.transaction.readonly ()
returns: n/a (no Return section in guide)

name: set.tree.background
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This changes the background color of a specified tree.
syntax: function void set.tree.background (string tree_name, long color [, long process_id])
returns: void

name: set.tree.font
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. This changes the font used for nodes at a particular level in a specified tree. Use load.font() to load the font that you want to use.
syntax: function void set.tree.font (string tree_name, long visible_level, long font [, long process_id])

name: set.tree.foreground

name: set.tree.linewidth
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for Baan Windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. name: setenv

syntax: function long setenv (string env_var, string env_value)
returns: 0 — success -1 — failed to set environment variable 1 — name of environment variable is too long 2 — value for environment variable is too long 3 — both name and value are too long

name: sf$
doc: Deprecated. This function is only supported for character-based windows and its usage is therefore deprecated. Use this to set all text on the screen to bold. Use face="Courier New" sf$(0) to reset the screen to normal.
syntax: function void sf$ (long num_expr)
returns: void

name: sha.add.data
doc: Adds one block of data to be hashed. It is not needed to supply all input data at once in one large block. Sha.add.data() may be called several times with relatively small blocks. Internally, the SHA-1 algorithm processes the input in 512 bit blocks, i.e. 64 byte at a time.
syntax: function void sha.add.data (long id, string data.in)
returns: void

name: sha.compute.output
doc: Adds some padding and a bit count to the message, as prescribed in the standard, and computes the resulting message digest. After this, the Secure Hash Algorithm state may be reused for hashing another message, by calling sha.initialize(), sha.add.data(), and sha.compute.output() again.
syntax: function long sha.compute.output (long id, ref string data.out)
returns: The size of the Secure Hash Algorithm output is returned. If this value is greater than the size of data.out, then no output at all is written to data.out, and sha.compute.output() may be called again with a larger output buffer. The size of the Secure Hash Algorithm output is in all cases 20 bytes.

name: sha.create
doc: Allocates memory to contain the state of the Secure Hash Algorithm.
syntax: function long sha.create ()
returns: An Id corresponding to the allocated state is returned. This Id can be used in subsequent calls to sha.initialize(), sha.add.data(), and sha.compute.output(). The returned Id can only be used in the original BAAN process where sha.create was called, and is useless in other BAAN processes in the same bshell. The allocated memory is freed explicitly by passing the Id to sha.destroy(). The allocated memory is freed implicitly when the BAAN process exits. Any number of Secure Hash Algorithm states may be in use concurrently.

This starts the vt200 compatible terminal emulator to execute the command specified in the command argument. The shell (UNIX only) process is connected with the bshell by means of a pseudo tty. name: shiftc$

name: shiftr$

name: sprintf$
doc: This formats a string and returns the formatted string. The format argument contains zero or more ordinary characters and substitution symbols. The ordinary characters are copied directly to the output string. The substitution symbols specify formats for the values specified in the expression arguments and are substituted by these formatted values. The substitution symbols are used in the sequence in which they are specified. The first substitution symbol is used for the first expression argument. The second substitution symbol is used for the second expression argument, and so on. In addition to a range of numeric type expressions, the function supports dates, amounts, single-byte strings, multi-byte strings, bidirectional strings, and combined normal and bidirectional strings. input strings that contain bidirectional strings must be specified in logic order. The result is also returned in logic order.
syntax: function string sprintf$ (string format [, void ...])
returns: The formatted string. If you specify an invalid format, sprintf$() returns a percentage character [%].

As a result, the values of the field retrieved by the SELECT statement are stored in the 4GL variable. They can then be used elsewhere in the program. Note that it is not necessary to bind external variables.

name: ssl.mode
doc: This is a function to determine whether the bshell runs in SSL mode, and if so, which. When runing in GovCloud mode, both FIPS and SSL mode are turned on. But a system administrator can also decide to turn SSL mode on outside of a GovCloud environment, using the "ssl" resource in the lib/defaults/bootstrap resource file. This works on all operating systems and environments. When SSL mode is on, SSL (Secure Socket Layer) communication is enforced between the LN-UI and the bshell, and between bshells that use sockets to communicate to other bshells (using sock.start.process()). This protects data transmitted over the network from eavesdropping and tampering. This function can be used to find out what minimum level of security is in use. It returns a string.
syntax: function string ssl.mode ()
returns: off — Bshell does not have SSL security on. Network traffic is unencrypted. This is the default for non GovCloud environments. on — Bshell has default SSL security turned on. It is up to the cryptographic library in use by the bshell to negotiate a default protocol that is considered sufficient by both ends of the link. As long as some form of SSL is negotiated, the connection will succeed. tlsv1.1 — The security level is downgraded so (old) TLSv1.1 connections are acceptable. Many modern installations will insist on using at least level TLSv1.2, using this setting may be required to communicate with older installations. During negotiations, a higher level of security may be decided upon. tlsv1.2 — The security level is set to so TLSv1.2 as minimum, TLSv1.1 on either end will result in a failure to connect. This is the default level for GovCloud environments. tlsv1.3 — The security level is set to so TLSv1.3 as minimum, TLSv1.1 or v1.2 on either end will result in a failure to connect. At the time of writing (July 2020) many systems do not support v1.3 yet, but WolfSSL based bshells do.

The function starts the specified child session when the user chooses a particular form command in the multioccurrence parent session. The primary key of the parent's main table must be a subset of the primary key of the child's main table. Although you normally use this function to synchronize sessions that act on different main tables, it is also possible to use it to synchronize sessions that act on the same main table.
syntax: function long start.synchronized.child (string sess_code [, string parent.var child.var] [, long start.mode])

name: start.synchronized.child.with

name: store.byte
doc: The function store.byte() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The function store.byte() writes the 8 least significant bits of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first byte of the supplied string. The inverse function load.byte() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the unsigned 8-bit value range [0 … 2^8 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 255]) by repeatedly adding or subtracting 2^8 until the value is in the unsigned 8-bit value range. More specifically, the inverse function load.byte() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the unsigned 8-bit value range [0 … 2^8 - 1] (i.e. [0 … 255]). This function is machine independent and can be used (for example) in network communications.
syntax: function void store.byte (long value, ref string rec$)
returns: void

name: store.double
doc: The function store.double() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The bytes written to the string are not the encoding of certain characters, but the encoding of the numerical value of the first argument of the function. The function store.double writes eight bytes to the supplied string, representing the eight-byte encoding of the floating point value of its first argument. The store.double() function is not machine independent and must be used with care in (for example) network communications.
syntax: function void store.double (double value, ref string rec$)
returns: void

name: store.float
doc: The function store.float() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The bytes written to the string are not the encoding of certain characters, but the encoding of the numerical value of the first argument of the function. The function store.float writes four bytes to the supplied string, representing the four-byte encoding of the floating point value of its first argument. The store.float() function is not machine independent and must be used with care in (for example) network communications.
syntax: function void store.float (double value, ref string rec$)
returns: void

name: store.long
doc: The function store.long() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The function store.long() writes the 32 least significant bits of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first 4 bytes of the supplied string. The inverse function load.long() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the signed 32-bit value range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]) by repeatedly adding or subtracting 2^32 until the value is in the signed 32-bit value range. More specifically, the inverse function load.long() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the signed 32-bit value range [-2^31 … 2^31 - 1] (i.e. [-2,147,483,648 … 2,147,483,647]). This function is machine independent and can be used (for example) in network communications.
syntax: function void store.long (long value, ref string rec$)
returns: void

name: store.occ.max
doc: Normally, standard commands that access records of the main table can access all records of that table. You can use these functions to limit the records that can be accessed to those whose key values are within a specified range. Use store.occ.max() to define the upper limit of the range. Use store.occ.min() to define the lower limit of the range. If you wish, you can define only a maximum or only a minimum limit. Before you call either of these functions, you must fill the key value with the required maximum or minimum value. If you set a limit that has previously been defined, the new value of the limit overwrites the previous value of the limit. Use set.limits.off() to switch off the limits defined with these functions.
syntax: function void store.occ.max ()
returns: void

name: store.short
doc: The function store.short() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The function store.short() writes the 16 least significant bits of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first 2 bytes of the supplied string. The inverse function load.short() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the signed 16-bit value range [-2^15 … 2^15 - 1] (i.e. [-32,768 … 32,767]) by repeatedly adding or subtracting 2^16 until the value is in the signed 16-bit value range. More specifically, the inverse function load.short() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the signed 16-bit value range [-2^15 … 2^15 - 1] (i.e. [-32,768 … 32,767]). This function is machine independent and can be used (for example) in network communications.
syntax: function void store.short (long value, ref string rec$)
returns: void

name: store.utc
doc: The function store.utc() treats the supplied string merely as a sequence of bytes. The function store.utc() writes the byte.count least significant bytes of the two’s complement representation of the supplied integer value into the first byte.count bytes of the supplied string. The inverse function load.utc() will retrieve the original supplied integer value, wrapped to the signed byte.count-byte value range [-(256^ byte.count)/2 … (256^ byte.count)/2 - 1] by repeatedly adding or subtracting 256^ byte.count until the value is in the signed byte.count-byte value range. More specifically, the inverse function load.utc() will retrieve the exact original supplied integer value if and only if that integer value is within the signed byte.count-byte value range [-(256^ byte.count)/2 … (256^ byte.count)/2 - 1]. This function is machine independent and can be used (for example) in network communications.
syntax: function void store.utc (long value, ref string rec$ [, long byte.count])
returns: void

In that case the following limitations apply: string$ parts parts string$ parts parts

returns: the string without the surrounding quotes, if any

name: str_pos
doc: This returns the start position of a specified substring ( part) in a specified string ( source). source and part can be either strings or string expressions. As of TIV 2200, this alternative function to pos() exists which finds the same parts in the source string as pos() does, but always returns a start position in the source which can be used as offset in the source string. For examples of callling this function, see pos(). When a multi-byte part is found in a single-byte source, the start position yielded by the function pos() is given as if the source was a multi-byte string. When more multi-byte characters were present in the source, this start position may be different from the start position of the found part in the source, when the source is viewed as single-byte (which it is, in this case). The function str_pos() yields the start position in the same mode as the source string. str_pos() starts searching for the substring at the first position in the source string. It returns the start position relative to the beginning of the source string. To start searching at the last position instead, use str_rpos(). str_pos() can start the search at the specified offset. In this way it is possible to not only find the first occurrence of a substring, but also the next one(s). The returned start position is also in this case relative to the beginning of the source string.
syntax: function long str_pos (string source, string part [, long offset])
returns: The start position of the substring in the string. Or 0 if the substring is not found.

name: str_rpos
doc: This returns the start position of a specified substring ( part) in a specified string ( source). source and part can be either strings or string expressions. As of TIV 2200, this alternative function to rpos() exists which finds the same parts in the source string as rpos() does, but always returns a start position in the source which can be used as offset in the source string. For examples of callling this function, see rpos(). When a multi-byte part is found in a single-byte source, the start position yielded by the function rpos() is given as if the source was a multi-byte string. When more multi-byte characters were present in the source, this start position may be different from the start position of the found part in the source, when the source is viewed as single-byte (which it is, in this case). The function str_rpos() yields the start position in the same mode as the source string. str_rpos() starts searching for the substring at the last position in the source string, searching backward. It returns the start position relative to the beginning of the source string. To start searching at the first position instead, use str_pos(). str_rpos() can start the search at the specified offset. In this way it is possible to not only find the first occurrence of a substring, but also the next one(s). The returned start position is also in this case relative to the beginning of the source string.
syntax: function long str_rpos (string source, string part [, long offset])
returns: The start position of the substring in the string. Or 0 if the substring is not found.

name: stream.type
